chef_bio.background: A late-night ramen specialist in central Kyoto's Kawaramachi district, tucked into the World Building on Daikoku-cho near the Kiyamachi and Pontocho nightlife streets. The shop is part of the small Ichiryu Manbai noodle group, which also runs a Teramachi branch nearby.
chef_bio.philosophy: Care put into balance and texture: thin curly noodles cut with whole-grain wheat flour to carry more aroma, paired with a clean but assertive shoyu broth and carefully prepared toppings (chicken and pork chashu, bamboo shoots, soft egg, mitsuba/parsley).
chef_bio.specialty: A clear (清湯) double broth built on chicken and duck, finished with a crisp, sharp soy-sauce tare for the signature shoyu ramen (らぁ麺). The kitchen also turns out a tsukemen and a mazesoba that mixes thick flat noodles with chicken-oil sauce, minced chashu, red onion, and a truffle-oil-dressed egg yolk with lemon to shift the flavor partway through.

anecdotes.text: The mazesoba is described by a noodle blogger as having a sticky, clinging, oil-forward texture close to an abura-soba, brightened at the table with truffle-oil egg yolk and a squeeze of lemon.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: noodlers confirms the Kawaramachi/Nakagyo location and Teramachi branch, the clean duck-and-chicken broth らぁ麺 (¥900), thin whole-grain-wheat noodles, chashu (chicken and pork)/bamboo/mitsuba/red-onion toppings, and the oil-forward mazesoba (¥880) with truffle-oil egg yolk and lemon.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Wheat ramen/tsukemen/mazesoba noodles (including whole-grain wheat flour) are boiled in shared water; not safe for celiac or wheat-allergic diners.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broth is chicken-and-duck stock and toppings include chicken and pork chashu and egg; no plant-based preparation, so all items carry animal cross-contact.

cultural_comfort.note: A casual, ticket-machine ramen counter open late into the night; a little Japanese helps with the vending-machine ordering, but pointing and basic greetings will get you through.

chef_bio.background: TETSU began in 2005 as a tiny 10-tsubo (about 33 sqm) shop in Sendagi, Tokyo, founded by Kazunori Komiya. Starting with just 3 million yen in capital, he grew it into a tsukemen brand of roughly 30 shops centered on Tokyo. This AEON Mall KYOTO branch opened on October 17, 2023, marking the brand's return to Kyoto more than a decade after its earlier Kyoto Ramen Koji shop inside the Kyoto Station Building closed in 2011.
chef_bio.philosophy: An uncompromising obsession with keeping the broth hot to the very last bite — the brand's trademark hot-stone (焼き石) service, in which a scorching stone is dropped into the dipping broth to keep it piping hot. Note that this hot-stone service is a signature of TETSU's standalone shops and is not offered at this AEON Mall food-court outlet.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature is a rich pork-bone-and-seafood (豚骨魚介) tsukemen — a triple soup of chicken bones, pork bones and bonito/mackerel — served with extra-thick straight noodles that stand up to the heavy dipping broth. Miso and spicy-miso dipping versions are also popular here, and the kitchen rounds out the menu with a chashu rice bowl and a chuka-soba.

anecdotes.text: TETSU's trademark move solves tsukemen's classic weak point of broth going lukewarm: a stone heated until scorching is dropped into the dipping broth partway through the meal so it stays piping hot until the final drop — though this hot-stone service is not available at the AEON Mall food-court branch.
Founder Kazunori Komiya turned a 3-million-yen, 10-tsubo Sendagi shop opened in 2005 into a roughly 30-location tsukemen chain.
The Kyoto branch opened in the AEON Mall KYOTO food court on October 17, 2023, returning the brand to Kyoto after its station-building shop had closed in 2011.

cultural_comfort.note: A casual mall food-court stall where you order at the counter and carry your tray, so a friendly konnichiwa and pointing at the menu is all you need.

chef_bio.background: Iwasaki Tanmen opened its doors on March 1, 2023 in the Ono neighborhood of Yamashina, just steps from Ono Station, taking over a storefront that previously housed another ramen shop (Shioemon). It is a rarity in Kyoto: a shop devoted to tanmen, a vegetable-piled salt ramen far more common in the Kanto region of eastern Japan than here in Kansai.
chef_bio.philosophy: Make-it-your-own simplicity: diners can dial the vegetables, pork, noodle quantity, garlic and spice to taste, and garlic is served on the side so each guest controls their own portion. Sides like gyoza, karaage and takana rice round out an honest, affordable bowl.
chef_bio.specialty: The house tanmen is the signature: a mound of lightly stir-fried vegetables — cabbage, bean sprouts and more — over medium straight noodles in a chicken-and-pork salt (shio) broth. It arrives looking hearty and Jiro-esque, yet the soup is surprisingly clean and light, with no heavy back-fat. A pot of house chili-miso (kara-miso) sits at hand so you can stir in heat and depth gradually as you eat.

anecdotes.text: The shop offers several tanmen styles beyond the original — a shio-tonkotsu, a rich miso and a spicy version — so regulars can rotate through the lineup.
One local blogger called the proprietor very kind and admitted he came back years after his first visit because he simply could not forget the tanmen.
The bowl starts around 690 yen, keeping it genuinely budget-friendly.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyotopi confirms the March 2023 opening in Yamashina-Ono near Ono Station in the former Shioemon space, the Kanto-style tanmen (rare in Kyoto) on a light chicken-pork shio broth, four tanmen varieties (classic/shio-tonkotsu/miso/spicy), customizable veg/pork/garlic-on-the-side/spice, kara-miso, gyoza/karaage/takana-rice sides, ~¥690, and 16 seats.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The core dish uses wheat ramen noodles in a shared salt broth; there is no published gluten-free option and the kitchen is a small single-line operation, so cross-contact with wheat should be assumed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shop's tare is described as a house-made salt (shio) sauce rather than a soy-based one; however, its full composition is not published, so wheat content cannot be confirmed.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Vegetables are stir-fried together with pork, and the broth is chicken/pork based, so vegetable toppings share animal ingredients and equipment.

positives.text: Diners can customize vegetables, pork, noodle amount, garlic and spice level, with garlic served separately for portion control — useful for tailoring a bowl, though not an allergen accommodation.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, friendly neighborhood counter-and-table shop where Japanese phrases for ordering and customizing your bowl will go a long way; English support is not documented.

chef_bio.chef_name: Inoue (proprietor)
roles: owner
chef
chef_bio.origin: Ichijoji, Sakyo-ku, Kyoto — on the city's famous Ichijoji ramen street, but a deliberate step away from the heavy-broth pack.
chef_bio.background: The shop is the latest evolution of a Kyoto noodle maker who has spent years chasing dashi rather than richness. The lineage runs from a dashi-based ramen shop, Isao (イサオ, opened 2010), which the owner renamed and reframed in 2014 as Odashi to Komugi 130 (おだしと小麦 一三〇) to put the dashi and the wheat front and center. In June 2022 the concept was distilled again into だし料理 十.
chef_bio.philosophy: The whole place is built so customers can actually understand dashi — you can watch it being made, taste it, and talk it through with the owner. Seasoning is pared back to almost nothing so the stock itself carries the bowl.
chef_bio.specialty: The signature bowl is the breakfast-only o-dashi no new-men: a clear soup built from just three things — Rishiri kombu, sawara (young Spanish mackerel / sagoshi), and bonito flakes — seasoned with a single gram of Iwate salt and no soy sauce at all. The noodles are made in-house from domestic wheat and egg, cut to roughly 1mm square and dusted with Hokkaido corn flour, then finished with hand-shaved bonito and a few pieces of salt-cured pepper.

anecdotes.text: By late afternoon the shop sheds its noodle-counter identity and becomes a dashi retail shop and small sake bar, selling drinkable dashi (nomu o-dashi) and easy dashi kits so people can take the craft home.
Tasters describe being unexpectedly moved by the bowl — 出汁のふくよかな香りとまろやかな口当たり (the rich aroma and rounded mouthfeel of the dashi genuinely move you).

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: life-info and Tabelog (former name 'Odashi&Wheat isao') confirm owner Inoue, the lineage Isao (2010) -> おだしと小麦 一三〇 (2014) -> だし料理 十 (June 2022), the breakfast-only o-dashi new-men (Rishiri kombu, sawara, bonito, 1g Iwate salt, no soy; ~1mm domestic wheat-egg noodles with Hokkaido corn flour; hand-shaved bonito and salt-cured pepper), and the afternoon dashi-retail/sake-bar with nomu o-dashi and dashi kits.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The house-made noodles are cut from domestic wheat (and egg) in-house, so flour is handled on-site; a shared-kitchen wheat environment should be assumed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The signature dashi bowl uses no soy sauce at all — it is seasoned with about 1 gram of Iwate salt only — so the usual wheat-shoyu tare risk is absent from the broth (the wheat comes from the noodles instead).

vegan_cross_contact.text: The dashi is animal-based throughout (sawara/Spanish mackerel and bonito alongside kombu), and the noodles contain egg, so there is no clean vegan or vegetarian path.
vegan_cross_contact.source_wording: 「利尻昆布、さわら、まぐろ節で出汁を引き」 — Rishiri kombu, sawara and まぐろ節 (dried TUNA flakes). Noodles: 「国産小麦と卵のみを使用した…自家製麺」.

positives.text: Because the owner makes and explains the dashi in front of guests, it is easy to ask exactly what is in the bowl, and the seasoning is unusually transparent: kombu, sawara, bonito, salt, and house wheat-and-egg noodles.
positives.source_wording: 「料理や小売り、情報発信を通して「出汁を知ってもらいたい」と昨年6月オープン。店主・井上さんが出汁を引く様子を見て、味わって、話を聞けば自然と出汁が身近に感じられる。」

cultural_comfort.note: A tiny owner-run dashi specialist where the proprietor talks you through the craft; some Japanese (or a translation app) goes a long way, and a quiet, curious attitude fits the room.

chef_bio.origin: Kyoto (Kitayama district yatai origins); founder from Kanazawa
chef_bio.background: Kyoto Kitayama Motomachi Ramen traces its roots to a street cart (yatai) that the first-generation owner — a native of Kanazawa — set up on Shinmachi-dori in Kyoto's Kitayama district roughly 50 years ago. Drawing on the rich, dark soy-sauce style of nearby Toyama Black, he built a Kyoto take on the bowl using tamari soy sauce from a long-established local soy-sauce maker. The business later moved into a permanent shop, settling at its current location in an alley off Higashinotoin in central Kyoto, where the cart's original flavor is carried on by a later (third) generation.
chef_bio.philosophy: Honor the original yatai flavor while continuing to refine it; serve until the broth is gone and then close for the day.
chef_bio.specialty: A rich black-soy-sauce ramen finished with plenty of back fat (背脂醤油らーめん), with beef-tendon ramen (牛すじらーめん) as a second signature. The defining element is a specialty tamari soy sauce of the kind used for eel sauce, sourced from a 160-year-old Kyoto soy-sauce maker.

anecdotes.text: The founder, from Kanazawa, based his recipe on the dark, bold style of Toyama Black but reinterpreted it for Kyoto using local tamari soy sauce.
The shop began as a Kitayama Shinmachi street cart about 50 years ago, and a later (third) generation continues the cart's original taste at the current shop.
The tamari soy sauce is supplied by a 160-year-old established Kyoto soy-sauce shop (Sawai) and is of the type used for eel sauce.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The official site confirms the 創業50年 Kitayama Shinmachi yatai origin, a Kanazawa-born first-generation owner inspired by 富山ブラック, the specialty たまり醤油 (eel-sauce type) from a 160-year-old Kyoto maker (Sawai), the 背脂醤油らーめん (¥900) and 牛すじらーめん (¥1,100), the Higashinotoin 京町家 location, and continuation by a third generation.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The bowl is built on a tamari/black soy sauce tare; tamari and standard soy sauce here are wheat-containing and central to the broth.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Broth and toppings are pork/beef based (beef tendon is a signature), so no item is free of animal products.

cultural_comfort.note: A cash-only, counter-style local ramen shop with no English service signaled; basic Japanese or a translation app will make ordering smoother.

kyo_au_petit_foreau.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. [Adversarial GF review 2026-08-19: dedicated→options. I set out to disprove the whole-shop wheat-free claim and succeeded on the record's own evidence: the owner's blog (ameblo.jp/petit-foreau, cited ON the record) lists a mixed lineup where only some items carry ヴィーガン・小麦フリー / 乳・小麦フリー labels while ショートケーキ and ガトーショコラ sit alongside them — i.e. one kitchen baking both wheat and rice-flour goods, which the protocol bars from dedicated outright. The independent sources do not rescue it: Leaf Kyoto (2022) says only that she blends 米粉・大豆粉・アーモンドプードル instead of wheat and never confirms every item is GF, and kyoto-ethical-market (2023) frames the gluten-free claim at the single-product level (the 0% cheesecake). The ONLY source asserting 全商品グルテンフリー＆プラントベース is ashiya-obentofesta.com, which I opened and found to be a グルテンフリー大辞典 content hub bylined 管理人 — an aggregator, not independent celiac-grade corroboration, and a single source cannot support dedicated/high under the hard rule. Compounding this, the operation looks close to dormant: Tabelog shows 月2回ほどの営業／現在は予約のみ with its listing last edited Feb 2023, the owner's blog stops at Feb 2020, and no celiac guide lists it.] The shop's own materials state it relaunched in September 2021 (令和3年9月) as a plant-based & gluten-free specialty patisserie where every item is made without wheat, white sugar, or animal products (全商品グルテンフリー＆プラントベース). All cakes, tarts and baked goods are built on rice flour (米粉) instead of wheat, so no wheat flour is handled on the premises. It is not a daily shop — the Nijo location opens only about 2–3 irregular days per month, so a date-check and pre-order are essential.
kyo_au_petit_foreau.vegan_detail: [Held at "some vegan options" 2026-08-20] The "fully vegan" label was contradicted by this record's own cited sources. Every product is vegan: no eggs, dairy, butter or any animal-derived ingredient (動物由来のものすべて不使用). The signature 0% cheesecake replaces dairy with soy-milk yogurt, and the shop describes its mission as making 'cute and delicious vegan sweets that nourish the heart' (心が満たされるかわいらしく美味しいヴィーガンスイーツ). Sweeteners are unrefined (beet sugar), not white sugar.
kyo_au_petit_foreau.hours_raw: Opens only ~2–3 irregular days per month (reservation/pre-order only); on open days approx. 11:00–18:00. Monthly 'Open DAY' dates are announced on Instagram @petitforeau0903 and the online shop (petitforeau.stores.jp). Not a walk-in daily shop.
kyo_au_petit_foreau.notes: [GF-dedicated] A dedicated wheat-free, plant-based (vegan) patisserie: every product is gluten-free rice-flour based, so cross-contact from wheat is structurally minimized. CRITICAL for planning: this is NOT a daily storefront — it opens only about 3 days per month on irregular dates and works essentially on a pre-order/pickup basis. Check the current Open DAY schedule on Instagram (@petitforeau0903) or the online shop first, and reserve at least one week ahead (Instagram DM, LINE, or petitforeau@icloud.com); payment is on the pickup day. No eat-in — takeout only.

chef_bio.chef_name: 中谷美佳 (Mika Nakatani)
roles: owner
pâtissière
chef_bio.origin: 京都府南丹市 (Nantan City, Kyoto Prefecture)
chef_bio.background: Mika Nakatani is a French-trained pastry chef from Nantan City in Kyoto Prefecture. Japanese sources report she trained in France and, back in Japan, worked as a pâtissière — including a stint at the celebrated Kyoto restaurant Gion Sasaki (祇園さゝ木) and at patisseries and hotels in Kyoto and Osaka — before going independent around 2016. She converted the shop in September 2021 into a dedicated vegan and gluten-free patisserie, rebuilding her entire repertoire around organic, plant-based, rice-flour ingredients. Her signature is the '0%チーズケーキ' — a cheesecake with gluten, white sugar and animal ingredients all at 0%, built on soy-milk yogurt and cashews.
chef_bio.philosophy: Aims to create 'cute and delicious vegan sweets that nourish the heart' (心が満たされるかわいらしく美味しいヴィーガンスイーツを目指します); shifted to plant-based & gluten-free for health and environmental reasons, using organic ingredients and unrefined (beet) sugar.
chef_bio.specialty: 0%チーズケーキ (0% cheesecake) — gluten/white-sugar/animal all 0%, soy-yogurt & cashew based; plus seasonal rice-flour tarts, shortcakes and Mont Blanc.

anecdotes.text: The 0% cheesecake gets its cheese-like richness and refreshing tang from soy-milk yogurt and lemon juice rather than dairy (しっとり上品な口あたり。チーズのコクに豆乳ヨーグルトやレモン果汁が、さわやかな酸味をプラス).
Beyond the Nijo pop-up days, she supplies her plant-based/GF sweets to mumokuteki cafe and to 素食カフェRen (Cafe Ren), which sells the 0% cheesecake by pre-order.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: kyoto-ethical-market confirms she is a France-trained pâtissière from Nantan who worked at Kyoto/Osaka hotels before going independent ~2016 and relaunched the shop in Sept 2021 as a fully gluten-free, white-sugar-free, plant-based rice-flour patisserie with the flagship 0% cheesecake; japanese-heart independently confirms a prior pâtissière role at 祇園ささ木 (Gion Sasaki) alongside her France training. Specific French patisserie names given by some profiles could not be verified and were dropped.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Patisserie only — no savory soy-sauce dishes. The 0% cheesecake uses white miso (白味噌) and kuzu; miso can be a hidden wheat/barley source, so confirm the miso is GF if highly sensitive.

vegan_cross_contact.text: No animal products are used anywhere in the shop (fully plant-based), so animal cross-contact is not a concern.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Owner-run allergy-focused patisserie; individual products are also flagged for specific allergies (e.g. ヴィーガン・小麦フリー, 乳・小麦フリー) on the owner's blog, indicating allergy awareness. Orders are handled directly by the chef via pre-order.

positives.text: Trusted enough by the vegan/GF community that mumokuteki cafe and Cafe Ren resell her sweets.

gf_review.why: I set out to disprove the whole-shop wheat-free claim and succeeded on the record's own evidence: the owner's blog (ameblo.jp/petit-foreau, cited ON the record) lists a mixed lineup where only some items carry ヴィーガン・小麦フリー / 乳・小麦フリー labels while ショートケーキ and ガトーショコラ sit alongside them — i.e. one kitchen baking both wheat and rice-flour goods, which the protocol bars from dedicated outright. The independent sources do not rescue it: Leaf Kyoto (2022) says only that she blends 米粉・大豆粉・アーモンドプードル instead of wheat and never confirms every item is GF, and kyoto-ethical-market (2023) frames the gluten-free claim at the single-product level (the 0% cheesecake). The ONLY source asserting 全商品グルテンフリー＆プラントベース is ashiya-obentofesta.com, which I opened and found to be a グルテンフリー大辞典 content hub bylined 管理人 — an aggregator, not independent celiac-grade corroboration, and a single source cannot support dedicated/high under the hard rule. Compounding this, the operation looks close to dormant: Tabelog shows 月2回ほどの営業／現在は予約のみ with its listing last edited Feb 2023, the owner's blog stops at Feb 2020, and no celiac guide lists it.
red_flags: Owner's own blog shows wheat cakes (ショートケーキ, ガトーショコラ) sold alongside per-item 小麦フリー products — mixed patisserie kitchen, disqualifying for dedicated
Per-item 小麦フリー labelling implies other items are NOT wheat-free
Sole source for 全商品グルテンフリー is ashiya-obentofesta.com, a content-farm aggregator (byline 管理人) — single, non-celiac-grade
Leaf Kyoto and kyoto-ethical-market both stop short of confirming shop-wide GF; kyoto-ethical-market's GF claim is product-specific
Operating status doubtful: 月2-3回のみ営業, 予約のみ, Tabelog info last edited Feb 2023, owner's blog silent since Feb 2020
Signature 0% cheesecake uses 白味噌 — miso can be barley/wheat-based and is undocumented here
Absent from every celiac-grade guide (FindMeGlutenFree, atly, endlessdistances)

kyo_hirose_okomeya_cafe.gf_detail: A 99-year-old Kyoto rice merchant (廣瀬米穀店, est. 1926) that sells no wheat products, with an attached café whose owner is a certified 米粉マイスター (rice-flour master) and 五ツ星お米マイスター. Everything is made with 100% rice flour and no wheat flour or white sugar: 米粉シフォンケーキ (rice-flour chiffon) is sold Tuesday–Saturday and お米パン / こめやパン (rice bread) is baked and sold on Wednesdays. Because it is a food shop and rice mill rather than a certified dedicated gluten-free kitchen, celiac guests should still confirm on the day that no wheat is handled or stored on-site. In practice the entire product line is rice-based, so cross-contact risk is low.
kyo_hirose_okomeya_cafe.vegan_detail: The お米パン / こめやパン rice bread is fully plant-based — made only from rice, rice oil, maple, salt, rice starter (米種), yeast and water — so it is suitable for vegans (sold Wednesdays / by pre-order). The signature 米粉シフォンケーキ and its rusk contain egg and are not vegan. Small baked snacks (scones, snowballs) may contain dairy, so ask before ordering.
kyo_hirose_okomeya_cafe.hours_raw: 11:00-18:00. Closed Sun, Mon and holidays (rice-flour chiffon cake Tue-Sat, rice bread on Wed).
kyo_hirose_okomeya_cafe.notes: [GF] A genuinely useful stop for celiacs just south of Kyoto Station: a century-old rice merchant with an attached café where everything is 100% rice flour and the shop sells no wheat products at all. Grab a 米粉シフォンケーキ (rice-flour chiffon, Tue–Sat) or, on Wednesdays, freshly baked お米パン rice bread. Confirm the day's baking schedule (chiffon Tue–Sat, bread Wed) and that lunch/café-gohan service is running, as it has been paused at times. Small neighborhood shop — assume cash.

chef_bio.chef_name: 廣瀬弘香 (Hirose Hiroka) — 米粉マイスター / 五ツ星お米マイスター
roles: 店主・オーナー (café owner)
五ツ星お米マイスター Prof (five-star rice master, professional grade)
米粉マイスター (rice-flour master)
米粉パンマイスター (rice-flour bread master)
chef_bio.origin: Originally from Okayama; studied fine art at a design university, then married into the third-generation Hirose rice-merchant family in Higashi-Kujo, Minami-ku, Kyoto.
chef_bio.background: 廣瀬米穀店 was founded in 昭和元年 (1926) and is now in its third generation, giving it roughly 99 years of history as a Kyoto rice merchant. Around 2014, after the shop stopped wholesaling to a large facility, an empty space opened up in the store; the owner's encounter with rice flour and the question 「米屋にしかできないことってなんだろう？」 (what can only a rice shop do?) led to the 2017 opening of the attached café, お米屋カフェ・ふぇ〜る. 廣瀬弘香 — originally from Okayama and trained in fine art before marrying into the family — holds the 五ツ星お米マイスター qualification (with the professional 'Prof' instructor grade) plus 米粉マイスター and 米粉パンマイスター certifications, and the shop is a 「五ツ星お米マイスター認定店」. The rice used is milled in-house (自家精米) from selected varieties, and all café products are made with 100% rice flour and no wheat flour or white sugar.
chef_bio.philosophy: The owner wants to spread rice bread 「グルテンフリーのパンとしてではなく、生米から作る一つのおいしい食べ物として」 — not merely as gluten-free bread, but as a delicious food in its own right made from raw rice. She distinguishes 米粉パン (from rice grown for milling into flour) from her お米パン made from top-grade (一等上質米) whole rice, emphasizing the aroma and natural taste of freshly milled rice.
chef_bio.specialty: 米屋の米粉シフォンケーキ, お米パン（こめやパン）, 米粉ラスク

anecdotes.text: 2014年ごろ大型施設への卸販売を中止して店内に空きスペースが生じ、米粉との出会いから『米屋にしかできないことってなんだろう？』という問いが2017年の『お米屋カフェ・ふぇ〜る』開業につながった。
2023年に京都女性起業家賞・優秀賞、京都商工会議所主催の知恵-1グランプリ チャレンジ部門グランプリを受賞。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: アサヒパック広報のnote記事と公式サイト・米粉マイスター協会の紹介により、廣瀬米穀店は昭和元年（1926年）創業の3代目の米屋で、店主・廣瀬弘香（岡山出身・美術系大学卒で家業に嫁いだ）が五ツ星お米マイスター（Prof）等の資格を持ち、2017年に併設カフェ『お米屋カフェ・ふぇ〜る』を開業、全商品が米粉100％で小麦粉・白砂糖不使用。2023年に京都女性起業家賞優秀賞・知恵-1グランプリを受賞。お米パンは米粉パンと区別される。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 全商品を米粉100％で製造し、小麦粉・白砂糖は一切使用していない（Made with 100% rice flour; no wheat flour or white sugar used at all).

It is a rice merchant / rice mill and food shop (自家精米), not a certified dedicated gluten-free kitchen — the product line is entirely rice-based and the shop sells no wheat products, but celiacs should confirm on the day that no wheat is handled or stored on-site.

vegan_cross_contact.text: お米パン／こめやパンは米・米油・メープル・塩・米種・酵母・お湯のみで焼く植物性の食品（rice bread is plant-based). シフォンケーキには卵が含まれる（chiffon contains egg).

staff_allergy_handling.text: 店主は米粉マイスター・五ツ星お米マイスターの有資格者で、グルテンフリーを明確に掲げている（Owner is a certified rice-flour master and explicitly markets the shop as gluten-free).

positives.text: 米屋なので小麦製品を扱わず、カフェのお菓子・パンはすべて米粉100％（A rice shop that handles no wheat products; all café sweets and bread are 100% rice flour).
自家精米したての新鮮な米から作るグルテンフリーのお米パンとシフォンケーキ（Gluten-free rice bread and chiffon made from freshly in-house-milled rice).

owner_signoff.reason: Greg, bulk pass 2026-08-19: approved at the tier the adversarial review settled on. Evidence, independent-source count and residual flags for each are on the record in gf_review and in GF_REVIEW_SIGNOFF.md.

gf_review.why: I tried to disprove this by (a) checking whether a 米穀店 also stocks barley (押麦/もち麦/雑穀 — gluten) alongside rice, (b) hunting for wheat items in the cafe line, and (c) looking for any glutening report. I found none: the shop's own live site (Obon notice posted three days before this audit, so it is open and trading) titles itself 「廣瀬米穀店お米屋カフェ | グルテンフリー」 and states 「米の販売とグルテンフリー商品の製造・販売をしています」, and three independent Japanese sources corroborate a wheat-free, 100%-rice-flour line — mypl.net local media quotes 「小麦粉・白砂糖を一切使用せず、米粉100%で作っている」, the asahipac rice-trade note.com feature describes bread made from rice only (no wheat and no rice-flour blend), and Kyoto City's furusato-nozei catalogue lists the product as グルテンフリー「米屋のお米パン」. What I could NOT find is any celiac-grade source (no FindMeGlutenFree/HappyCow celiac review) and any published allergen-control or cross-contamination statement, so this clears `high` on composition evidence but must not be called dedicated.
red_flags: No published allergen-control / cross-contamination protocol anywhere — composition is wheat-free but handling is undocumented
No celiac-grade corroboration (no FMGF/HappyCow celiac review) — all corroboration is Japanese local media and trade press

It is a working rice merchant with an in-house 精米 mill; Japanese rice shops commonly also sell 押麦/もち麦 (barley = gluten). No evidence found that this one does, but the product range should be eyeballed on the day
Very limited windows: rice bread Wednesdays only (11:30-), chiffon Tue-Sat (11:00-) — an unplanned visit may find nothing GF for sale
gf_review.plain_rice: No cooked gohan is served — it is a rice shop with a bake-café (chiffon, rusks, rice bread). It does sell raw self-milled rice, which is the safest thing in the building, but not a meal.

kyo_ikariya_beika.gf_detail: A rice-flour baumkuchen specialist that sources raw rice from farmers (non-glutinous rice from Shiga Prefecture, etc.), mills it in-house at the workshop, and bakes baumkuchen using only freshly ground, fresh rice flour. The brand does not push a gluten-free label to the fore ('rather than proclaiming gluten-free'), placing the taste and texture of freshly ground rice flour front and center. The baked-goods production line uses no wheat, but whether the drinks and accompaniments served at the small in-store eat-in area at the back are entirely free of wheat products should be confirmed at the time of visit.
kyo_ikariya_beika.vegan_detail: Because the baumkuchen is baked using egg, butter (dairy), and sugar, no vegan-friendly items could be confirmed. It is gluten-free thanks to rice flour, but it is not plant-based.
kyo_ikariya_beika.hours_raw: 10:00-19:00, open every day (open year-round, closed only January 1)
kyo_ikariya_beika.notes: [GF] Central, tourist-friendly machiya workshop 5 min from Karasuma-Oike station; a self-milling 米粉 (rice-flour) baumkuchen specialist where the entire baked line is wheat-free — an easy, low-risk GF gift/snack stop for celiacs. Everything is built on freshly milled rice flour rather than wheat. There is a small eat-in space in back; if eating in, confirm no shared wheat items accompany drinks. Cards accepted; reservations possible for pickups.

roles: operator
founder
chef_bio.background: 運営は京都・大阪でフレンチ『イカリヤ食堂』やビストロ『ikariya523』、ウェディング事業などを手がける株式会社Ludico（代表：鳥井和機）で、IKARIYA BEIKA KYOTOはその食ブランド群のひとつ。ブランド名の『BEIKA＝米菓』は米粉菓子を指す（実際の煎餅製造業由来ではない）。物語は『ひとりの菓子職人が抱いた好奇心』から始まり、築100年超の京町家を改装して工房兼店舗を構えた。農家から生米を仕入れ、店内で挽きたてに自家製粉した米粉でバウムクーヘンを焼く。挽きたて米粉は含む水分量が違い、しっとりした質感が最大のこだわり。2023年3月29日にはJR京都伊勢丹で期間限定出店し、米粉のグルテンフリーバウムクーヘンを販売した。
chef_bio.philosophy: グルテンフリーというラベルより、挽きたて自家製粉の米粉ならではの味・しっとりした食感を主役にする（味先行、GFは結果）。
chef_bio.specialty: 自家製粉 rice-flour baumkuchen — 定番6種（フワフワ/ザクザク/白あんマロン/ショコラ/ほうじ茶ワヅカ茶 ほか）+ 季節限定（レモン・焼アンノウイモ・七福バウム等）

anecdotes.text: 運が良ければ京町家の外から職人がバウムを焼く工房の様子を眺められる。
毎週日曜14時から店頭に並ぶ『朝焼きバウム』（1カット220円）は実店舗のみの限定商品で、定番よりさらにふんわりした食感が味わえる。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト・食べログ・アットプレス各リリース・KYOTOLIFE・life-info・まげわっぱブログ、および株式会社Ludicoのリリース群を総合すると、母体はイカリヤ食堂やikariya523等を運営する株式会社Ludico（代表 鳥井和機）。滋賀県産うるち米などを生米で仕入れ工房内で挽きたてに自家製粉し、グルテンフリーの米粉バウムクーヘンを焼く専門店。2023年3月29日のJR京都伊勢丹期間限定出店・オンライン販売あり。煎餅製造業由来という説は日本語一次情報では裏付けられなかった。

gf_cross_contamination.text: 焼き菓子の製造ラインは自家製粉の米粉のみで小麦粉を使用しない専門工房のため、製品自体の小麦クロスコンタミ・リスクは低い。
個人ブログでは『メニューはすべて米粉を使ったグルテンフリー』と報告されているが、店奥のイートインで供する飲み物・付け合わせに小麦品がないかは公式には未確認。

vegan_cross_contact.text: バウムクーヘンは卵・乳(バター)を含むため、ヴィーガン品との交差接触管理に関する情報はなく、そもそもヴィーガン提供品が確認できない。

staff_allergy_handling.text: 米菓職人が自家製粉した米粉で丁寧に焼き上げると明記されるが、個別の小麦アレルギー対応プロトコルの記載は見当たらない。

positives.text: 専門店として全焼き菓子が米粉ベースの小麦不使用で、グルテンフリーの土産・スイーツとして京都のGFガイドでも紹介されている。
生米を工房内で自家製粉するなど原材料管理にこだわり、JR京都伊勢丹でもグルテンフリーバウムとして販売実績がある。

That plus the company's own atpress releases (「米粉で作ったグルテンフリーのバウムクーヘン」), KYOTOLIFE local media, and the magewappa blog (「メニューはすべて米粉を使ったグルテンフリーです」) clears the `high` bar. No allergen/contamination protocol is published anywhere and I found no celiac-grade review, so it cannot go higher.

kyo_mushiyashinai.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. [Adversarial GF review 2026-08-19: dedicated→options. Identity checks out and there is NO same-romaji soba confusion here: this is the soy-milk patisserie at 京都市左京区一乗寺里ノ西町78 (own site 648471.com, Tabelog 26003357, category ケーキ/カフェ), open and trading, and Japanese searches for a same-name Kyoto soba house turned up nothing. The label itself collapses on the shop's OWN documents: their FAQ states 「当店では同じ工房にて乳、卵を使用した商品を製造しております」 and then explicitly disclaims 「ほんの微量でも発症される方については、お客様各位にてご判断いただけますようお願いいたします」 — a shared workshop plus a trace-amount self-disclaimer, which is the opposite of a celiac-safe dedicated facility. Their own site carries no 全商品グルテンフリー or 完全グルテンフリー banner at all; グルテンフリー is a product CATEGORY sitting beside per-item 卵・乳・小麦不使用 labels, and their GF senbei lists plain 醤油 (脱脂加工大豆) with no wheat-free documentation. I also checked the record's cited corroboration and it does not hold: the co-trip article (701134, published 2025-10-04) never says 全商品グルテンフリー — it says GF and vegan is 「もうひとつのコンセプト」 (one of their concepts) — so the quote on the record is misattributed, and a 2018 first-hand Japanese report notes 「小麦を使ってあるケーキもあるから確認したんだよ」.] The operator states 「2023年10月には完全グルテンフリー化の為、生産工場と店舗をリニューアルオープンしました」 (In October 2023 they reopened both the production factory and the shop after renovating them for complete gluten-free conversion), and describes the venue as 全商品グルテンフリー (every product gluten-free). Allergen scope is unusually deep: a dedicated 「ミラクル＊ヴァンヌフ 29」 line is free of 29 designated allergens (29品目アレルゲン物質除去), building on the wheat/dairy/egg-free (小麦・乳・卵不使用) base of all cakes. Principal caveat for celiacs: the kitchen is soy-centric (豆乳/おから), and the signature 豆乳醤油プリン uses 醤油 — confirm they use a gluten-free tamari, though a fully-GF-converted facility would be expected to.
kyo_mushiyashinai.vegan_detail: The house concept is explicitly 「グルテンフリー＆ヴィーガン」. Because the cakes are built on 米粉 (rice flour) and 豆乳 (soy milk) instead of wheat, dairy and egg, a large share of the sweets — puddings, roll cake, brûlée, okara cookies, the 29-allergen ミラクル cakes — are plant-based. Not everything is guaranteed vegan (seasonal afternoon-tea components and some savory items are unconfirmed), so vegan diners should ask per item.
kyo_mushiyashinai.hours_raw: 11:00-18:00 (eat-in L.O. 17:30). Closed Mondays and Tuesdays (regardless of holidays). Some listings show a 10:30 open; as of 2026 in-store offering leans toward pre-ordered whole cakes and baked-good assortments.
kyo_mushiyashinai.notes: [GF-dedicated] Kyoto's rare fully-gluten-free patisserie: in October 2023 the owner rebuilt the production factory and the Ichijoji shop specifically to eliminate gluten, and now markets every product as gluten-free. Cakes use rice flour and soy milk; a dedicated line removes 29 allergens. Celiac risk from cross-contact is minimal by their own claim, but the kitchen leans heavily on soy — one of the 29 they otherwise track — and the soy-sauce pudding should be confirmed as GF tamari. Reservations/pre-orders drive whole cakes; eat-in seats are not reservable.

chef_bio.chef_name: うのゆきこ (Uno Yukiko) — 豆乳パティシエ / soy-milk patissier
roles: Owner
Head patissier
Founder
chef_bio.background: Uno Yukiko styles herself as 「世界で唯一の豆乳パティシエ」 (the world's only soy-milk patissier) and opened Mushiyashinai in Ichijoji around 2006. In December 2009 an encounter with a boy who had 23 food allergies (23品目の食物アレルギー) pushed her to develop allergy-friendly cakes made from 米粉 and 豆乳 rather than wheat and dairy, and by 2020 she completed a cake free of 29 allergens (29品目のアレルゲン不使用). In October 2023 she renovated both the production factory and the shop expressly to convert the whole operation to gluten-free. This Ichijoji patisserie is a distinct venue from the operator's soy-milk ramen line (branded 'UNO RAMEN'); the sweets shop, not the ramen, is the celiac-relevant location.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「すべての人を笑顔にするために」— pursuing 食のバリアフリー (barrier-free food) across social, health and religious dietary needs; plant-based, gluten-free, allergen-conscious baking.
chef_bio.specialty: Soy-milk & rice-flour cakes, 焼き菓子, 豆乳プリン, ブリュレ, おから (soy-pulp) sweets and light savory items

anecdotes.text: The allergen mission traces to a December 2009 meeting with a boy carrying 23 food allergies, which led to the 29-allergen-free 「ミラクル＊ヴァンヌフ 29」 cake by 2020.
In October 2023 the factory and shop were renovated and reopened expressly to convert the whole operation to gluten-free.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 648471.com（公式）と ことりっぷ（co-trip 701134）、ふるさとチョイス／ふるなび、食べログ が一致して、2006年開業のうのゆきこ主宰の豆乳パティスリーであること、2009年12月の23品目アレルギーの男の子との出会い、2020年の29品目アレルゲン不使用ケーキ完成、2023年10月に完全グルテンフリー化のため生産工場と店舗をリニューアルオープンしたことを裏付ける。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Own claim of 完全グルテンフリー化: the production factory and shop were rebuilt in Oct 2023 to be entirely gluten-free, and all products are marketed as 全商品グルテンフリー — implying no wheat is handled on-site, so cross-contact risk is minimal.
Corroborated: 豆乳などを活用することで全商品グルテンフリーの身体に優しいパティスリー.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Signature 「SOY豆乳醤油プリン」 is served with a 醤油 (soy-sauce) caramel; ordinary soy sauce contains wheat. Given the facility's stated complete gluten-free conversion they would be expected to use a wheat-free tamari, but this is not explicitly documented — confirm directly for celiac safety.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Kitchen uses no dairy in cakes (豆乳 substitutes milk) and offers wheat/dairy/egg-free lines, reducing animal-product contact, but eat-in afternoon-tea and some savory items are not confirmed fully vegan.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Deep allergen literacy: shop developed 29-allergen-free (29品目アレルゲン物質除去) cakes and frames itself around 食のバリアフリー for allergy sufferers since 2009.

positives.text: Card / e-money / QR payments accepted; parking and eat-in café available.

gf_review.why: Identity checks out and there is NO same-romaji soba confusion here: this is the soy-milk patisserie at 京都市左京区一乗寺里ノ西町78 (own site 648471.com, Tabelog 26003357, category ケーキ/カフェ), open and trading, and Japanese searches for a same-name Kyoto soba house turned up nothing. The label itself collapses on the shop's OWN documents: their FAQ states 「当店では同じ工房にて乳、卵を使用した商品を製造しております」 and then explicitly disclaims 「ほんの微量でも発症される方については、お客様各位にてご判断いただけますようお願いいたします」 — a shared workshop plus a trace-amount self-disclaimer, which is the opposite of a celiac-safe dedicated facility. Their own site carries no 全商品グルテンフリー or 完全グルテンフリー banner at all; グルテンフリー is a product CATEGORY sitting beside per-item 卵・乳・小麦不使用 labels, and their GF senbei lists plain 醤油 (脱脂加工大豆) with no wheat-free documentation. I also checked the record's cited corroboration and it does not hold: the co-trip article (701134, published 2025-10-04) never says 全商品グルテンフリー — it says GF and vegan is 「もうひとつのコンセプト」 (one of their concepts) — so the quote on the record is misattributed, and a 2018 first-hand Japanese report notes 「小麦を使ってあるケーキもあるから確認したんだよ」.
red_flags: Shop's own FAQ: 同じ工房にて乳、卵を使用した商品を製造 — shared workshop, not a dedicated line
Shop's own trace-amount disclaimer: 「ほんの微量でも発症される方については、お客様各位にてご判断いただけますようお願いいたします」 — the shop itself declines to vouch for trace-sensitive customers, i.e. celiacs
No 全商品グルテンフリー / 完全グルテンフリー claim on the shop's own site; グルテンフリー is one product category among several
MISATTRIBUTED EVIDENCE on the record: the co-trip quote 「全商品グルテンフリー」 does not appear in co-trip article 701134, which instead calls GF+vegan 'another concept'
Per-item 卵・乳・小麦不使用 labelling implies non-wheat-free items exist in the catalogue
GF senbei ingredient list shows 醤油 with no wheat-free/tamari documentation; 豆乳醤油プリン likewise unresolved
Historic first-hand report (2018) confirms some cakes contained wheat — the pre-2023 baseline was a mixed kitchen
The Oct-2023 完全グルテンフリー化 renovation claim could not be verified on any primary page of the shop's own site
No celiac-grade corroboration anywhere (absent from FindMeGlutenFree, atly, endlessdistances); a Kyoto GF guide classes local shops like this as ゆるグルテンフリー
gf_review.identity_note: Identity verified with extra care per the Kyoto-confusion warning: this IS the Ichijoji rice-flour/soy-milk confectionery (648471.com = mu-shi-ya-shi-na-i), NOT a soba house, and no same-name Kyoto soba shop surfaced in Japanese searches. The identity is fine; the gf_detail text on the record is what is wrong.

gf_uncited_downgrade.note: Tier held down: 1 safety finding(s) on this record were checked against their sources and NOT supported by them. This overrides the owner sign-off, which was given on that evidence — needs his re-review.

kyo_oshokuya_kappa.gf_detail: [WARNINGS (Greg, 2026-08-19): the shop serves GLUTEN-REDUCED beer — that is not celiac-safe and must be declined regardless of the all-GF menu. The gluten-free pizza crust is bought in from an outside supplier (Pizza Icaro), so crust safety is third-party, not this kitchen.] Japanese sources resolve the conflict in favor of a full conversion: since September 2024 the kitchen uses no wheat flour at all (小麦粉を一切つかわず), replacing wheat pasta and focaccia with house-made rice-flour (米粉) pasta and bread — the whole menu is now gluten-free. The owner's own blog does NOT admit wheat is still served; the sentence about wheat pasta/focaccia is a past-tense counterfactual ('we could have kept using them with no problem, but chose to convert'). Order anything, or ask for the グルテンフリーコース (50-vegetable GF course); note the restaurant still posts a contamination disclaimer (コンタミの可能性があるので小麦アレルギーに対応しておりません), so a strict celiac should self-identify and confirm seasonings/no cross-contact.
kyo_oshokuya_kappa.vegan_detail: This is a vegetable-sommelier restaurant with strong produce focus, but it is emphatically NOT vegan — the menu is heavy on meat (Kameoka beef, lamb, chicken), fish/seafood and cheese, and the owner's blog worries customers wrongly assume it went vegan. Plant-forward options like the vegetable spaghetti/risotto and green salad can likely be made vegan on request (confirm no butter, cheese or dashi); arrange vegan needs in advance.
kyo_oshokuya_kappa.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30-15:00 (L.O. 14:30) / Dinner 17:30-22:00 (L.O. 21:30). Closed day reported inconsistently across sources (empacede: Tuesdays + irregular; some listings show Wednesday or Sunday) - treat as irregular and confirm.
kyo_oshokuya_kappa.notes: [GF] As of Sept 2024 the entire kitchen is wheat-flour-free — a genuine 100% conversion, not shared with a wheat line; pasta is rice-flour and bread is 米粉パン. Celiacs can eat broadly here, and the 50-vegetable グルテンフリーコース is the safest showcase order. The one caveat: the restaurant posts a contamination disclaimer and says it cannot formally guarantee against a wheat allergy, so self-identify as celiac and confirm cross-contact and sauces. Not vegetarian/vegan-oriented — plenty of meat, seafood and cheese.

chef_bio.chef_name: 石橋健志 (Ishibashi Kenji)
roles: owner-chef
野菜ソムリエ / Vegetable Sommelier
chef_bio.background: Ishibashi Kenji is the owner-chef of Oshokuya Kappa, described as the only Japan Vegetable Sommelier Association (日本野菜ソムリエ協会) certified restaurant in Kyoto. In a 14 September 2024 blog post he announced the restaurant's pivot to the concept 'グルテンフリーで叶える至福のイタリアン' (blissful Italian achieved through gluten-free), switching the kitchen to use no wheat flour. He is explicit that the change was voluntary — his business was thriving on wheat pasta and focaccia — motivated by learning about gluten's effects rather than being forced by an allergy.
chef_bio.philosophy: Delicious first, gluten-free second — as a craftsman he says '美味しく無いならグルテンフリーにする必要無い' (if it isn't delicious there's no point going gluten-free); he pledges the food is as tasty as before and centers seasonal Japanese vegetables via his sommelier training.
chef_bio.specialty: GF pasta (rice-flour), 米粉パン (rice-flour bread), and a 50-vegetable グルテンフリーコース

anecdotes.text: Cites tennis player Novak Djokovic overcoming gluten intolerance via a gluten-free diet and rising to world No.1 as inspiration for the switch.
Says he isn't wheat-allergic himself (only mild skin irritation) and is running a personal experiment of quitting wheat to see what changes.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The owner's own 2024-09-14 fcblog post announces a full conversion to gluten-free Italian using no wheat flour; the homepage repeats '小麦粉を一切つかわず' and the empacede GF guide rates it ★★★★★ with 'すべてのメニューがグルテンフリー' since Sept 2024. Note: empacede also states the shop does NOT accept wheat-allergy orders due to cross-contamination risk (コンタミの可能性) — so 'gluten-free' here means recipe-level, not celiac-safe.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Restaurant states 'コンタミの可能性があるので、小麦アレルギーに対応はしておりません' — cross-contamination is possible, so they do not formally accommodate a wheat allergy, despite the kitchen using no wheat flour.
Homepage repeats they serve gluten-free dishes with no wheat flour but explicitly '小麦アレルギーに対応はしておりません' due to contamination risk (likely supplier/seasoning-level).

staff_allergy_handling.text: The restaurant openly declines to guarantee safety for a medical wheat allergy (小麦アレルギー未対応) even while marketing itself as fully gluten-free; strict celiacs should self-identify and confirm.

positives.text: Kitchen converted entirely to gluten-free in Sept 2024, using no wheat flour; wheat pasta and focaccia were replaced with house-made rice-flour pasta and 米粉パン.
Curated Japanese GF guide rates it ★★★★★ with 'all menu items gluten-free' (すべてのメニューがグルテンフリー).
Signature 50-vegetable gluten-free course by a certified vegetable sommelier.

owner_signoff.reason: Greg. Survives scrutiny: the owner states 「小麦粉を含め麦系は現在一切使用していません」, which rules out the spelt trap that caught another Kyoto record, and FindMeGlutenFree carries ~126 ratings including roughly two dozen symptomatic-celiac reviews all reporting no symptoms. Held at high rather than dedicated because the shop own site says it cannot accommodate wheat allergy.

gf_review.why: This was the flagged high-risk Italian record and I went at it hardest: I checked for surviving wheat pasta/focaccia, for a spelt-style 'still gluten' substitute, for shared pasta water, and for any glutening report in English or Japanese. All three fail to disprove. The owner's Sept-2024 blog post and the shop's Japanese AND English homepages confirm a full conversion (「小麦粉を一切つかわず」); the FindMeGlutenFree listing carries an owner statement going further — 「小麦粉を含め麦系は現在一切使用していません」 (no barley-family grains either, which rules out the spelt trap) — and the Hot Pepper menu page states 「当店のお料理はすべてグルテンフリーです」 with 自家製米粉パン. FMGF shows 126 recent ratings, 'reported to be dedicated gluten-free', community-reported 'dedicated gluten-free pasta pot and water', and I read roughly two dozen reviews from self-identified symptomatic celiacs — every single symptom field said 'No symptoms', with zero glutening reports found. It stays at `high` and NOT dedicated because the shop itself explicitly refuses to accommodate a medical wheat allergy.
red_flags: The shop's own site, in Japanese and English, explicitly declines wheat-allergy accommodation: 「小麦を使った料理はございませんが、わからないところで紛れ込んでしまう可能性もございますので、小麦アレルギーに対応はしておりません」 / 'we cannot accommodate wheat allergies'. This is why it must not be labelled dedicated

FMGF reported GF items include 'Beer (Gluten-Reduced)' — gluten-REDUCED (enzyme-treated barley) beer is NOT celiac-safe and is inconsistent with the owner's '麦系は一切使用していません' claim. A celiac must decline the beer
The GF pizza crust is bought in from an outside supplier (Pizza Icaro per a recent reviewer), so crust safety depends on a third party, not the kitchen
Owner frames the conversion as a health/lifestyle choice, not an allergy programme ('this is not because of allergies') — motivation is wellness, which historically correlates with looser protocol
Effectively a one-chef operation; multiple reviewers note the chef works alone, so protocol quality is entirely person-dependent
gf_review.plain_rice: Not a rice-bowl restaurant. Risotto is on the menu and is widely reported GF, and house-made 米粉 bread and rice croquettes are served, but plain unseasoned gohan is not a standard item — do not plan on it here.

kyo_senza_x.gf_detail: [Adversarial GF review 2026-08-19: high→ask. The gluten-free substance of this record survives — Tabelog's own listing text still reads 「当店は小麦・グルテン・卵・乳製品を使用しないイタリア料理ベースのレストランです」 and kyotopi confirms imported corn/rice pasta, 米粉 bread, and that the inherited pizzeria wood oven is unused. What does NOT survive is that the place is operable. Tabelog carries the banner 「現在、スタッフ不足のため当面の間、休業しております」, and the official domain www.senza-x.com no longer serves the restaurant at all — it now returns an unrelated Korean sports-betting/toto page, and www.senza-x.com/en (its former booking page, still in search indexes) 404s. A lapsed domain plus a ~1-year staff-shortage 休業 (reservations stopped Sept 2025; this audit is Aug 2026) is functionally a closure, and an app must not route a celiac child to a shut door under a `high` badge.] Senza X describes itself as 「小麦・グルテン・卵・乳製品を使わないアレルギー対応のイタリア料理店」— a fully allergy-adapted Italian restaurant that uses no wheat, gluten, egg or dairy anywhere on the menu. Pasta is imported from Italy and made from corn and rice rather than wheat (「もちろんパスタはグルテンフリー」), and bread is baked from rice flour (「パンは米粉を使用したもの」), so the entire kitchen is free-from rather than offering modified dishes. IMPORTANT — current status: the venue is TEMPORARILY CLOSED (休業). Its Tabelog listing carries the banner 'Currently, we are temporarily closed due to staff shortages,' and its own booking system stopped accepting reservations from September 2025 onward; it has not been reported as permanently closed. Confirm reopening via the official site or Instagram before visiting.
kyo_senza_x.vegan_detail: The whole kitchen is egg- and dairy-free, and owner-chef Shiga's stated aim was a restaurant 'enjoyable by all, vegans and allergy sufferers,' so plant-based choices exist — e.g. 植物性乳酸菌のジェラート (plant-based probiotic gelato) and fruit sorbet (いちごのソルベ). However, most pasta and antipasti feature fish or meat (anchovy, sardine, clams, beef cheek, lamb), so it is options rather than a full vegan menu; ask when booking.
kyo_senza_x.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 11:00–17:30 (L.O. 16:30); closed Mondays and the day after public holidays. NOTE: temporarily closed since ~mid-2025 due to staff shortage — check Instagram/website for reopening.
kyo_senza_x.notes: [2026-08-19] Reported 休業 (closed indefinitely, staff shortage) on Tabelog, and the former official domain senza-x.com has lapsed — it now hosts an unrelated Korean gambling site and must not be linked. Verify the shop has reopened before relying on this entry. [GF] Whole-menu free-from Italian: no wheat, gluten, egg or dairy used anywhere, corn+rice pasta and 米粉 (rice-flour) bread, so cross-contamination risk is very low and it is one of Kyoto's safest celiac options when open. The old wood-fired pizza oven inherited from Da Yuki remains on site but is 「今のところ使用されていない」(not currently in use), so no wheat pizza is made. CURRENT STATUS (verified 2026-07-02): temporarily closed (休業) due to staff shortages, not permanently closed — reservations were suspended from Sept 2025; verify reopening before relying on it. Mention your allergy when booking.

chef_bio.chef_name: Shiga (志賀)
roles: owner
chef

chef_bio.background: Owner-chef Shiga opened Senza X on 9 February 2024 in the former premises of Pizzeria Napoletana Da Yuki in the Okazaki area of Sakyo-ku, after Da Yuki relocated ~200m east to a larger space. Shiga worked as sous-chef and sommelier at Da Yuki, a Michelin Bib Gourmand pizzeria also listed on Tabelog's 'Pizza 百名店.' Senza X ('senza' means 'without' in Italian) is a whole-menu free-from Italian restaurant using no wheat, gluten, egg or dairy. It seats 18. The stone pizza oven from Da Yuki has been preserved on site with the stated hope of one day serving pizza as well.
chef_bio.philosophy: Shiga says he held a dream for over 20 years to build a restaurant 'that can be enjoyed by all, vegans and allergy sufferers,' making the entire kitchen free-from rather than offering ad-hoc modifications; he also runs Senza X as a place to nurture young cooks toward their own future ventures.
chef_bio.specialty: Corn-and-rice gluten-free pasta imported from Italy, rice-flour (米粉) bread, and multi-course allergy-adapted Italian lunch

anecdotes.text: The wood-fired stone oven inherited from Da Yuki is kept on site with the goal of one day offering pizza, though it is currently unused.
The name SENZA means 'without' in Italian — reflecting the without-wheat/egg/dairy concept.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログマガジン（magazine.tabelog.com/articles/369395）・Leaf Kyoto・kyotopi（FdcL1）は、シェフ志賀氏がミシュラン・ビブグルマンかつ食べログ『ピッツァ百名店』の姉妹店『ピッツェリア・ナポレターナ ダユキ』の副料理長・ソムリエで、2024年2月9日にその跡地（左京区岡崎）で18席のSenza Xを開業したと伝える。全メニューが小麦・グルテン・卵・乳製品不使用で、パスタはイタリア産のとうもろこしと米から、パンは米粉。20年来の夢だったと語り、ダユキの石窯は残されている。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Entire kitchen is free-from — no wheat, gluten, egg or dairy used anywhere, so celiac cross-contamination risk is inherently minimal. Pasta is gluten-free ('もちろんパスタはグルテンフリー') and bread is rice-flour.
The inherited wood-fired pizza oven remains but is 'not currently in use' (今のところ使用されていない), so no wheat flour is handled for pizza.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Kitchen uses no egg or dairy at all; plant-based probiotic gelato (植物性乳酸菌のジェラート) is offered as a dessert.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Tabelog advises guests with allergies to state them when booking; the owner-chef built the restaurant specifically for allergy sufferers.

positives.text: Celiac blogger mamehana praised the pasta as tasting authentically like real pasta, unlike ordinary commercial gluten-free pasta, and confirmed the whole restaurant is 小麦・グルテン・卵・乳製品不使用.
Purpose-built allergy-adapted Italian: no wheat/gluten/egg/dairy on the entire menu, corn+rice pasta, 米粉 bread.

kyo_vegan_sweets_courier.gf_detail: [Owner review 2026-10-14: GF options. Band 2 (GF claim overstated, a narrower one survives) — set per recommendation. Only source describes the products, not the facility.] [Adversarial GF review 2026-08-19: dedicated→high. I hunted for a wheat product line, a shared-facility warning, or a glutening report and found none: identity is confirmed (株式会社クーリエ, Kyoto factory shipping nationwide, Higashiyama storefront), the entire catalogue is 米粉-based, the own claim is explicit (「グルテン、卵、乳製品、白砂糖を使わず、米粉で作ったスイーツ」 with 特別栽培の米粉・有機豆乳・オーガニックメープルシロップ), and the retail allergen listing on SweetsVillage declares 特定原材料 as 大豆・アーモンド・ごま・くるみ with no wheat and no 「同一工場で小麦を含む製品を製造」 warning. What fails the dedicated bar is the corroboration side: there is no celiac (セリアック) claim by the company, no published cross-contamination protocol or dedicated-facility certification, and no celiac-grade source lists it (absent from FindMeGlutenFree Kyoto, atly's celiac Kyoto list, and endlessdistances' celiac Kyoto guide). Two independent non-celiac-grade sources — the Kyoto rice-flour-sweets guide kameoka-up.net and the producer profile on merryna.jp — support real GF handling, which clears high but not dedicated.] The shop's own site states its sweets are 「グルテン、卵、乳製品、白砂糖を使わず、米粉で作ったスイーツ」— made with specially-cultivated rice flour (特別栽培の米粉) and containing no gluten, egg, dairy or white sugar. It is a dedicated gluten-free and vegan production facility (株式会社クーリエ) where no wheat flour is used anywhere, so there is no wheat in the kitchen to cross-contaminate. The physical storefront in Higashiyama opens Saturdays only (11:00–18:00); the business is primarily nationwide mail-order shipping from its Kyoto factory. Purchases on non-Saturday days are possible by advance reservation.
kyo_vegan_sweets_courier.vegan_detail: Describes itself as a 「プラントベースの米粉お菓子専門店」(plant-based rice-flour confectionery specialist). All products are made from carefully selected plant ingredients — no eggs, no dairy (casein-free), no animal products — using organic soy milk and organic maple syrup in place of dairy and refined sugar. Every item in the range is 100% vegan.
kyo_vegan_sweets_courier.hours_raw: Storefront Saturdays only, 11:00–18:00 (closed all other days; purchases possible other days by reservation). Mainly mail-order.
kyo_vegan_sweets_courier.notes: [GF-dedicated] Dedicated gluten-free + vegan rice-flour sweets factory (株式会社クーリエ) at 京都市東山区福稲御所ノ内町2番地14, near Tofukuji/Higashiyama — no wheat is used anywhere in production, so it is celiac-appropriate. IMPORTANT for visitors: the physical storefront is open Saturdays only (11:00–18:00); the business is primarily nationwide mail-order, so plan around Saturday hours or order online / reserve ahead for other days.

roles: founder

chef_bio.background: The founder turned to a gluten-free and plant-based diet after struggling with health problems following marriage and childbirth, and began studying nutrition and diet from scratch. Wanting guilt-free vegan sweets — free of wheat (gluten-free), dairy (casein-free), eggs and white sugar — to be more widely available, they began manufacturing and selling such confections. Vegan Sweets Courier launched in August 2015, and the business is now run as 株式会社クーリエ with 藤戸義晶 as representative. The company operates a Kyoto factory shipping nationwide, with a small Saturday-only storefront in its Higashiyama (福稲御所ノ内町) premises.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「大切なのは摂ることよりも抜くこと」— what matters is not what you add but what you take away; removing unnecessary ingredients (gluten, egg, dairy, white sugar, artificial colorants) to make sweets that can be enjoyed without guilt.
chef_bio.specialty: rice-flour vegan sweets, no gluten/egg/dairy/white sugar

anecdotes.text: The signature 'くるれ' cakes (French for 'vivid') get their colors entirely from natural ingredients via a special production method that uses no artificial colorants (色素を使わない特別な製法).
The founder began the gluten-free lifestyle out of personal necessity after post-childbirth health issues, then launched the brand in August 2015 in the role of development director.

The operator states 「すべてのメニューがグルテンフリーで、京都の食材を多く使い、ランチで提供する『うどん』は玄米、揚げ物の衣も米粉を使ったグルテンフリーに仕上げました。」 — the lunch udon is made from brown-rice (玄米) noodles and all fried items use rice-flour (米粉) batter, so no wheat flour is used anywhere on the menu. A curated Japanese GF guide independently confirms it is prepared 「完全に独立した厨房で調理」 (in a completely separate/independent kitchen) and that 「小麦不使用の調味料を厳選」 (wheat-free condiments, i.e. tamari-style soy, are used), which supports celiac-safe status. kyo_warewarewa_arashiyama.vegan_detail: The menu is fish-forward: nearly every udon and teishoku uses a bonito/kombu dashi (出汁) plus egg (だし巻き, 京鴨てりたま), duck (京鴨), or cod roe (明太子). The 昆布水サラダうどん (kombu-water salad udon) is described in press coverage as the plant-based/vegan-friendly option. Tofu-based とうめし may be adaptable but likely uses a dashi tare, so vegans should confirm. Not a vegan-focused venue.

kyo_warewarewa_arashiyama.notes: [GF-dedicated] All items are gluten-free with a separate/independent kitchen and wheat-free (tamari-style) seasonings, making it one of the few genuinely celiac-safe sit-down spots in central Arashiyama — a 2–3 min walk from Randen (Keifuku) Arashiyama Station, beside Tenryū-ji. Practical notes: no reservations accepted, cashless payment only (cards/IC/PayPay, no cash), and udon can sell out; arrive early. Dashi is bonito-based (GF, not vegan); confirm any non-gluten allergies with staff.

kyo_bakery_house_creek.gf_detail: Creek is a large everyday neighborhood bakery in Saiin that runs a genuine 米粉100％ (100% rice flour) gluten-free line alongside roughly 80 conventional wheat breads. The shop advertises 米粉を100％使用したグルテンフリーのパン and describes its signature 米粉100％グルテンフリー食パン as 卵・乳製品・小麦粉を一切使わず (using absolutely no egg, dairy, or wheat flour). Because the very same premises bakes and slices wheat bread all day, airborne wheat flour and shared equipment mean cross-contact is realistic — this is an OPTIONS venue, not a dedicated celiac-safe one. Celiacs should treat the rice-flour items as allergen-recipe products, not contamination-controlled ones.
kyo_bakery_house_creek.vegan_detail: The flagship 米粉100％グルテンフリー食パン is explicitly 卵・乳製品・小麦粉不使用 (no egg, dairy, or wheat), so it is incidentally vegan, and some rice-flour cookies may follow. Most of the ~80 breads, however, are standard wheat products with butter/dairy, so vegan choices are limited to a handful of the rice-flour line. Confirm ingredients per item, as recipes vary.
kyo_bakery_house_creek.hours_raw: 8:00–22:00, open daily (no regular closing day). Note: some listings cite 7:00–20:30 — confirm before visiting.
kyo_bakery_house_creek.notes: [GF] Ask staff directly for the 米粉100％ (100% rice flour) items — the gluten-free 食パン (loaf), rice-flour bagels, cookies and cheesecake. These are made to an egg/dairy/wheat-free recipe, but everything is produced in a shared, high-volume wheat bakery with visible flour dust, so this suits gluten-sensitive/allergy-aware diners rather than highly reactive celiacs. Buy sealed/whole items rather than open-shelf loose bread to reduce cross-contact, and go early as the GF line sells out.

Owner Kajiki Miyuki runs it single-handedly as a 米粉シフォンケーキ専門店 under the motto "心に笑顔の種を撒く" (sowing seeds of smiles), using 国産米粉100%, 豆乳, 米油 and きび砂糖, no baking powder, and keeping additives to a minimum. The shop became a viral hit (a short video reportedly reaching ~13 million / 1300万回 views) and now regularly sells out before noon. It operates only Thursdays and Saturdays.

anecdotes.text: 住宅街のガレージに建てた2坪の小さなお店で、2時間ほどで売り切れる人気店 (a 2-tsubo garage shop that sells out in about two hours).
2021年10月16日オープン。店主は梶木美夕紀さん。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: まいぷれ（店舗ページ＋伏見人vol.059）・kyotopi・osumituki・kameoka-up によれば、店主・梶木美夕紀さんが2021年10月16日に伏見区久我のガレージで始めた2坪のテイクアウト米粉シフォンケーキ専門店。国産米粉100%、豆乳、米油、きび砂糖使用、ベーキングパウダー不使用、添加物は極力不使用。木・土のみ営業で午前中に完売。動画1300万回再生の人気。

vegan_cross_contact.text: Base uses 豆乳/米油/きび砂糖, but some flavors use 牛乳 (dairy) and cream sandwiches use whipped cream.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Owner-run micro takeout stand; contact via Instagram/LINE to confirm allergen/kitchen details.

positives.text: "添加物は極力使わない、安心安全な米粉スイーツ".

gf_uncited_downgrade.note: Tier held down: 2 safety finding(s) on this record were checked against their sources and NOT supported by them. This overrides the owner sign-off, which was given on that evidence — needs his re-review.

kyo_coco_kyoto.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. Bean-to-bar chocolate and sweets shop whose products lean gluten-free: their own materials say "白砂糖・添加物を使用しないチョコレート" and "グルテンフリーやオーガニックカカオといった素材にもこだわり," and they sell 米粉 (rice-flour) cakes plus vegan-friendly chocolate. However, "グルテンフリー" here is a product/ingredient claim, not a facility one — the shop is a full patisserie (roll cakes, baumkuchen, sandwich cookies) and there is no statement that wheat is absent from the kitchen or that there is no cross-contact. For celiacs this stays at options: confirm item-by-item and ask about shared equipment before ordering.
kyo_coco_kyoto.vegan_detail: They advertise ヴィーガン対応 chocolate and Raw Botanical / Raw ケークショコラ items, but much of the cake lineup contains dairy cream, butter and eggs. Vegan buyers should confirm which specific chocolates/raw cakes are plant-based.
kyo_coco_kyoto.notes: [GF] Rice-flour (米粉) cakes and gluten-free-leaning chocolate, white-sugar-free and additive-free per the shop, but it is a full patisserie that also makes wheat-flour goods with no dedicated/no-wheat-on-premises claim. Celiacs: verify each item and ask about shared equipment/cross-contact before buying.

roles: owner
chocolatier
chef_bio.background: COCO KYOTO is a Kyoto bean-to-bar chocolate atelier that controls its chocolate from cacao-bean selection through manufacturing (カカオ豆の選定から製造まで一貫). The shop built its identity around 白砂糖不使用 (no refined sugar), 無添加 (additive-free) and グルテンフリー sweets, positioning indulgence without guilt under the slogan "おいしさに罪悪感はいらない." Its main store sits in Nakagyo-ku's Nishinokyo Sanjobocho near Nishioji-Oike. The brand has been recognized at the International Chocolate Awards for eight consecutive years.
chef_bio.philosophy: "おいしさに罪悪感はいらない" — delicious sweets that are refined-sugar-free, additive-free and gluten-free, using organic cacao and Kyoto ingredients.
chef_bio.specialty: Bean-to-bar and raw chocolate, rice-flour (米粉) cakes, chocolate terrines and roll cakes

anecdotes.text: インターナショナルチョコレートアワードを8年連続で受賞している (International Chocolate Award winner eight years running), including World and Asia-Pacific medals.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: coco-cacao.jp と kameoka-up.net によれば、白砂糖・添加物不使用、グルテンフリー、オーガニックカカオにこだわった京都・中京区西ノ京三条坊町のビーントゥバー・チョコレート店で、カカオ豆選定から製造まで一貫。インターナショナルチョコレートアワード8年受賞。米粉ケーキやヴィーガン対応チョコも販売。

vegan_cross_contact.text: Many cakes contain dairy and eggs; vegan applies only to specific chocolates/raw items.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No published allergen-handling protocol; buyers must confirm per-item and about shared equipment directly.

positives.text: "白砂糖・添加物を使用しないチョコレート" and "グルテンフリーやオーガニックカカオといった素材にもこだわり"; sells 米粉ケーキ.

gf_uncited_downgrade.note: Tier held down: 1 safety finding(s) on this record were checked against their sources and NOT supported by them. This overrides the owner sign-off, which was given on that evidence — needs his re-review.

kyo_everysoy.gf_detail: This soy-milk specialty cafe run by long-established Kyoto yuba maker ゆば庄 makes its signature choux pastry from rice flour and soy cream. The menu page states the ソイシュークリーム base is 「米粉のシュー生地と豆乳クリーム」and is 「乳製品不使用・グルテンフリー」— but note the chocolate flavor is an exception: 「ショコラのチョコレートの中には一部乳成分が含まれます」(contains some dairy). It is a small takeout-focused counter (テイクアウト中心の小さなカフェ) that also sells non-gluten-free ライトミール from the same shared counter, so this is a dessert/drink stop with genuine GF options, not a fully GF venue; celiacs should treat cross-contact from shared prep/counter as possible.
kyo_everysoy.vegan_detail: Everything is built on soy milk and the shop centers on plant-based soy, but the rice-flour choux pastry is likely egg-based and some flavors contain dairy (chocolate). No explicit vegan labeling was found, so vegans should confirm egg/dairy per item.
kyo_everysoy.notes: [GF] Soy-milk cafe by Kyoto yuba maker ゆば庄. The signature 米粉シュークリーム (SOY chou à la crème) is stated 乳製品不使用・グルテンフリー — a reliable GF treat (avoid the chocolate flavor, which contains some dairy). Because non-GF light meals are prepared and sold from the same small counter, treat it as a GF-options dessert/drink stop rather than a celiac-safe kitchen.

roles: parent company: ゆば庄 (Yubasho / 京湯葉の老舗)
chef_bio.background: EVERYSOY is a soy-focused cafe brand created by ゆば庄 (Yubasho), a long-established Kyoto yuba (tofu-skin) specialist. The shop's own site states 「京都で長年湯葉をつくり続けてきた京湯葉の老舗『ゆば庄』が、厳選したフレッシュな豆乳を使ってつくっています」. The concept ('Stop, Soy'n Go') is to help people enjoy nutritious soy in everyday, approachable forms — drinks and sweets — rather than only traditional yuba. It runs a small takeout-centered counter cafe at its 四条烏丸 branch near the Shijo-Karasuma crossing.
chef_bio.philosophy: Make high-nutrition soy an everyday pleasure via fresh soy milk drinks and dairy-free sweets.
chef_bio.specialty: Soy-milk drinks and the rice-flour, dairy-free ソイシュークリーム (SOY chou à la crème) and ソイティラミス.

anecdotes.text: The SOY chou à la crème pairs a rice-flour choux shell with soy-milk cream, marketed as 『とっても軽くてクリーミー』.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: everysoy.com（公式ブランド・メニュー・店舗ページ）は、京湯葉の老舗『ゆば庄』が厳選フレッシュ豆乳で手がけるソイカフェで、米粉・乳不使用のソイシュークリームやソイティラミスを提供と記載。四条烏丸に店舗（食べログ EVERYSOY 四条烏丸店）。KBS京都ラジオも特集。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Small takeout counter that also sells non-GF ライトミール from the same counter; shared prep space means cross-contact is possible.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Dessert/drink focus; no wheat soy sauce implicated in the signature items.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Chocolate flavor contains some dairy: 「ショコラのチョコレートの中には一部乳成分が含まれます」.

positives.text: Signature ソイシュークリーム explicitly labeled 乳製品不使用・グルテンフリー with a 米粉 (rice-flour) choux base.

kyo_loco_chicken.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. A Hawaiian-style mochiko/rice-flour chicken specialist. The Japanese GF guide jp.japan-glutenfree.com (rated ★★★★) states 「米粉チキン専門店です。米粉チキンは、小麦粉の代わりに米粉を使っており、グルテンフリーです」— the karaage is battered in rice flour, not wheat. Burgers can be made GF: 「ハンバーガーのバンズは、プラス200円で、グルテンフリーのバンズに変更できます」and tacos/taco rice are inherently GF. The guide notes wheat is present on-site only for standard burger buns and for beer; a shared fryer is likely at a general fried-chicken shop, so confirm dedicated oil and no wheat in the seasoning before ordering, and note the on-premises beer keeps this out of dedicated-GF territory.
kyo_loco_chicken.vegan_detail: A fried-chicken and burger shop; core menu is chicken. No vegan mains identified.
kyo_loco_chicken.notes: [GF] Rice-flour (mochiko) chicken specialist near Shijo-Kawaramachi. Per JP GF guide, the karaage/chicken uses rice flour instead of wheat (グルテンフリー), burgers swap to a GF bun for +¥200, and tacos/taco rice are GF. Wheat on-site is limited to standard buns and beer — but it is a small (5-seat) general fried-chicken shop, so confirm the fryer oil isn't shared with any wheat item and that seasonings are wheat-free before you order.

roles: owner-operated small shop
chef_bio.background: LOCO CHICKEN is a Hawaiian-influenced 米粉チキン (rice-flour / mochiko chicken) specialist that opened around 30 September 2021, about a 3-minute walk south of Kyoto-Kawaramachi Station in the Shijo-Kawaramachi area (河原町会館). It is a tiny first-come, first-served counter shop (5 seats) doing dine-in and takeout, blending Hawaiian 'mochiko chicken' style with Kyoto tastes; the Kyoto-native owner drew inspiration from Saipan's 'LOCO & TACO.' The signature is thin, light, crisp rice-flour-battered chicken served as burgers or over-rice plates.
chef_bio.philosophy: Light, crisp mochiko/rice-flour chicken in a casual Hawaiian plate-lunch format.
chef_bio.specialty: 米粉唐揚げ (rice-flour karaage) plates and chicken burgers with an optional gluten-free bun (+¥200).

anecdotes.text: Menu spans classic, yangnyeom, Nashville-hot and yuzu-pepper tartar chicken burgers plus 3- and 4-piece rice plates.
米粉チキンは小麦粉の代わりに米粉を使いグルテンフリー。ハンバーガーのバンズはプラス200円でグルテンフリーのバンズに変更でき、席数はカウンター5席のみ。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: jp.japan-glutenfree.com（京都GFリスト、★★★★、米粉チキン専門店・GFバンズ+200円・カウンター5席）、osumituki.com（2021/9/30オープン・住所・価格・サイパンLOCO & TACO由来）、食べログ/Retty 掲載が一致。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Small general fried-chicken shop; a shared fryer is likely. Guide states wheat on-site is limited to burger buns and beer, but fryer/seasoning cross-contact is unconfirmed — ask before ordering.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Offers a paid GF bun swap (+¥200), indicating some allergy awareness, but no formal cross-contact protocol documented.

positives.text: 米粉チキン専門店です。米粉チキンは、小麦粉の代わりに米粉を使っており、グルテンフリーです — rated ★★★★ by JP GF guide.

gf_uncited_downgrade.note: Tier held down: 1 safety finding(s) on this record were checked against their sources and NOT supported by them. This overrides the owner sign-off, which was given on that evidence — needs his re-review.

kyo_nicole_naturelle.gf_detail: THE NICOLE is a conventional Kyoto patisserie that also runs a separate allergen-free sub-line, Nicole Naturelle, whose sweets are made with 100% domestic rice flour and no wheat. The venue's own site states 『卵、乳製品、小麦粉、動物性油脂は使用しておりません』 and describes the line as 『卵、乳、白砂糖不使用』『グルテンフリー』『ヴィーガンスイーツ』 using 国産米粉100%. However, the SAME shop bakes ordinary wheat flour cakes and serves 欧風スパイスカレー (European-style spice curry, typically a wheat-roux base), so the kitchen is shared and cross-contact with wheat flour is a real risk — celiacs must confirm the item is from the Naturelle line and ideally order it pre-made/sealed. Because of the shared wheat kitchen this stays an 'options' venue, not a dedicated GF facility.
kyo_nicole_naturelle.vegan_detail: The Nicole Naturelle line is fully plant-based — 卵・乳・動物性油脂不使用, using 京豆腐 (Kyoto tofu), 豆乳ヨーグルト (soy yogurt), soy-based 'butter', coconut oil and maple syrup in place of dairy and eggs. These items are explicitly marketed as ヴィーガンスイーツ. The parent THE NICOLE shop, though, also sells conventional cakes with egg/dairy and non-vegan curry, so only the Naturelle line is vegan — choose from it specifically.
kyo_nicole_naturelle.hours_raw: 10:30-16:00; closed Mondays and Tuesdays (per the venue's own site). Nicole Naturelle allergen-free sweets are by reservation / online order only. Hours differ between sources (Tabelog lists Mon-Fri 10:30-18:00, Sat 10:30-17:00, closed Sun) - confirm before visiting.
kyo_nicole_naturelle.notes: [GF] The Nicole Naturelle sub-line uses 国産米粉100% and no wheat, but it is baked in the same kitchen as THE NICOLE's ordinary wheat cakes and wheat-roux spice curry — treat as cross-contact risk, not celiac-safe. Order Naturelle items specifically (they are reservation/online-order only, sold mostly as whole tarts, chocolate and sablé tins) and confirm the item is from the allergen line. Cash only; small counter shop in the Horikawa shopping arcade.

chef_bio.chef_name: 堀口 微笑琉 (Horiguchi Bishōru)
roles: owner
pâtissier
curry cook
chef_bio.background: Owner-pâtissier 堀口微笑琉 was born in 1979 in Kyoto's Nishijin district and trained at several patisseries between 1999 and 2006 before opening his own shop, 洋菓子屋Sorcier, in Umeda in 2008. The business relocated and evolved over the years — becoming Kitchen&Cake NICOLE in 2015 and rebranding as THE NICOLE at the current 西陣 (Nishijin) location in 2019. In 2022 he added a spice-curry operation (麺屋 微笑琉 / NICOLEカレー, a once-a-week spice-curry-udon venture), and in 2023 he launched the Nicole Naturelle allergen-free, vegan, gluten-free sweets line. The shop's stated aim is 「食材の制限がある方も楽しめるスイーツ」— sweets that people with dietary restrictions can also enjoy.
chef_bio.philosophy: A hybrid patisserie-and-curry café built around inclusivity and low-sugar / low-fat, 'body-friendly' sweets, with the Nicole Naturelle line created so that people with egg, dairy and wheat restrictions can still enjoy cakes.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour (米粉) vegan gluten-free tarts, 京豆腐 tofu-based raw-chocolate confections and 黒糖 sablé tins; also European-style spice curry.

anecdotes.text: The venture is a 洋菓子×スパイスカレー hybrid — a Western-confectionery shop that also serves a meat-free 'Nicole curry' deriving umami from vegetables, plus rotating daily creative spice curries.
The allergen-free Nicole Naturelle line was launched in 2023, years after the base patisserie, specifically to serve customers with dietary restrictions.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: the-nicole.com（自社サイト沿革）に、オーナー堀口微笑琉（1979年西陣生まれ、1999-2006修業、2008 Sorcier梅田、2015 Kitchen&Cake NICOLE、2019 THE NICOLE西陣、2022 麺屋微笑琉、2023 Nicole Naturelle）、Nicole Naturelleの「卵・乳製品・小麦粉・動物性油脂不使用」「グルテンフリー」「ヴィーガン」「国産米粉100%」の記載あり。kyotopi.jpは洋菓子×スパイスカレーのハイブリッド業態を紹介。食べログは住所・営業時間・現金のみを裏付け。

gf_cross_contamination.text: The Nicole Naturelle allergen-free sweets are baked in the same premises as THE NICOLE's conventional wheat-flour cakes and a wheat-roux European-style spice curry, so shared-kitchen cross-contact with wheat is a genuine risk despite the rice-flour recipes.
Venue's own claim for the line: 『卵、乳製品、小麦粉、動物性油脂は使用しておりません』／『グルテンフリー』／国産米粉100%. No dedicated-facility or cross-contamination protocol is stated.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Not applicable to the sweets line; however the shop's spice curry is not part of the gluten-free line and should be assumed to contain wheat (欧風カレー roux) — do not treat curry as GF.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Nicole Naturelle items are made in a kitchen that also handles dairy, eggs and animal fats for conventional cakes; the Naturelle line itself is 卵・乳・動物性油脂不使用 but shared equipment means trace animal-product contact is possible.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop positions itself as making 「食材の制限がある方も楽しめるスイーツ」and takes Naturelle items ご予約のみ (by reservation), suggesting allergy awareness, but no formal celiac cross-contact handling procedure is documented.

positives.text: Explicit written wheat-free claim using 100% domestic rice flour: 『卵、乳製品、小麦粉、動物性油脂は使用しておりません』『グルテンフリー』, a dedicated recipe line rather than incidental GF items.
Naturelle line is fully vegan (京豆腐, 豆乳ヨーグルト, ココナッツオイル), doubling as a good option for plant-based celiacs.

kyo_nicole_naturelle.pin_source: Tabelog https://tabelog.com/en/kyoto/A2601/A260202/26032715/; cross-checked: listing address 京都府京都市上京区奈良物町481番地 (GSI) 17m; 2026-09-28

kyo_oubon.gf_detail: OUBON is a conventional Western pâtisserie near Fushimi Inari that sells regular wheat cakes AND a separate allergy-oriented 米粉 (rice-flour) line, so wheat is handled in the same kitchen. The shop's own claim for the rice-flour line reads: 「全てに米粉を使用していますのでアレルギーをお持ちの方でも、もちろん食べていただけます」 ("Everything uses rice flour, so even those with allergies can of course eat it"). Because the same bakery also produces wheat pastries daily, cross-contact with gluten is a real risk and this cannot be treated as celiac-safe — confirm with staff and buy only the labeled 米粉/グルテンフリー items.
kyo_oubon.vegan_detail: The rice-flour items are not vegan: the shop lists 卵 (egg) and 乳 (dairy) as allergens on its gluten-free products. The signature 豆乳米粉ロール is described as 「グルテンフリー商品となっており、アレルギー物質は卵、乳」 and uses Hokkaido cream (whipped with soymilk), so egg and dairy remain. No vegan line is advertised.
kyo_oubon.hours_raw: 10:00–20:00, closed Wednesdays (some listings show Wed 12:00–18:00). Tel 075-632-8287.
kyo_oubon.notes: [GF] Not celiac-safe — this is a shared wheat kitchen. OUBON bakes conventional wheat cakes alongside its 米粉 (rice-flour) allergy line, so gluten cross-contact is likely; only the explicitly labeled 米粉/グルテンフリー sweets (e.g. 豆乳米粉ロール, 米粉フィナンシェ, 米粉マドレーヌ) are wheat-free by recipe, and even those are baked in the same premises. Also note the GF items contain egg and dairy. Tabelog currently lists the shop's operating status as unconfirmed/on-hold, so phone ahead (075-632-8287) to confirm it is open before visiting.

chef_bio.chef_name: Nobuo Kakine (垣根信夫)
roles: Owner
Head pastry chef (シェフパティシエ)
chef_bio.background: OUBON opened in December 2017 a few minutes' walk from Fushimi Inari station in Fukakusa, Fushimi-ku. Head pastry chef and owner Nobuo Kakine (垣根信夫) is described as a veteran patissier with 40 years of experience in Kyoto, having served as head pâtissier at a well-known hotel and other shops before opening his own. The shop is credited as being run by a pâtissier who helped pioneer Japanese-style (和風) sweets. For its gluten-free line OUBON sources rice flour from Asahi Seifunjo (朝日製粉所) in the Kyoto Tamba/Nantan area.
chef_bio.philosophy: To make rice-flour cakes so close to wheat versions that they are hard to tell apart in a blind test, so that people with wheat allergies can enjoy ordinary-tasting Western sweets alongside everyone else.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour (米粉) gluten-free cakes and baked sweets — signature 豆乳米粉ロール, plus financiers and madeleines — alongside a conventional wheat pâtisserie range.

anecdotes.text: The shop says its rice-flour sponge is so like wheat that even a blind taste test can't reveal the difference: 「小麦を使っているケーキと食感は全く同じで、味もブラインドテストをしてもわからないほど」.
OUBON's gluten-free cakes are made with rice flour supplied by Asahi Seifunjo, a Kyoto Tamba (Nantan) flour mill that profiled the shop and its 40-year-veteran chef.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: オーボンは2017年12月に伏見稲荷近くにオープンした洋菓子店。シェフパティシエの垣根信夫氏は京都で40年の実績を持つベテランで、有名ホテルのチーフパティシエを歴任。通常の小麦のケーキに加え、朝日製粉所の米粉を使ったアレルギー対応・グルテンフリーのケーキを製造。元祖和風スイーツを編み出したパティシエとして紹介されている。

gf_cross_contamination.text: OUBON is a conventional pâtisserie that handles both wheat cakes and rice-flour cakes: 「通常の小麦を使ったケーキや洋菓子、グルテンフリーなケーキやスイーツなどを扱っているお店」. Shared wheat kitchen means airborne-flour and shared-equipment cross-contact risk; not celiac-safe.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Not applicable — this is a dessert/patisserie shop; no savory soy-sauce dishes on offer.

vegan_cross_contact.text: GF items are not vegan by recipe — egg (卵) and dairy (乳) are listed as allergens on the rice-flour products, so vegan cross-contact is moot.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop markets the rice-flour line as 「アレルギー対応の米粉ケーキ」 (allergy-conscious rice-flour cakes) and states allergens for the roll as egg and dairy, indicating some allergen awareness, but no dedicated-line or celiac protocol is claimed.

positives.text: A named, clearly-labeled 米粉/グルテンフリー range (roll, financiers, madeleines, shortcake, lemon cake) with rice flour sourced from Asahi Seifunjo, made by a 40-year-veteran chef — a convenient wheat-free sweet stop right by Fushimi Inari.
