tosaya_muroto.gf_detail: A Tosa (Kōchi) izakaya built on charcoal yakitori and seared bonito (katsuo tataki) — soy sauce, yakitori tare and ponzu (all typically wheat-based) run through the menu, so it is not celiac-safe by default. Some items can be gluten-free if confirmed: sashimi, salt (shio) skewers, and salt-style katsuo tataki without ponzu. But the shared charcoal grill, shared fryer and wheat-containing sauces make cross-contamination likely — order shio, skip the tare/ponzu, and show the celiac card.
tosaya_muroto.vegan_detail: A Tosa seafood-and-yakitori counter: seared bonito, charcoal chicken, and shamo (game-fowl) hot pot. Bonito dashi and fish run through almost everything, so even vegetable dishes likely carry animal-derived stock. A few plain vegetable skewers or pickles may be possible, but confirm dashi/bonito with the chef. Not a vegan destination.
tosaya_muroto.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00. Closed Sunday. (Some listings also note the 2nd & 3rd Monday closed and lunch by reservation only — confirm before visiting.)
tosaya_muroto.notes: [Mom & Pop — a Tosa master, ~50 years at the counter] A tiny Kōchi (Tosa) izakaya on Kiyamachi just south of Sanjo — up on the 2nd floor above an Italian restaurant, with a ~10-seat counter plus one small tatami (6–8). The chef, a Tosa native with roughly half a century behind the grill, cooks yakitori over Tosa binchōtan charcoal and serves Kōchi's signature seared bonito (katsuo tataki), shamo (game-fowl) hot pot, and seasonal Tosa dishes. Reviewers praise thick, odorless bonito and carefully grilled skewers, and a charming old-Kyoto exterior; it draws locals and food-loving visitors alike. Reservations accepted (HotPepper). Address: 河原町通三条下ル大黒町49 (entrance on Kiyamachi-dōri). Instagram @tosayamuroto.

roles: master chef / owner (taishō)
chef_bio.origin: Tosa (Kōchi Prefecture); the shop is in Kiyamachi, Nakagyo Ward, Kyoto
chef_bio.background: A Tosa (Kōchi) native who by most accounts has spent roughly fifty years cooking, running a small counter izakaya devoted to the food of his home region. He grills over Tosa binchōtan (the prized white charcoal of Kōchi) and centers the menu on Kōchi's most famous dish, seared bonito — the kind of veteran, single-counter kitchen where the chef works in front of you and the seasons drive what's served.
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal yakitori over Tosa binchōtan and Kōchi's signature katsuo (bonito) tataki, plus shamo (game-fowl) hot pot and seasonal Tosa dishes.

anecdotes.text: Regulars single out the bonito tataki as thick, generous and completely free of any fishy odor — the hallmark of well-handled katsuo — and note that each yakitori skewer is grilled with real care over binchōtan.

The shop is described as an izakaya serving 'the finest yakitori in Kyoto' by a chef with about 50 years of experience, originally from Tosa in Kōchi Prefecture, with a charming, old-Kyoto exterior that draws both locals and foreign guests.
It sits on Kiyamachi just south of Sanjo, upstairs on the 2nd floor above an Italian restaurant — an easy-to-miss counter that rewards those who seek it out.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Japanese listings (Tabelog 郷土料理/焼き鳥, Retty, hitosara, navikyo, HotPepper) describe 土佐屋室戸 as a small Kōchi (Tosa) izakaya at 河原町通三条下ル大黒町49, entrance on Kiyamachi, on the 2nd floor above an Italian restaurant, with a ~10-seat counter and one small tatami room (6–8). Open Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00, closed Sunday; phone 075-221-3056; reservations accepted. The taishō, a Tosa native, is credited with ~50 years of experience; signatures are binchōtan yakitori, katsuo (bonito) tataki, and shamo hot pot, with seasonal Kōchi fare.

cultural_comfort.note: A small veteran-run counter on Kiyamachi that does see foreign diners and takes online reservations — but it's a Japanese izakaya led by a ~50-year chef, with little to no English. A reservation, a few words of Japanese, and easy counter manners go a long way.

gf_cross_contamination.text: This is a yakitori-and-izakaya counter, not a celiac-safe kitchen. Skewers are grilled over a shared charcoal grill alongside tare-basted (wheat soy sauce) items, and any battered/fried dishes share oil, so cross-contamination with wheat is likely across the menu.

Naturally gluten-free choices may exist if confirmed — sashimi, salt (shio) skewers, and salt-style katsuo tataki without ponzu — but they must be ordered explicitly shio/no-sauce and confirmed with the chef.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Yakitori tare, ponzu for the katsuo tataki, and nabe broths are built on Japanese soy sauce, which typically contains wheat. Assume these sauces contain gluten unless the chef confirms a wheat-free alternative; ordering shio (salt) avoids the tare.

vegan_cross_contact.text: A fish- and meat-forward Tosa izakaya (bonito, chicken, game-fowl hot pot) with bonito dashi throughout — even vegetable dishes likely carry animal-derived stock. There is no documented vegan menu; confirm each item with the chef.

positives.text: A tiny, owner-run counter where the chef cooks directly in front of you, so you can ask about ingredients and preparation face-to-face — easiest with some Japanese or a translation app.

kyr_fukuchian_nijojo_mae.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The chain's own allergen chart lists wheat (小麦) in every ramen, set, side and topping on it — including the chashu, seasoned egg and menma — and the noodles are made in-house from wheat flour. The shop says it cooks with ordinary shared utensils and dishes and leaves cross-contamination to the diner's own judgment. The only food item the chart shows without wheat is the sherbet. Not suitable for celiacs.
kyr_fukuchian_nijojo_mae.vegan_detail: The regular bowls are built on a pork-bone and chicken-frame soup and topped with pork; the allergen chart lists pork and chicken for all of them. The shop does advertise a 'vegetarian ramen' (miso-based broth, house-made noodles), but in its own words it is made with 'almost no' (ほぼ) meat or fish ingredients — so do not assume it is vegan. Ask what the remaining animal ingredients are before ordering.
kyr_fukuchian_nijojo_mae.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–21:00 (last order 20:30). Closed over the New Year.
kyr_fukuchian_nijojo_mae.notes: [Ramen · Fukuchiyama chain] The Kyoto-city branch of ふくちあん, a ramen company from Fukuchiyama in northern Kyoto Prefecture, on the northeast corner of the Horikawa-Oike crossing, across the road from Nijō Castle; it opened in 2022. The house bowl is a pork-bone and Tamba chicken-frame soup simmered for 20+ hours, seasoned with a brewed soy tare aged a year in cedar barrels, over thin house-made noodles, and comes with two kinds of pork, a seasoned egg and green onion. Kara-age is the other draw — the shop advertises a Karaage Grand Prix gold award. You buy a ticket at the machine; an English menu is posted outside and many of the customers are overseas visitors. The shop also advertises a miso-based vegetarian ramen.

roles: ramen company (株式会社新福知庵), Fukuchiyama
chef_bio.origin: Fukuchiyama, northern Kyoto Prefecture — the chain's main shop is by JR Fukuchiyama Station
chef_bio.background: Fukuchian began as a change of trade: in 1996 a Fukuchiyama textile firm turned itself into a ramen business and opened the first ふくちあん. The company has since added branches in Kaibara, Kitaōji (Kyoto), Nijō-jō-mae (2022) and Shiga.
chef_bio.philosophy: The founding-spirit essay on the company site: no textbook, soup after soup poured away, and the temptation to make life easier with ready-made soy tare and stock — refused, because "I don't want to tell a lie" (ウソは嫌なんです).
chef_bio.specialty: Ramen in a pork-bone and Tamba chicken soup with a year-aged brewed soy tare and house-made thin noodles; tender kara-age.

anecdotes.text: Fukuchian started in 1996, when 丸三加工, a Fukuchiyama textile company hit by the industry moving overseas, renamed itself 株式会社福知庵 and became a ramen shop. The Nijō-jō-mae branch opened in 2022.

The soup: Japanese pork leg bones are washed, blanched to remove blood and scum, then simmered in a large pot with Tamba chicken frames, negi and plenty of onion — more than 20 hours in all. It is finished with a brewed soy sauce aged a full year in cedar barrels.
The noodles are made in-house from Nisshin's 特ナンバーワン flour with Inner-Mongolian kansui and 天外天 salt, kneaded, layered, rolled and rested before cutting.
The shop advertises a gold award at the Karaage Grand Prix (からあげグランプリ金賞受賞) for its kara-age.

A June 2026 diner noted the English menu posted outside and the overseas customers inside, ordered the 特濃 (extra-rich) Fukuchian ramen, and praised its slightly sweet pork-bone broth with crunchy bean sprouts and thick chashu.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト(fukuchian.jp)より、株式会社新福知庵(福知山市)。平成8年に繊維業の丸三加工が株式会社福知庵に商号変更しラーメン専門店へ業態変更、ふくちあん本店開店。令和4年 二条城前店開店。二条城前店: 京都市中京区東堀川通御池上る押堀町45-1、TEL 075-212-7620、11:00〜21:00(L.O.20:30)、年中無休(年始を除く)、27席。スープは国産げん骨と丹波産鶏ガラを20時間以上炊く豚骨、元ダレは杉樽で一年熟成の本醸造醤油、自家製麺は日清「特ナンバーワン」。アレルギー表では全ラーメン・サイド・トッピングに小麦。Instagram(2026/10/03)でベジタリアンラーメン(味噌ベース、自家製麺、肉・魚の成分を「ほぼ」使用せず)を告知。

cultural_comfort.note: Order and pay at the ticket machine (electronic money and QR payments accepted, no credit cards). An English menu is posted outside and the shop sees many overseas visitors on their way to or from Nijō Castle; expect a queue on weekends.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The chain's allergen chart lists 小麦 (wheat) for every ramen, set, side dish and topping on it, and the shop states it cooks with ordinary kitchen utensils and ordinarily washed dishes, asking diners to judge cross-contamination risk for themselves.
The noodles are made in-house from wheat flour (Nisshin 特ナンバーワン).

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The base tare (元ダレ) is a brewed soy sauce (本醸造醤油), combined with the pork-bone soup for every shoyu-style bowl.
On the allergen chart even the toppings — トロチャーシュー, バラチャーシュー, 味玉 and メンマ — list 小麦, so a "no noodles" order does not get you to a wheat-free bowl.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The soup is pork leg bone and Tamba chicken frames simmered together for 20+ hours.
The vegetarian ramen has a miso-based broth and is made with 'almost no' (ほぼ) meat or fish ingredients, in the shop's own words — not stated to be vegan.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The chain publishes a per-dish allergen chart (Japanese) that counts allergens shared during processing or cooking as "contained", not only those in the recipe.

kyr_fukuchian_nijojo_mae.pin_source: Tabelog https://tabelog.com/en/kyoto/A2601/A260202/26037359/; cross-checked: OSM node 14253814785 (KAUI, the 3F tenant whose sign is on this building's façade in Tabelog photo Rvw/365127) 2m; GSI town centroid 押堀町 33m; 2026-10-14

kyoto_shiro_karasuma_oike.gf_detail: Ask when booking. There is one chef's-choice course, and Tabelog says the shop does not change it for disliked ingredients; nothing is said about allergies. 2026 courses included pasta (cold Siciliana, maltagliati, chestnut pasta), a baguette with olive oil, a fried anago dish and a financier made with rice flour.
kyoto_shiro_karasuma_oike.vegan_detail: Not vegan: one fixed course built on fish, prosciutto, duck, lamb and beef (2026 reviews), which the shop does not change for dislikes (Tabelog).
kyoto_shiro_karasuma_oike.hours_raw: Wed–Fri dinner 18:00–21:00; Sat–Sun lunch 12:00–14:30 and dinner 18:00–21:00; closed Monday and Tuesday (Tabelog). Every sitting starts at once: lunch at 12:00 (doors 11:45), dinner at 18:00 (doors 17:45) (official site); late arrivals may miss dishes, and the course runs about two hours (Tabelog; an October 2026 diner stayed about two and a half). Reservation only, online (Tabelog). Guests 13 and over only; no strong perfume or very casual clothes (Tabelog). 8 counter seats; whole-shop hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Non-smoking; wheelchair accessible (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX); no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). One drink per person is required (October 2026 review). Opened 14 August 2024 (Tabelog; Leaf Kyoto).
kyoto_shiro_karasuma_oike.notes: [Italian · Karasuma Oike, a Shimane chef's 8-seat counter] Set back from Muromachi-dori, on the second floor of the black-walled IDO KYOTO building with its courtyard, eight seats wrap an open island kitchen in a white room of natural wood. Chef Atsushi Takenaka, from Hamada in Shimane, ran the restaurant Mia Paese there before moving to Kyoto in 2024 to aim higher. The single course, served to everyone at once, starts from Italian cooking and borrows from Japanese and French: Shimane seafood, ayu and rice, Kyoto vegetables and well water from the building's garden. The fried anago wrapped in prosciutto comes from the old restaurant. Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze and Italian WEST 100 (2025); the Michelin Guide's site lists it with a star. Diners in 2026 praise the wine and tea pairings and a friendly chef who explains each dish; some return every season. Guests 13 and over; closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Atsushi Takenaka (竹中 厚志)
roles: Owner-chef (Leaf Kyoto: "says the owner, Mr. Takenaka"; official site)
chef_bio.origin: Born and raised in Hamada, Shimane Prefecture (Leaf Kyoto).
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: entered the culinary world at 24; opened ミアパエーゼ (Mia Paese) in Shimane at 30; selected by Gault&Millau in 2020; supervised food as a "food artisan" for JR West's Twilight Express 瑞風; moved to Kyoto in 2024 and opened shiro. Leaf Kyoto (October 2024) adds that the chef grew interested in cooking while working part-time at a restaurant as a university student, worked in an office after graduating, trained at an Italian restaurant, and closed Mia Paese in Hamada in May 2024 to "aim for a higher rank"; the staff all hail from Hamada. A September 2026 diner calls the chef young and notes seven years of running a restaurant deep in the Shimane mountains; another (April 2026) notes partnerships with Shimane farmers, farms and roasters. Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze; Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025. The Michelin Guide's page shows a star (read November 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: "Shiro" (white) is not just a colour but blank space and purity, "nothing there, yet a sense that something is coming"; five rules: keep harmony, respect nature, make space, stay simple, lead to emotion (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Fried anago with prosciutto; Shimane ingredients in Italian form.

anecdotes.text: "The chef, originally from Shimane, has partnered with local farmers, farms, and roasteries to incorporate an abundance of Shimane ingredients into the menu." — April 2026.
"I didn't have any alcohol, but since there was a one-drink order policy per person, I opted for a homemade ume and cardamom soda." — October 2026.
"This was my fourth visit, and each time the experience gets better." — October 2026, caramelised figs and foie gras with a smoky wine.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (ido-kyoto.com/shiro): 白 (しろ)、IDO KYOTO 2F (1F は IDOCHA と KOKE)、庭の井戸から汲んだ湧き水を使う、コンセプト「しろ」は単なる色ではない、余白、潔白、しろ五則 (調和を保つこと、自然を尊むこと、余白を生むこと、簡素であること、感動を導くこと)、竹中厚志: 24歳で料理の世界に入る、30歳で島根でミアパエーゼOPEN、2020年 Gault&Millau に選出、JR西日本 Twilight Express 瑞風で食の匠として料理監修、2024年に京都へ移転し「しろ」として開店、ランチ12:00スタート (開場11:45)、ディナー18:00スタート (開場17:45)、19,800円 (税・サービス料込)、水・木・金はディナー、土・日はランチとディナー、月・火休み。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze、イタリアン WEST 百名店 2025、おまかせコース21,000円、ワインペアリング付き32,000円、お茶のペアリング付き29,000円、サービス料10%、カウンター8席、13歳以上、2024年8月14日オープン。口コミ(2026年3月〜10月): 穴子のフリットとプロシュート、Shimane と京都の食材、ペアリング、一斉スタート、1人1ドリンク。

cultural_comfort.note: One set course booked online; the chef explains each dish at the counter (2026).

existence.note: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing and official site; reviews dated through October 2026.

kyoto_gokomachi_tagawa.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; the official site asks guests to check dishes and ingredients with the shop. A Japanese course seasoned with soy sauce and miso; 2026 courses included a dried persimmon fried in Domyoji coating, fried sesame tofu with red miso (October) and soba with salmon roe (September).
kyoto_gokomachi_tagawa.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a Japanese omakase course built on dashi, fish, wagyu and duck (2026 reviews).
kyoto_gokomachi_tagawa.hours_raw: Daily from 18:00, one sitting (Tabelog lists 18:00–22:00; official site 18:00–20:30 last entry); closed irregularly (Tabelog; official site); other times can be discussed, and private lunches are taken for groups of five or more (Tabelog). Reservation only, online or by phone between about 11:00 and 17:00 (official site); same-day cancellations are charged 100% (official site; Tabelog). Seats: 10 at the counter (Tabelog) or 12 (official site), a sunken kotatsu-style counter where shoes come off, so wear socks (Tabelog). No strong perfume; bring a light jacket, as the air conditioning varies by seat (Tabelog). Children: ask by phone first (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog; official site). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners; Discover per the official site); no e-money or QR (Tabelog); service charge 10% (Tabelog). Opened 7 February 2017 (Tabelog).
kyoto_gokomachi_tagawa.notes: [Kappo · south of the Kyoto Gyoen, a former engineer's charcoal-hearth counter] A renovated machiya south of the Kyoto Gyoen, behind lattice, earthen walls and a yellow hemp noren, with a hinoki counter where guests sit with their feet in a sunken well and watch everything cooked over binchotan in ceramic hearths. Owner Yoshiaki Tagawa, born in Mie in 1976, left engineering for the kitchen at 25 and opened here in 2017 after training at well-known Japanese restaurants, with the theme of fine Japanese food enjoyed without stiffness. One course a month of about ten dishes: seafood from Mie ama divers, A5 wagyu, and two or three clay-pot rices at the end (one regular keeps lunch light on Tagawa days). Spring brings a flower-pepper hot pot, autumn a Matsutake feast. Tabelog Award Bronze every year from 2018 to 2026; the shop's site says it holds a Michelin star. Diners in 2026 describe a lively, laughing counter and an owner one compared to the actor Masato Sakai.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yoshiaki Tagawa (Tabelog's chef section; an October 2026 review gives "Yoshitaka Tagawa")
roles: Owner and chef (Tabelog: "the welcoming owner"; official site: 店主)
chef_bio.origin: Mie Prefecture, born 1976 (Tabelog); Matsusaka City in Mie, per an October 2026 review.
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in Mie Prefecture in 1976; changed from engineer to chef at 25, drawn by the "one-on-one interactions" between chefs and customers over a counter; trained at Masago Saryo (Yokohama), Gion Maruyama (Kyoto) and Kumura (Azabu-Juban); opened Tagawa in Gokomachi in February 2017. An October 2026 review lists Gion Maruyama and Azabu Yukimura. A March 2024 diner writes that the owner entered the trade "at a much older age than typical chefs, training under younger seniors at a renowned restaurant". The official site says the owner buys the fish, meat and Kyoto vegetables daily and the flowers for the room as well, and that the restaurant has a Michelin star. The ceramic hearth was passed down from the owner's master (Tabelog). Staff: apprentices (October 2026) and a Ms. Tanaka, thanked for warm hospitality in an October 2026 review. Tabelog Award Bronze 2018–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025. The site's news notes a collaboration event in Miami in May 2024.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Casually enjoying exquisite Japanese dishes" (気軽に味わう和の逸品): hospitality that keeps guests from feeling formal, and conversation across a flat counter (official site; Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal grilling in ceramic hearths; clay-pot rices; spring flower-pepper hot pot; autumn Matsutake.

anecdotes.text: "The private reservation event was lively, with the owner resembling Masato Sakai, who is currently starring in a popular drama." — October 2026, Matsutake course.
"On flower pepper days, there are four types of rice dishes, including zosui (rice porridge)." — April 2026, a regular's fourteenth visit.
"This year's fish lacks fat, so instead of slow-roasting it, [the chef] quickly grilled it using both top and bottom charcoal heat." — September 2026, Pacific saury.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (gokoumachi-tagawa.com): 御幸町 田がわ、夷川通御幸町西入松本町575、テーマは「気軽に味わう和の逸品」、硬くならないおもてなし、フラットなカウンター越しに目の前で調理、陶器で作られた炉と備長炭、ミシュランひとつ星を獲得、店主出身地の三重県をはじめ様々な産地の旬の素材、おまかせコースのみで一品料理なし、コースは10品前後で毎月変更、おまかせコース26,400円 (別ページに21,780円の記載も)、お正月特別料理33,000円、花山椒鍋特別コース33,000円 (4月)、松葉蟹の特別コース・蟹の会は参考価格44,000円、仕入れで価格が変動、料理内容・食材は店舗に確認を、完全予約制、電話は11:00〜17:00ごろ、営業時間18:00〜20:30 (最終入店)、不定休、カウンター12席、全席禁煙、当日キャンセル100%、店主が花も仕入れる。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award Bronze 2018〜2026、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025、おまかせコース29,040円、サービス料10%、カウンター10席、足を下ろせるカウンターで靴を脱ぐ、靴下着用、2017年2月7日オープン。口コミ(2026年1月〜10月): Matsutake の会、花山椒の鍋、土鍋ご飯が数種類、Mie の ama の魚介、店主は Masato Sakai に似ているという声、Tanaka さんのもてなし。

cultural_comfort.note: One omakase course booked online; shoes off at a sunken counter. A March 2024 diner noted an American staff member explaining dishes in English.

existence.note: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing and official site; reviews dated through October 2026.

kyoto_gokomachi_tagawa.pin_source: Tabelog https://tabelog.com/en/kyoto/A2601/A260202/26028604/ (35.015015, 135.766391); cross-checked: GSI 京都府京都市中京区松本町575番地 (lot) 64m; 2026-11-01

kyoto_radice_marutamachi.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. The one course has two pasta courses (handmade pasta is a house focus), panzerotti and fried gnocco, bread and a financier (2026 reviews); a diner in September 2026 had a liver sauce left off, so some changes are made.
kyoto_radice_marutamachi.vegan_detail: Ask. No vegan course is listed; the one course includes prosciutto, fish and beef (official menu; 2026 reviews). Every course has a salad course (official menu), in 2026 a dish of 10–11 vegetables.
kyoto_radice_marutamachi.hours_raw: Lunch Fri, Sat, Sun and holidays, one sitting at 12:00; dinner Thu–Mon, one sitting at 18:30; closed Tuesday and Wednesday (official site; Tabelog lists Mon and Thu 18:30–22:00, Fri–Sun and holidays 12:00–15:00 and 18:30–22:00). Tabelog asks guests to arrive on time (lunch from 11:50, dinner from 18:20; there is no waiting area); the course runs about 2.5 hours. **Closed for an autumn break 27 October – 5 November 2026** (official site). Reservations online only (TableCheck or Tabelog), not by phone (official site). 12 seats: 8 at the counter and one table for 4; whole-shop hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Non-smoking, with a smoking space on the balcony (Tabelog). No children under 10; no strong perfume, and no sandals for men (Tabelog). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). Opened 21 December 2013 (Tabelog; the shop marked 12 years in December 2025).
kyoto_radice_marutamachi.notes: [Italian · Marutamachi, a former kaiseki cook's Italian omakase] A renovated Kyoto townhouse near Marutamachi station with an eight-seat counter facing a display of the day's vegetables. Owner-chef Yoshihiko Nemoto, born in Shiga in 1977, cooked Japanese food for about ten years (ぎをん浜作 in Kyoto, then Kitashinchi in Osaka) before going to Italy at 29 and training at Ristorante Magnolia; the shop opened in 2013 and took its present form in 2021. One course for everyone at once, about a dozen plates with two pasta courses, light and playful rather than heavy: an 11-vegetable tart, panzerotti of porcini and lobster, a dan-dan-inspired pistachio capellini. Pairings come from a walk-in cellar of some 600 bottles. Tabelog Award Bronze 2019, 2025 and 2026, Italian WEST 100 (2021, 2023, 2025), and a Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2026 Selected restaurant. Book online only; closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays, and for an autumn break until 5 November 2026.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yoshihiko Nemoto (根本 嘉彦)
roles: Owner-chef (official site: "オーナーシェフ　根本")
chef_bio.origin: Born in Shiga Prefecture in 1977 (official site).
chef_bio.background: Per the official chef page: on the path to becoming a cook from age 15; about ten years of Japanese cooking, at ぎをん浜作 in Kyoto and in Kitashinchi, Osaka; went to Italy at 29 and trained about two years at Ristorante Magnolia ("now two stars"); then chef at 祇園t.v.b and Vineria t.v.b in Kyoto; opened RistoriaRadice as owner-chef in 2013, renewed in 2021 as RADICE. Tabelog adds that the chef trained in Emilia-Romagna. In August 2026 the chef told a diner of about ten years as a Japanese-cuisine cook. The shop's New Year message (January 2026) mentions a year short of staff, a first Christmas cake and sold-out osechi, and a price rise from January 2026. Selected Restaurant in the Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2026 (official site, April 2026). Tabelog Award Bronze 2019, 2025, 2026; Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Authentic Italian food from the best domestic and imported ingredients, without compromise (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Handmade pasta; panzerotti; vegetable tarts and salads.

anecdotes.text: "I had the chance to chat with the chef and learned that [the chef] had spent about 10 years as a Japanese cuisine chef in [a] previous job." — August 2026.

"When I made the reservation, the restaurant called me to inform me that they were offering a special course ... featuring a 'Pasta Festival'." — August 2026; course ¥19,800, bill ¥25,168 with sparkling water and non-alcoholic beer.
"I remembered the last time I came, the restaurant had large glass windows facing the street, but it seems to have been renovated." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (radice-kyoto.com): RADICE〈ラディーチェ〉、鏡屋町50番地、丸太町駅6番出口から徒歩3分、ランチ (金土日祝のみ) 12:00一斉スタート、ディナー (木〜月曜日) 18:30一斉スタート、定休日は火曜・水曜、予約はオンラインのみ、2026年10月27日〜11月5日は秋季休暇、シェフ根本嘉彦: 1977年滋賀県生まれ、15歳から料理人の道へ、京都の「ぎをん浜作」と大阪の北新地で約10年和食、29歳でイタリアへ、Ristorante Magnolia で約2年修行、祇園t.v.b と Vineria t.v.b でシェフ、2013年にオーナーシェフとして RistoriaRadice をオープン、2021年にリニューアルして現在の Radice に。おまかせコース1種類 “Idee e Sapori” 19,800円 (税込、別途サービス料10%)、ランチ・ディナー共通、ペアリングはフル (8種類〜) 9,900円、ハーフ (5種類) 6,600円、約600本のウォークインのワインセラー、ミシュランガイド京都・大阪2026でセレクテッドレストラン、ローストビーフのテイクアウト、御節。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award Bronze 2019・2025・2026、イタリアン WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025、12席 (カウンター8、テーブル1卓4名)、10歳未満不可、ベランダに喫煙スペース、2013年12月21日オープン。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月): 11種類の野菜のタルト、パンツェロッティ、ピスタチオとオマールのカッペリーニ、パスタの会、町家を改装した店内。

cultural_comfort.note: One set course booked online (TableCheck or Tabelog); the chef explains dishes at the counter (September 2026).

existence.note: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing and official site (notices into October 2026; closed for an autumn break 27 October – 5 November 2026); reviews dated through October 2026.

kyoto_motoi_tomikoji.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the official site says allergies and disliked foods are asked when you reserve, since the course is made up for each day. No gluten information. 2026 courses included ciabatta with butter, a pasta-style hamo and Matsutake dish, spring rolls, a macaron and a chiffon-cake dessert; Chinese seasonings such as fermented black beans and fermented tofu sauce appear.
kyoto_motoi_tomikoji.vegan_detail: Ask when booking (allergies and dislikes are taken at reservation, per the official site). Tabelog lists vegetarian options, but no vegetarian or vegan course is posted; the regular courses use fish, foie gras, wagyu, lamb or game, and a fish-dashi soup (2026 reviews). The salad of 50-plus Ohara vegetables is a fixture.
kyoto_motoi_tomikoji.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00–15:00 (enter 12:00–13:00) and dinner 18:00–22:00 (enter 18:00–19:00) on Mon, Tue, Fri, Sat, Sun and holidays; closed Wednesday and Thursday (Tabelog). The official site keeps a calendar of open days. Reservation only (Tabelog), by phone or online (official site); same-day cancellations are charged 100%, the private room from three days before (official site). 32 seats: eight tables for four, plus a special room for 2–8 with its own menu (Tabelog; official site). No children under 13; no shorts, sandals or strong perfume; no noisy filming devices (Tabelog). Non-smoking; wheelchair accessible; free Wi-Fi; English menu and English-speaking staff (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), contactless cards; no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). Opened 31 January 2012 (Tabelog).
kyoto_motoi_tomikoji.notes: [French · Tomikoji-Nijo, a former Chinese-cuisine chef's French in a kimono merchant's house] A Taisho-era kimono merchant's house of about 100 years on Tomikoji-dori, renovated into a high-ceilinged dining room looking onto a courtyard garden. Chef Motoi Maeda, born in Kyoto in 1976, spent about ten years cooking Chinese food at a Kyoto hotel, then trained in Burgundy and at Pittoresque and HAJIME before opening here in 2012. The cooking is French with Chinese accents: a cold mapo tofu of tofu mousse, wagyu meat-miso and chili oil is the dish everyone mentions, alongside a salad of some 50 Ohara vegetables and condiments such as fermented black beans and dried shrimp. The chef forages watercress on the Kamo River and hunts game in Niigata. Courses change each visit, and the shop asks about previous visits when you book. Tabelog Award Bronze every year from 2019 to 2026. 2026 diners loved the room and the surprises; a few found the service thin. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Motoi Maeda (前田 元)
roles: Chef (Tabelog: "Chef Motoi Maeda"; official site: シェフ 前田元)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: as a child read cookbooks like picture books and cooked from them; after high school joined what is now RIHGA Royal Hotel Kyoto and worked about ten years as a Chinese-cuisine chef; moved to France and trained in Burgundy and other regions; after returning worked at Pittoresque in Kyoto and HAJIME in Osaka; opened MOTOI in the chef's hometown of Kyoto in January 2012. Tabelog says the chef judges heat by eye rather than with a thermometer and gathers wild watercress from the Kamo River. In September 2026 the chef came out to greet a lunch table. Tabelog Award Bronze 2019–2026; French WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Shukyaku ittai" (主客一体), a tea-ceremony phrase for host and guest creating the time together; MOTOI values the harmony (和) that guests and staff make together (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Cold mapo tofu; Ohara vegetable salad; French sauces with Chinese seasonings.

anecdotes.text: "The tofu had a mousse-like texture, and inside was Wagyu beef coated in a sauce. The fact that it was served cold was also a nice seasonal touch." — August 2026, first visit.
"When I added the fermented tofu sauce, dried shrimp, salted fish, and fermented black beans, it transformed the dish into something distinctly Chinese." — September 2026, Japanese tea pairing.
"The total with pairings was JPY 47,000." — October 2026, dinner.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (kyoto-motoi.com): Restaurant MOTOÏ、シェフ前田元のフィルターを通した新しいフレンチ、「主客一体のおもてなし」、ランチ Collection de Saison 13,200円 (約10品)、Gourmand 18,700円 (メインが牛肉、前菜にオマール海老)、ディナー Création 25,300円 (約13品)、特別室 (2〜8名) は限定メニューでランチ27,500円、ディナー46,200円、いずれも税込、別途サービス料10%、その日ごとにコースを用意するため予約時に食材のアレルギーや苦手なものを聞く、来店履歴も聞く、当日キャンセル100%、MOTOIの餃子のお店「モトイギョーザ」、通販。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award Bronze 2019〜2026、フレンチ WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025、富小路通二条下ル俵屋町186、大正時代の呉服商の邸宅を改装した一軒家、中庭、32席、個室あり、13歳未満不可、英語メニュー、英語を話せるスタッフ、ベジタリアンメニューあり、2012年1月31日オープン。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月): 冷たい麻婆豆腐、Ohara の50〜55種類の野菜のサラダ、中国料理の調味料、ワインペアリング、日本茶のペアリング、ペアリング込みで47,000円。

cultural_comfort.note: English menu and English-speaking staff (Tabelog); the official site has an English version; set courses booked ahead.

existence.note: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing and official site (notice dated 21 October 2026); reviews dated through October 2026.

kyoto_niku_no_takumi_miyoshi_gion.gf_detail: Ask before booking, and expect little room: Tabelog warns that the shop may not be able to accommodate allergies (or guests who dislike raw or rare meat). The course leans on ponzu, soy-marinated egg yolk and sukiyaki sauce, and 2026 courses included beef fried in batter in beef fat, sushi and thin somen noodles.
kyoto_niku_no_takumi_miyoshi_gion.vegan_detail: Not vegan: an all-beef kaiseki course, with broths of meat, kombu and bonito (2026 reviews).
kyoto_niku_no_takumi_miyoshi_gion.hours_raw: Mon–Sat, two sittings that start together at 17:00 and 20:00; closed Sunday (official site; Tabelog lists 17:00–23:00). Reservation only, by phone 12:00–23:00 except Sunday or online: OMAKASE (Japanese), TABLEALL (English), foodies-reserve.com (Chinese, Korean, Taiwanese) (official site). Late arrivals join the course where it is; more than 30 minutes late cannot be seated; changes to date, time or numbers count as cancellations (Tabelog). 8 counter seats (Tabelog; an August 2026 diner counted 9); whole-shop hire possible (Tabelog). From middle-school age up; no strong perfume (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). Renovated in 2023 (closed January–June 2023 per the official site); the second floor is a one-group inn, THE MIYOSHI, with dinner and stay as a package (Tabelog; official site). Opened at the end of 2004 (official site).
kyoto_niku_no_takumi_miyoshi_gion.notes: [Meat kaiseki · Gion, a self-taught owner's all-wagyu counter] A two-storey wooden house a step off Hanamikoji, reached down a narrow path between textured earthen walls, with eight seats at a hinoki counter (renovated in 2023). Owner Tsutomu Ito came to meat through a friend who graded beef and a first taste of beef butchered that same day, is self-taught as a cook, and opened in the owner's home town of Gion at the end of 2004 under the family name Miyoshi; the building had been the owner's mother's salon. One course a month runs through a dozen beef dishes — tongue cured on kombu, beef sashimi, shabu-shabu, steak and sukiyaki — between seasonal seafood and vegetables, and ends with rice and egg yolk. Tabelog Award 2026 Silver; a 2026 reviewer notes a Michelin star from 2018 to 2022. Upstairs is a one-group inn where diners can eat and then sleep. Expect ¥60,000–75,000 plus service; one July 2026 diner felt regulars got more attention.

chef_bio.chef_name: Tsutomu Ito (伊藤力)
roles: Owner (official site greeting; Waraku: 店主 伊藤力（いとうつとむ）)
CEO of Miyoshi Co., Ltd. (an August 2026 review, which writes the name "Chikara Ito")
chef_bio.origin: Gion, Kyoto (Tabelog: opened in the owner's home town of Gion).
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: an encounter with exceptionally fresh offal drew the owner to meat; the restaurant took the name Miyoshi, used in the family since a great-grandfather; the cooking is self-taught and has won a Michelin star. Per the official greeting: before opening, "the best meat craftsman" served the owner beef butchered that day, and that taste is the shop's starting point; it opened at the end of 2004 in Gion. Waraku web: the owner entered the meat world because a friend was a beef grader; self-taught; the shop opened in 2005 (as Waraku has it) in a building that was originally a salon run by the owner's mother. A May 2026 diner adds that the owner first worked in restaurant service and held a Michelin star from 2018 to 2022. The space was renovated in 2023; the second floor became an inn with its own counter (Tabelog), which the site calls THE MIYOSHI, one group a night. Serai (山本益博) also wrote up the shop, noting the owner talks through the beef at the counter. Tabelog Award 2026 Silver.
chef_bio.philosophy: "I want to create meat dishes nobody has seen yet", searching for new flavours "in conversation with the meat" every day; come hungry (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Kombu-cured beef tongue; beef sashimi; shabu-shabu, steak and sukiyaki in one course.

anecdotes.text: "You can eat until you're full and then sleep right away. Isn't that the best?" — the owner on the upstairs inn (Tabelog).
"This shabu-shabu uses only the center cut of the rib, with the surrounding parts cut away." — May 2026; course ¥70,000 plus 10% service.
"It was nice that they asked if I wanted to add anything without needing to decide in advance." — June 2026, sukiyaki added mid-course.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (niku-miyoshi.com): にくの匠 三芳（みよし）、2004年末に京都・祇園で開業、開業前に最高の肉職人がその日にさばいた牛を食べさせてくれた「最高鮮度」の感動が原点、「今まで誰も見たことのない肉料理を創ってみたい」、日々肉と会話しながら新しい味を探求、お腹を空かせておいでください、旅館「THE MIYOSHI」(一組限定) で三芳でしか味わえない極上和牛懐石、東山区祇園町南側570-15、2部制 17:00/20:00、日曜定休、予約は電話 (12時〜23時、日曜を除く) と OMAKASE・TABLEALL (英語)・foodies-reserve、改装のため2023年1月3日〜6月30日休業。和樂web: 店主の伊藤力（いとうつとむ）さんは友人に肉の格付員がいたことから肉の世界へ、料理は独学、店は2005年開店、もとは伊藤さんの母が営むサロン。サライ.jp (山本益博): カウンター内で調理するご主人の伊藤さんが牛肉の話をしてくれる、上海蟹と牛肉とキャビアのお凌ぎ。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award 2026 Silver、Tajima beef の特別コース60,000円、すき焼き付き75,000円、サービス料10%、カウンター8席、中学生以上。口コミ(2026年5月〜10月): タン刺し、kombu で締めた牛タン、牛トロの刺身、しゃぶしゃぶ、ステーキ、すき焼き、卵黄の醤油漬けとご飯。

cultural_comfort.note: English booking through TABLEALL (official site); one set course at a counter; an October 2026 diner sat beside an overseas guest.

existence.note: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing and official site (holiday calendar for November 2026); reviews dated through October 2026.

kyoto_higashiyama_tsukasa.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the menu cannot be changed on the day (Tabelog). No gluten information. 2026 courses included fresh spring rolls and a fried spring-roll wrapper, corn tempura on rice balls, soba in more than one form and a tantanmen-style dish, alongside soy- and miso-seasoned dishes.
kyoto_higashiyama_tsukasa.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a Japanese omakase course built on dashi, seafood and beef (2026 reviews).
kyoto_higashiyama_tsukasa.hours_raw: Tue–Sat dinner from 18:00 (one start); Sat lunch from 12:30; closed Sunday and Monday, though the shop may open on closing days or serve lunch on other days — ask (Tabelog). Reservation only; no changes to bookings or to the menu on the day; more than 30 minutes late cancels the table (Tabelog). Lunch for one by phone only (Tabelog). 9 counter seats; whole-shop hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). Opened 1 November 2021 (Tabelog).
kyoto_higashiyama_tsukasa.notes: [Kappo · Higashiyama, a ryotei-trained chef's playful counter] A second-floor counter of nine near Higashiyama station, where owner-chef Tsukasa Miyashita, from Mie and trained for sixteen years at Gion Maruyama and Gion Sasaki, cooks Japanese food with turns no one else takes: fried ayu wrapped in fresh spring rolls, a dried-Matsutake soup with a Chinese edge, an autumn "parfait" of tofu sauce and dashi jelly, rice served as sushi, as egg-on-rice and as mapo. Opened in 2021 with Yuumei Hongo, it holds a star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2026 (per 2026 reviews) and Tabelog's 2026 Bronze. Everyone starts at 18:00; the room is lively, and a July 2026 diner was greeted at the door by the chef. Course ¥30,250 plus service; closed Sundays and Mondays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Tsukasa Miyashita
roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog set menu: "our chef and owner, Tsukasa Miyashita")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section (written in the first person): born in 1985 in Mie, interested in cooking from childhood, studied at Tsuji Culinary Institute, then six years at Gion Maruyama and ten at Gion Sasaki; opened Higashiyama Tsukasa in 2021 together with Yuumei Hongo, met during training, drawing on both ryotei and kappo cooking under the idea of "cuisine not served elsewhere". Tabelog's introduction adds experience in innovative and Chinese cooking. Reviewers in 2026 greet "Tsukasa, Hongo, and Hiraku-kun" at the counter (September) and report one Michelin star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto & Osaka 2026 (August, October). Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Cuisine not served elsewhere"; delicious food and enjoyable experiences (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Ayu spring rolls; dried-Matsutake soup; rice in several forms.

anecdotes.text: "The chef personally welcomed us at the entrance, which was a nice touch." — July 2026, date night.
"The staff and customers here seem to have a great camaraderie, making it a fun place to be!" — July 2026.
"I also appreciated that I could enjoy rice in various forms, including sushi, tamago kake gohan (rice with raw egg), and mapo rice." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): ひがしやま 司、日本料理、東山区西町127 三条白川橋ビル 2F、東西線東山駅から徒歩2分、火〜土 18:00一斉スタート、土曜は12:30からランチも、日・月休み (不定、臨時営業あり)、季節のおまかせコース30,250円 (税込)、サービス料10%、カウンター9席、貸切20名まで、当日のメニュー変更不可、2021年11月1日オープン、The Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2025。店主の Tsukasa Miyashita さんは1985年 Mie 生まれ、Tsuji Culinary Institute、Gion Maruyama で6年、Gion Sasaki で10年、2021年に Yuumei Hongo さんと開業、料亭と割烹の経験を生かした「よそにはない料理」。口コミ(2026年7月〜10月): ayu の生春巻き、干し Matsutake のお椀、ウニと turban shell のシャリ粥、焼き warabi mochi、ご飯の食べ方がいろいろ、ミシュランガイド京都・大阪2026で一つ星、店主が入口で出迎える、にぎやかなカウンター。

cultural_comfort.note: One omakase course at a shared start; book through Tabelog; menu changes are not taken on the day.

existence.note: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing; reviews dated through October 2026. No official website found.

kyoto_tsukioka_shorenin.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. The soba in the course is handmade 100% buckwheat from Ryuo (Shiga) buckwheat flour (Tabelog; August 2026), but the course also has tempura and other fried dishes and soy- and miso-seasoned food (2026 reviews).
kyoto_tsukioka_shorenin.vegan_detail: Not vegan: vegetables and wild plants lead, but the course is built on dashi, fish and 50-day aged beef (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_tsukioka_shorenin.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00–15:00 and dinner 18:00–21:00 on Mon, Thu–Sun and holidays; closed Tuesday, Wednesday and the last day of each month (Tabelog). All guests start together; seating begins five minutes before; more than 30 minutes late counts as a same-day cancellation, charged 100% (Tabelog). Reservation only. Seats: 8 at a tatami-topped counter on the first floor, and a second-floor private room with a table for up to 12, reached by stairs only, shoes off (Tabelog). Children from 12, with the adult menu; smart casual (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; a 5% service charge from 1 December (Tabelog). Lunch was fully booked twice for an October 2026 diner. Opened 14 April 2021 (Tabelog).
kyoto_tsukioka_shorenin.notes: [Kappo · Higashiyama, a forager's "museum of food" opposite Shoren-in] Across the lane from the gate of Shoren-in, behind a plaque reading Shun Gyuan and a tea-house approach, eight seats face a tatami-topped counter, an okudo stove and shelves of antique jars. Owner Masanori Tsukioka, from Hokkaido, began cooking at 15 in Sapporo, trained around Japan including under Hisao Nakahigashi at Kusakui Nakahigashi, ran Jimi Kougetsu in Kusatsu, and moved to the United States in 2019 to open a restaurant, but COVID ended the plan and the chef restarted in Kyoto, opening here in 2021. The course follows what the chef picks in Ohara and Miyama: a hassun like a summer meadow, white-miso soups, Akashi conger eel, 50-day aged beef from Sakaeya in Kusatsu, handmade 100% buckwheat soba and stove-cooked rice. Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze and Japanese cuisine WEST 100. Lunch ¥15,000, dinner ¥30,000; closed Tuesdays, Wednesdays and the last day of the month.

chef_bio.chef_name: Masanori Tsukioka
roles: Owner-chef (August 2026 review: "The owner, Masanori Tsukioka"; Tabelog: "the owner personally sources")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section (first person): born in 1976 in Hokkaido; began cooking at 15 at a local-cuisine restaurant in Sapporo; trained in Aichi, Kyoto, Tokyo and Shiga; moved to the United States in 2019 to open a restaurant, gave that up because of COVID and restarted in Kyoto; inspired by the owner of Kusakui Nakahigashi, met during training, to work in dialogue with nature, walking the mountains and fields. An August 2026 review adds that the chef trained under Hisao Nakahigashi at Kusakui Nakahigashi and ran Jimi Kougetsu in Kusatsu, Shiga, before Tsukioka, and gathers vegetables, wild plants and flowers in Ohara, Miyama and Kyoko. The aged beef comes from Sakaeya, a Kusatsu butcher (Tabelog). An October 2026 diner thanks "the head chef and the owner" for warm hospitality; another found the proprietress "very beautiful and elegant". Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "A museum of food": wabi-sabi in a traditional Japanese room, and dishes that express gratitude for nature's blessings (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Foraged Ohara and Miyama vegetables; 50-day aged beef; handmade 100% buckwheat soba; okudo-cooked rice.

anecdotes.text: "The table in front of me is not wooden but tatami-style. Interesting." — August 2026, dinner.
"Lunch was fully booked both times. It seems there were cancellations due to the typhoon, but the seats were still filled." — October 2026, a second visit.
"The sardine rice was enhanced by the rich yolk from the Hirako Chicken farm in Kobayashi City, Miyazaki Prefecture." — September 2026, ¥15,000 lunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 青蓮院門跡前 月おか、日本料理、東山区粟田口三条坊町16-2、東山駅から徒歩5分、月・木〜日・祝 12:00〜15:00、18:00〜21:00、火・水と月末休み、一斉スタート、おまかせコース 昼15,000円・夜30,000円 (税込)、12月1日以降は別途サービス料5%、1階カウンター8席、2階は12名までのテーブルの個室 (階段のみ、靴を脱ぐ)、12歳以上、2021年4月14日オープン、The Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2025。店主の Masanori Tsukioka さんは1976年 Hokkaido 生まれ、15歳から Sapporo で修業、Kusakui Nakahigashi の店主に影響を受け、Ohara と Miyama で野菜や野草を採る、Kusatsu の Sakaeya の50日熟成の牛肉。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月): 八寸から心を掴まれる名店、器や設えまで世界観が作り込まれている (日本語の口コミ)、Ohara の野菜、白味噌の椀、Akashi の穴子、100%のそば、昼は満席。

kyoto_cenci_shogoin.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the official site asks guests to mention allergies and disliked foods when reserving. No gluten information. kyoto_cenci_shogoin.vegan_detail: Ask when booking (allergies and dislikes are taken at reservation, per the official site). Courses in August and October 2026 included a dish made with no animal products, but the rest uses prosciutto, fish, eel, beef or duck (2026 reviews; official sample menu).
kyoto_cenci_shogoin.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00 (last entry) to 15:00 and dinner 18:00–18:30 last entry to 21:30, Wed–Sun; closed Monday, and irregularly on Tuesday and Sunday (official site; Tabelog lists Mon and Tue closed). Reservation only, online or by phone from 10:00, not during service; bookings open two months ahead to the day (official site). 26 seats: 4 at the counter, tables, and one private room for 5–6 (Tabelog; official site). No children under 6; at lunch, children 6–11 in the private room only; dinner from 12 (official site). No sandals or very casual clothes; no strong perfume (Tabelog; official site). Non-smoking; wheelchair accessible; free Wi-Fi (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). Same-day cancellation 100% (official site). Opened 5 December 2014 (Tabelog).
kyoto_cenci_shogoin.notes: [Italian · Shogoin, a Kyoto-born chef's Italian in a century-old house] Near Heian Shrine, down a narrow entrance and stairs that one diner likened to entering a cave, a renovated house of over 100 years with walls of twisted Meiji-style brickwork, Wajima lacquer and Kyoto ceramics on the table. Chef Ken Sakamoto, born in Kyoto in 1975, fell for Italian food on a university trip, trained at Il Papparaldo and spent nine years as head chef of Il Giottone before opening here in 2014. The courses pair Kyoto vegetables with fish and meat in surprising ways — prosciutto with mango and dosa, a hamo soup like tom yum — and the meal ends with cenci, the fried pastry that gives the shop its name; a vegan plate has appeared mid-course. Michelin Guide Kyoto Osaka 2026 one star (per 2026 reviews), Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze. Weekday lunch is ¥12,100; one October 2026 diner found the explanations hurried.

chef_bio.chef_name: Ken Sakamoto
roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog: "Chef Sakamoto"; opened cenci in 2014)
chef_bio.origin: Born and raised in Kyoto, 1975 (Tabelog chef section).
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in Kyoto in 1975, with a mother who was a fine cook and a family that liked eating out; a university trip to Italy led to cooking; three and a half years at Il Papparaldo, then moved to Il Giottone when chef Yasuhiro Sasajima went independent, and was head chef of the main restaurant for nine years; opened cenci in 2014. The house is over 100 years old, with walls in the Meiji-era "nejirimanpo" twisted brickwork, woodwork by Japanese craftsmen, Wajima lacquerware, Kyoto ceramics and Ryusen knives (Tabelog). 2026 reviewers report one Michelin star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto-Osaka 2026 (August). Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze; Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Ingredients first: local produce from Kyoto and around Japan, at their peak or aged to their best, combined in Italian dishes "you won't find anywhere else" (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Kyoto vegetables in Italian courses; handmade pasta; the fried pastry "cenci".

anecdotes.text: "The dessert at the end, called 'Cenci,' is a type of fried pasta snack, which was a delightful palate cleanser in small bites." — September 2026, second visit.
"As I descended the stairs, I felt as if I was entering a cave, revealing a space that was unimaginable from the outside." — August 2026.
"Not only were the dishes delightful, but the tea pairings were also wonderful." — October 2026, dinner course at lunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (cenci-kyoto.com): cenci チェンチ、左京区聖護院円頓美町44-7、ランチ12:00 (L.O.)〜15:00、ディナー18:00〜18:30 (L.O.)〜21:30、毎週月曜日と不定で火曜日・日曜日休み、ランチ21,780円 (8皿とデザート3皿、ディナーと同じ) と12,100円 (6皿とデザート2皿)、ディナー21,780円 (税サ込)、ある日のディナー: ペルシュウ、じゃがいも、柚子胡椒、ガスパチョ、桜海老、花穂紫蘇、トマト、新生姜、太刀魚、パクチー、上賀茂胡瓜、経産牛、胡麻、ニラ、サザエ、キタッラなど、料理に合わせたお茶も、予約は2か月先の同日まで、予約時にアレルギーや苦手な食材を知らせて、小学生未満は不可、ディナーは中学生未満不可、個室は5〜6名、当日キャンセル100%。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award 2026 Bronze、イタリアン WEST 百名店 2025、平日ランチ12,100円、土日祝ランチ16,940円、24,200円 (ディナーと同じ)、サービス料10%、26席、2014年12月5日オープン。口コミ(2026年8月〜10月): 最後の小菓子が cenci、新烏賊のリゾット、動物性のものを使わない一皿、お茶のペアリング、ミシュランガイド京都・大阪2026で一つ星。

kyoto_takeyamachi_mita.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. A set Japanese course seasoned with soy sauce and miso; 2026 courses included fried spring rolls, an asparagus tempura, somen noodles and sushi.
kyoto_takeyamachi_mita.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish-led kaiseki course built on dashi, with soft-shelled turtle and beef in some dishes (2026 reviews).
kyoto_takeyamachi_mita.hours_raw: Tabelog lists daily 16:00–22:00 with irregular closing days and asks guests to check; one dinner sitting a night, which 2026 diners report starting at 16:00 (September, a Saturday) or 18:00 (October) (Tabelog; reviews). Reservation only, online (Tabelog); hard to book, though cancellations open up on reservation sites (2026 reviews; a September 2026 diner booked through OMAKASE). Some autumn nights are private Matsutake gatherings (October 2026). 6 counter seats; whole-shop hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Opened 11 September 2010 (Tabelog).
kyoto_takeyamachi_mita.notes: [Kaiseki · Teramachi-Marutamachi, six seats and one sitting a night] A pure Japanese room of straw-flecked earthen walls and a single slab of keyaki for a counter that seats six, on a quiet street south of the Imperial Palace. Chef Hiroyuki Mita cooks one seasonal course for everyone and explains each dish; diners in 2026 single out the horse-mackerel and mackerel sushi, hamo in white miso, Matsutake spring rolls and the clay-pot rices at the end, all on old and notable tableware. The chef greets guests at the door and sees them off, a woman owner looks after the drinks, and reviewers call the service warm and unstuffy. Tabelog Silver every year from 2019 to 2026 and Japanese cuisine WEST 100. Hard to book; watch reservation sites for cancellations. Expect ¥60,000–79,999.

kyoto_mizai_maruyama.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the official site says the shop confirms portion size and allergies when you reserve. No gluten information; a long tea-kaiseki course with many dishes seasoned with soy sauce and miso.
kyoto_mizai_maruyama.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a tea-kaiseki course of sashimi, fish, meat and hamo, built on dashi (2026 reviews).
kyoto_mizai_maruyama.hours_raw: One sitting a night: doors from about 17:30, everyone starts at 18:00 (arrive by 17:45) and the meal takes about three hours (official site; Tabelog); 2026 diners report anything from under 2.5 hours to near midnight. Closed Wednesday and irregularly (Tabelog). Reservation by phone, up to a year ahead; the phone is hard to reach during service and an hour either side (official site; Tabelog). The shop confirms a week before; cancellation 50% from seven days before, 100% from five days, and no date changes in that period (official site). Smart casual or better, kimono welcome; children from middle-school age (official site). 14 counter seats and a tea room as a private room (Tabelog; official site). Payment basically cash, though cards are accepted (official site; Tabelog lists VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX). Photos of the food are not allowed (2026 reviews). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Opened June 2004; the site marked 22 years in June 2026. Relocated within Maruyama-cho from 620-1 (Tabelog).
kyoto_mizai_maruyama.notes: [Tea kaiseki · Maruyama Park, a Kyoto master's one-sitting counter] At the far end of Maruyama Park, beyond Yasaka Shrine, fourteen guests sit at one counter and start together at 18:00 for about three hours of tea kaiseki. The owner, Hitoshi Ishihara (石原仁司), born in Shimane in 1952, began training at 15 at a famous Osaka restaurant, rose to head chef in Kyoto at 24, and opened Mizai in 2004; a June 2026 reviewer recalls three Michelin stars many times over. The name is a Zen phrase: the way is never finished. The evening opens with the etiquette of a tea meal, then relaxes; it runs through a lavish sashimi course, a grand hassun, a scorched-rice tea porridge and an astonishing fruit course, and ends with matcha the owner whisks. No food photos. ¥65,000 plus tax and service, cash preferred; book by phone up to a year ahead.

chef_bio.chef_name: Hitoshi Ishihara (石原仁司)
roles: Owner (official site: "未在 主人　石原仁司")
chef_bio.background: Per a June 2026 review: born in 1952 in Shimane; joined the Osaka main restaurant of "Kichijo" (the review's spelling) at 15 and trained under its founder, Teiichi Yuki; head chef of its Kyoto restaurant at 24 and executive chef at 38; opened Mizai in Maruyama Park in 2004; the name comes from a Zen phrase meaning training never ends; three Michelin stars "multiple times". The official site's greeting (August 2026) marks 22 years since opening in June 2004, says the way is "still half-travelled", and offers a house eight-spice blend as an anniversary gift. A September 2026 diner first saw the owner on the NHK programme "Professional" about ten years earlier. Reviewers in 2026 describe the owner as strict and dignified at first, explaining tea-meal etiquette, then increasingly friendly; apprentices greet guests and explain dishes. Tabelog Award Silver 2019–2023, Bronze 2024–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "一座建立": a fine shared time through the spirit of tea kaiseki, which also asks guests to show consideration for one another (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Tea kaiseki in the Mizai style; the hassun; the closing fruit; matcha.

anecdotes.text: "Come after skipping breakfast and lunch. This is no joke; it's a technical necessity." — June 2026, a third visit.
"I felt relieved when I was told I could enjoy the dishes in my preferred way starting from the second course." — June 2026; about ¥130,000 per person with wine.
"Ishihara-san initially comes across as dignified, but he becomes increasingly friendly as the meal progresses." — September 2026.

kyoto_hassun_gion.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. An omakase kaiseki seasoned with soy sauce and miso; 2026 courses included sea bream with sea-urchin soy sauce, a Yawata roll, simmered fried tofu and grilled fish with miso.
kyoto_hassun_gion.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a seasonal kaiseki built on dashi, with hamo, eel, duck and other fish (2026 reviews).
kyoto_hassun_gion.hours_raw: Lunch Tue–Sat 12:00–13:00 (last order 13:00); dinner Mon–Sat 18:00–21:00; closed Sunday (Tabelog). Reservations online until the day before (Tabelog); Ikkyu and Tabelog bookings reported (2026 reviews). 18 seats: a 12-seat counter and a sunken-kotatsu private room for 6 (Tabelog). Children welcome; call to book with children (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Founded in 1945 (September 2026 review).
kyoto_hassun_gion.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion, a family kaiseki house since 1945] Through a simple noren and a stone-paved passage in the middle of Gion, a long, polished hinoki counter of twelve and a sunken-kotatsu room at the back. The restaurant was founded in 1945; the chef now is Kanji Kubota, born in Kyoto Prefecture in 1976, who trained in Tokyo and came home to take over from the chef's father, who still appears now and then. The cooking is quiet and seasonal — hamo in summer, Matsutake dobin-mushi in autumn, a hassun on artists' tableware — and lunch is ¥13,200. New guests are called by name, and in September 2026 an apprentice explained dishes in fluent English to overseas diners. Tabelog Bronze or Silver every year since 2019 and Japanese cuisine WEST 100. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Kanji Kubota (Tabelog; a September 2026 review)
roles: Chef and owner, second generation (Tabelog: "the second generation of 'Hassun'"; "only ingredients that both the owner and his father ... agree upon")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1976 in Kyoto Prefecture; trained in Tokyo, then returned to Kyoto; with little wish to be a chef at first, was encouraged by regular customers to take over the restaurant run by the father, and now stands in the kitchen as the second generation; the father and son choose the ingredients together, and the tableware is by contemporary artists the chef collects. Tabelog's English gives the father's name as both "Masaru Kubota" and "Mamoru Kubota"; no kanji is given. A September 2026 diner reports a founding in 1945, the chef aged 51, and the father appearing occasionally. Tabelog Award Bronze 2019 and 2021–2026, Silver 2020; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasoning that brings out the ingredients' own flavour (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal hassun; hamo; Matsutake dobin-mushi.

anecdotes.text: "The Japanese and overseas guests were separated, and the overseas guests were given fluent explanations in English by an apprentice." — September 2026, lunch.
"Even new customers are greeted by name, making it an easy place to enter alone." — September 2026.
"I spent two and a half hours enjoying my meal while chatting with the chef." — October 2026, dinner.

kyoto_suppon_daiichi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free as served: there is one dish, and its broth is turtle, sake, soy sauce and ginger (a July 2026 diner asked); no gluten-free version is mentioned.
kyoto_suppon_daiichi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the only dish is soft-shelled turtle hot pot, then rice porridge with egg.
kyoto_suppon_daiichi.hours_raw: Lunch from 12:00 (last entry 12:30); dinner in two sittings from 17:00 (last entry 17:30) and 19:00 (last entry 19:30); closed Tuesday (may change), a summer break from late July to early August, and over the New Year (Tabelog). Reservation only (Tabelog). 12 seats at tables, and tatami private rooms for 2 to 20 (Tabelog); some meals are served side by side in a private room off a courtyard (July 2026). No children (Tabelog). The dining rooms are non-smoking; smoking is allowed in the entrance area (Tabelog). Parking for 6 cars (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; no service charge, as it is included in the course (Tabelog). A taxi from the centre costs about ¥1,300; Kitano-Hakubaicho Stn (Randen) is about 18 minutes on foot (Tabelog; July 2026 review). The official site is down for maintenance (November 2026).
kyoto_suppon_daiichi.notes: [Suppon · Kamigyo, a 340-year-old turtle house] An Edo-period building on a quiet street near Senbon-dori, with a courtyard and tatami rooms, where one family has served a single dish for about 340 years and eighteen generations, by diners' accounts since the Genroku era. Sword marks said to be left by samurai remain at the entrance (July 2026), and reviewers note that writers such as Yasunari Kawabata and Naoya Shiga were patrons. The course never changes: turtle jelly, the bubbling marunabe of turtle, sake, soy sauce and ginger served twice, then a rich rice porridge with mochi and egg. Fans call it odourless and deeply savoury; one 2026 diner found the repeated pot monotonous, another the pace brisk. ¥26,000 all in; no children; parking for six.

chef_bio.background: A soft-shelled turtle specialist said by 2026 reviewers to be about 340 years old (founded in the Genroku era) and in its eighteenth generation, with the building kept as it was in the Edo period, including sword marks at the entrance said to be from samurai (July and August 2026 reviews). An August 2026 reviewer names Yasunari Kawabata and Naoya Shiga among past patrons and describes the round Kyoto fans given by maiko and geiko that hang in the house. A server portions the hot pot at the table (August, October 2026). Tabelog Award Bronze 2021–2026. No owner is named in a source read.
chef_bio.specialty: Soft-shelled turtle marunabe; turtle rice porridge.

anecdotes.text: "When I asked what was in it, I found out it was just turtle, Japanese sake, soy sauce, and ginger." — July 2026, private room.
"It retains the same appearance since its founding, with even sword marks said to be made by samurai remaining at the entrance." — July 2026.
"The same hot pot dish was served twice in the course, which made me quite tired of eating." — July 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (suppon-daiichi.com): すっぽん 大市、ショッピングサイトは一時停止中 (2026年11月)。食べログ: 大市、すっぽん・日本料理・鍋、上京区六番町364、昼12:00 (最終入店12:30)、夜は17:00 (最終入店17:30) と19:00 (最終入店19:30) の2部、火曜休み、夏季休暇 (7月下旬〜8月上旬) と年末年始、予約のみ、テーブル12席と個室、子ども不可、駐車場6台、サービス料なし (コース料金内に込み)、すっぽん鍋と zosui が中心のコースは昼夜とも1人26,000円 (税込)、追加は1人10,600円から、zosui のおかわりも、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2021〜2026。口コミ(2026年6月〜10月): 約340年、18代、marunabe を2回、zosui、Shigaraki の土鍋とコークスの火 (英語の口コミ)、生姜、Yasunari Kawabata や Naoya Shiga も通った。

cultural_comfort.note: One fixed course, so there is nothing to order but drinks; staff serve the hot pot at the table.

existence.note: Tabelog listing (not shop-maintained) with reviews dated through October 2026; the official site's shop is under maintenance.

kyoto_soujiki_nakahigashi.gf_detail: Ask when booking (by phone, in Japanese, or through the foreign-language booking site). No gluten information. Vegetables and wild plants lead, but the set course includes tempura in spring (official site), and dishes are seasoned with soy sauce and miso.
kyoto_soujiki_nakahigashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the course is plant-led but built on dashi, with charcoal-grilled fish, dried sardines (mezashi) with the rice, and in 2026 also ayu, carp, eel, venison and wagyu (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_soujiki_nakahigashi.hours_raw: Lunch entry 12:00–13:00, dinner entry 18:00–19:00 (official site; Tabelog lists 12:00–14:00 and 18:00–21:00). Closed Monday (holidays included), alternate Tuesdays (ask) and the last day of each month (official site; Tabelog says the last Tuesday of the month). Reservations by phone from 8:00 on the 1st of the month before (the next day if the 1st is a closing day); phone bookings are in Japanese only, and the site links an online booking site for other languages (official site). Hard to book: a September 2026 diner called for 30 minutes. 30 seats: 12 at the counter and two tatami rooms upstairs for 2–6 (Tabelog; official site). Children from upper elementary school; smart casual, no flip-flops or beachwear (Tabelog). Non-smoking; wheelchair accessible (Tabelog). Cash or credit cards (official site); Tabelog also lists transit IC cards. A 22-minute walk from Demachiyanagi Stn, or 3 minutes from the Ginkakuji-michi bus stop (official site).
kyoto_soujiki_nakahigashi.notes: [Kaiseki · Ginkaku-ji, a forager's kitchen of wild plants and stove-cooked rice] At the foot of the approach to Ginkaku-ji, a counter of twelve and two upstairs tatami rooms where the course is whatever Hisao Nakahigashi found that morning in Ohara: shoots, leaves, flowers and seeds, in a hassun laid out like a hillside, soups and plainly grilled dishes. Born in Kyoto Prefecture in 1952 and raised at Miyamasou, the inn in Hanase known for tsumikusa (foraged-plant) cooking, the owner trained there, served as its head chef and opened here in 1997; the rice, cooked in an okudo-san wood stove and served with grilled dried sardines, became the main event after the 1993 rice shortage. The site reports a Michelin Green Star for its sustainable approach. Diners love the chef's jokes at the counter; book by phone from 8:00 on the 1st of the month before. Lunch from ¥12,100, dinner from ¥24,200 all in.

chef_bio.chef_name: Hisao Nakahigashi (中東久雄)
roles: Owner and representative (official site: 代表 中東久雄; Tabelog: "owner of Kusakui Nakahigashi")
chef_bio.origin: Kyoto Prefecture, born 1952; raised at Miyamasou in Hanase (Tabelog).
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1952 in Kyoto Prefecture and raised at Miyamasou, a traditional inn in Hanase known for tsumikusa cooking; after high school trained under its previous head, Kichiji Nakahigashi, the originator of tsumikusa cooking (a September 2026 review gives "Yoshitsugu Nakahigashi"); head chef at Miyamasou, then opened this restaurant in 1997 (a September 2026 review says 1996). In the 1993 rice shortage a clay rice pot from Ichishiro-gama in Hikone led to the house style with plain white rice as the main dish. Every morning the owner goes to Ohara to gather wild plants and seasonal produce (Tabelog; official site). The official site's message from 中東久雄 cites the motto "eat everything that can be eaten" and a Michelin Green Star for its sustainable approach; the site also carries a message from 中東克之, whose role is not stated. In October 2026 one diner visited on a day the head chef was away. Tabelog Award Gold 2020, Silver 2019, 2021–2023 and 2025, Bronze 2024 and 2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025. Tabelog's English spells the name Kusajiki, Kusakui and Sojiki; the shop's own domain is soujiki-nakahigashi.jp.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Eat everything that can be eaten": gratitude for every life the sun and water raise, and no waste, down to radish and carrot peel and roots (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Foraged wild plants from Ohara; the hassun; okudo-san rice with grilled dried sardines.

anecdotes.text: "As always, I was introduced to new ingredients, including a type of 'grass' I had never heard of before." — September 2026; about three visits a year.
"After 30 minutes of continuous calling, I finally got through and secured a lunch slot." — September 2026.
"The rice was cooked in an okudo (traditional stove)! It was glossy and sweet." — October 2026, lunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (soujiki-nakahigashi.jp): 草喰なかひがし、運営会社 有限会社草喰なかひがし、代表 中東久雄、左京区浄土寺石橋町32-3、入店時間12:00〜13:00・18:00〜19:00、定休日は月曜日・隔週火曜日 (要問合せ)・月の最終日、現金・各種クレジット、予約は毎月1日の午前8時から翌月分を電話で (日本語のみ、外国語は予約サイト)、お昼のコース12,100円〜・夜のコース24,200円〜 (税・サ込)、2026年4月1日から昼10,000円〜・夜20,000円〜 (税・サ別)、京都・大原の山々から採集した山菜や野菜、八寸、炭火で焼いた肴、お竃さんご飯とめざし、ご飯のおかわり自由、大将の軽快なトーク、2階の個室、「食べられるものはすべて食べ尽くす」、ミシュラングリーンスター、銀閣寺道バス停から徒歩3分。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award Gold 2020 ほか、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025、30席 (カウンター12、2階に座敷2室)、小学校高学年から、スマートカジュアル。口コミ(2026年9月〜10月): 松茸とすっぽん (日本語の写真説明)、ayu、鹿、karasumi をのせた Matsutake ご飯、めざしと漬物、電話予約がつながりにくい。

cultural_comfort.note: Phone bookings are in Japanese only; the official site links a booking site for other languages. One set course; the chef talks with guests at the counter.

existence.note: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing and official site (notice dated March 2026); reviews dated through October 2026.

kyoto_il_garage_sakaimachi.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the shop asks for allergies in advance and may not manage changes on the day (official site; Tabelog). No gluten information; handmade pasta such as bigoli is a house specialty, and bread and cannoli are part of the course (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_il_garage_sakaimachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: one seasonal course with fish, duck, beef and, in autumn and winter, game; apart from allergies the shop does not change ingredients for dislikes (official site; Tabelog).
kyoto_il_garage_sakaimachi.hours_raw: Lunch from 12:00 on Saturday and Sunday; dinner from 18:00; closed Wednesday and occasionally (Tabelog). The lunch course takes about 2.5 hours and dinner about 3 (Tabelog). Reservation only, by the day before, for just two groups per sitting; five or more take the whole room (Tabelog). 8 seats at two round tables (Tabelog). No children (Tabelog). Up a flight of stairs, no lift (Tabelog). Please keep phones out of the way during the meal (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog; official site). Opened 17 December 2018 (Tabelog).
kyoto_il_garage_sakaimachi.notes: [Italian · Sakaimachi-Sanjo, a couple's two-table dining room above a garage] Up the stairs over a garage on Sakaimachi-dori, two round tables and one sitting at lunch and at dinner, run by Masato and Midori Shirakawa, who met at a Kyoto Italian restaurant, married and spent 2009–2014 cooking and serving in Italy at Locanda San Lorenzo (Belluno), La Torre del Saracino (Naples) and La Madia (Agrigento). Masato cooks; Midori makes the desserts and runs the room and the wine. The course follows the season with Italian regional dishes and a light creative touch: bigoli rolled each morning, sweet-shrimp cannoli, duck, charcoal-grilled beef, game in winter. Tabelog likens it to being invited into the Shirakawas' home. Tabelog Bronze 2025 and 2026, Italian WEST 100. Book by the day before; closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Masato Shirakawa; Midori Shirakawa (official site: "Masato e Midori Shirakawa")
roles: Masato: chef (Tabelog: "Masato handles the cooking")
Midori: desserts and service (Tabelog: "Midori takes care of desserts and service")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: Masato met Midori, who handled service at the Kyoto Italian restaurant where Masato was training; the two married and went to Italy together to learn regional cooking in Veneto, Naples and Sicily, then opened in 2018 after five years in Italy. The official site lists 2009–2014 at Locanda San Lorenzo (one star, Belluno), La Torre del Saracino (two stars, Naples) and La Madia (two stars, Agrigento). The chef was drawn in Italy to modern cooking rooted in tradition (Tabelog). Reviewers in 2026 note the husband cooks every dish and the wife recommends drinks (July). The owners want a relaxed room rather than a tense one (Tabelog). Tabelog Award Bronze 2025, 2026; Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Semplice, ma con un pizzico di fantasia": Italian regional cooking with a pinch of creativity, and the Italy the couple lived in for five years (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Bigoli made each morning; sweet-shrimp cannoli; seasonal Italian courses.

anecdotes.text: "The chef, who is the husband, prepares all the dishes himself, while his wife provides detailed recommendations for drinks in the dining area." — July 2026, lunch.
"True to its name, it's located above a garage." — August 2026, dinner booked two days ahead.
"The lunch course is priced at JPY 13,200 (service charge not included)." — February 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (ilgaragekyoto.com): IL GARAGE -イル ガラージュ-、ガレージの二階、テーブル2卓だけのレストラン、日本の旬の食材を季節を感じるコース仕立てに、イタリア地方料理とひと摘みの創造性、夫婦で5年を過ごしたイタリアを表現したい、Masato e Midori Shirakawa、2009〜2014 Locanda San Lorenzo* (Belluno)、La Torre del Saracino** (Napoli)、La Madia** (Agrigento)、アレルギーは事前に、当日の変更は対応しかねる場合がある、秋冬はジビエ、苦手な食材には基本的に対応できない、サービス料10%、道祐町147 2F。食べログ (店舗会員): The Tabelog Award Bronze 2025・2026、イタリアン WEST 百名店 2023・2025、昼は土日12:00〜、夜18:00〜、水曜と不定休、昼夜2組限定、前日までに予約、8席 (2卓)、子ども不可、エレベーターなし、2018年12月17日オープン。口コミ(2026年1月〜10月): ピオーネの上に牛の生ハム (日本語の写真説明)、夫が料理、妻がサービスとデザート、ランチ13,200円 (サービス料別)。

cultural_comfort.note: One set course; book by the day before; plate messages can be written in Italian (Tabelog).

existence.note: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing and official site; reviews dated through October 2026.

kyoto_el_tesoro_gion.gf_detail: Ask. A cocktail and whisky bar; spirits and fresh-fruit cocktails are the likelier choices. The home-made cakes (Basque cheesecake, chocolate and cinnamon cakes) are not described either way.
kyoto_el_tesoro_gion.vegan_detail: Ask. Fresh-fruit cocktails and spirits may suit; cheesecake and other cakes likely contain dairy and egg.
kyoto_el_tesoro_gion.hours_raw: 16:00–1:00 (last entry 0:00, last order 0:30); closing days irregular, posted monthly — in November 2026 the 1st, 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th (official site); Tabelog lists Wednesdays closed. Reservations for 16:00–18:00, and after 18:00 up to 30 minutes before arriving; seats are limited, so call ahead (official site). Table charge ¥1,000 per person (Tabelog). A designated smoking bar (喫煙目的店, official site). 12 seats: 8 at the counter, a table for 4 that can be a private room (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and QR payments; no e-money (Tabelog). Opened 22 November 2006 (Tabelog).
kyoto_el_tesoro_gion.notes: [Bar · Gion-Shinbashi, fruit cocktails and cake in a smoking bar] A polished counter of eight and soft jazz on the ground floor of the Yamato Building, a few minutes from Gion-Shijo station. The name is Spanish for treasure. The master, who a July 2026 reviewer says holds sommelier, sake and cheese qualifications, builds cocktails around whatever fruit is in season and will make one to your taste; diners pair them with home-made cakes or a vintage whisky. Diners in 2026 call the master kind and easy to talk to, which makes it a good first authentic bar. It is a designated smoking bar. One August 2026 diner heard that the bar does not take inbound tourists. ¥1,000 table charge; open to 1:00, irregular closing days posted monthly.

roles: Owner-bartender (unnamed; "the master" in 2026 reviews)
chef_bio.background: Opened 22 November 2006 (Tabelog). The name means "treasure" in Spanish (official site). A July 2026 reviewer writes that the owner holds sommelier, sake diploma and cheese professional qualifications and is known for fruit cocktails; an August 2026 diner noticed the bar's care with fresh fruit (a fruit and vegetable wash, a food-preservation spray behind the counter). Diners in 2026 describe the master as kind, modest and good at suggesting drinks. Selected for Tabelog Bar "Tabelog 100" 2022.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Colour in everyday life; one glass of magic to take you out of it" — a place to drink casually, alone or with someone dear (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal fresh-fruit cocktails; home-made cakes.

anecdotes.text: "I heard that they do not accept inbound tourists, which is quite rare in the Gion area where many tourists gather." — August 2026, a coffee cocktail with dessert.
"The combination of sweets and vintage whiskey is simply unbeatable." — October 2026.
"My companion had a watermelon cocktail, which was presented in a snow style." — August 2026, with cinnamon cake.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (eltesoro.jp): El tesoro (エル・テソロ)、京都祇園の BAR、エル・テソロはスペイン語で「宝物」、日常に彩りを、一杯の魔法で非日常へ、16:00〜翌1:00 (最終入店0:00、ラストオーダー0:30)、予約可能時間16:00〜18:00 (18:00以降は来店の30分前まで)、喫煙目的店、席に限りがあるので来店前に電話を、不定休 (11月の店休日は1、4、11、18、25日)、オリジナルのカクテルも含めて希望を伝えて、東山区大和大路通三条下ル三丁目弁財天町19番地 大和ビル一階 E号室、祇園四条駅から徒歩4分、三条駅から徒歩5分。食べログ: バー 百名店 2022、チャージ1,000円、12席 (カウンター8、テーブル4)、カード・QR可、2006年11月22日オープン。口コミ(2026年7月〜10月): 季節のフルーツのカクテル、手作りのケーキ、ウイスキー、マスターが親切、インバウンドの客は受けていないと聞いたという人も。

cultural_comfort.note: Order by telling the bartender what you like; an August 2026 diner heard the bar does not take inbound tourists, so call ahead.
