kyoto_yamamoto_menzou_okazaki.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat udon is the whole menu, and the signature toppings are tempura (burdock, chicken, vegetables).
kyoto_yamamoto_menzou_okazaki.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the broth is a natural dashi made with bonito (official site), and most bowls carry beef, pork, chicken or egg.
kyoto_yamamoto_menzou_okazaki.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Fri 10:00–16:00 (last order); Wed 10:00–15:30 (last order); Sat, Sun and holidays 10:00–17:00 (last order); closed Thursday and irregularly, posted monthly on Instagram; closes early when the noodles run out (official site; Tabelog lists 11:00 opening and the 4th Wednesday closed). Reservations: by phone on the day from 9:00 (to 11:00) for the 11:00–13:45 slots; online through TableCheck from midnight three days ahead for 9:45–10:45 and 14:00–16:30 (to 17:00 at weekends), with a credit card for the cancellation policy (official site). At your time you queue outside, order, and are seated as seats free (official site); expect 20–30 minutes (Tabelog). Cash only in the shop (official site). 18 seats: 10 at the counter, two tables for 4 (official site). Children welcome, with kids' bowls and forks (Tabelog). Three parking spaces (Tabelog). Takeout from a separate counter (official site; October 2026). Prices rose on 9 October 2026 (shop blog). Opened 27 August 2006 (Tabelog).
kyoto_yamamoto_menzou_okazaki.notes: [Udon · Okazaki, the queue-famous udon near the zoo] A small udon house in Okazaki, on land where the founder's grandmother ran an udon shop some fifty years earlier. The noodles are freshly cut and boiled, long, glossy and seriously chewy, in a dashi taken from bonito; the burdock tempura is the order everyone mentions, with chicken-tenderloin tempura close behind, and there is a spicy curry udon and cold tsukemen. Once known for long lines, it now runs on reservations: phone on the day from 9:00 or book online three days ahead, then queue briefly at your slot. Diners in 2026 single out the warm, attentive service from the owner and staff. Cash only; closed Thursdays.

roles: Run by 株式会社山元麺蔵; the person responsible named on the company page is 山元克之 (official site); reviewers mention "the owner" and "the manager" greeting tables (October–November 2026)
chef_bio.background: The founder's message on the official site (first person, unsigned) says the idea came when the company club team the founder belonged to stopped its activities; the founder's grandmother had run an udon shop on this land about fifty years earlier and raised seven children from it; the shop aims at freshly made udon, natural bonito dashi, good rice, fresh ingredients and smiles. The company page names 山元克之 as the person responsible (no romaji given). Opened 27 August 2006 (Tabelog). The shop blog (8 October 2026) announced a price rise from 9 October, citing oil, burdock, radish, chicken, bonito, packaging and wages. Tabelog Udon "Tabelog 100" 2017–2019 and Udon WEST 2020, 2022, 2024.
chef_bio.philosophy: Freshly made udon, natural bonito dashi, warm rice, fresh ingredients, and smiles, greetings and thanks in the room — the things that make a meal like home (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Burdock tempura udon; chicken-tenderloin tempura; Kyoto curry udon.

anecdotes.text: "While waiting in line, they kindly offered me an umbrella to shield me from the heat and served me tea." — November 2026, a second visit.
"The udon noodles were incredibly long, and they provided a cutter for them." — October 2026, cold beef-and-burdock tsukemen.
"The clientele was mostly foreign tourists, particularly from Korea." — October 2026, curry udon.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (yamamotomenzou.com): 山元麺蔵、月・火・金 10:00〜16:00 (L.O.)、水 10:00〜15:30 (L.O.)、土・日・祝 10:00〜17:00 (L.O.)、木曜定休と不定休 (インスタグラムで毎月告知)、麺がなくなり次第終了、電話予約は当日朝9:00〜11:00 (11時〜13時45分の枠)、オンラインは3日前の午前0時から (午前9時45分〜10時45分、午後14時〜16時30分、土日祝17時)、予約時にクレジットカード必須、店でのお会計は現金のみ、予約の時間に店の前に並んで注文、席が空き次第案内、カウンター10席と4人掛けテーブル2卓、岡崎南御所町34、運営は株式会社山元麺蔵 (責任者 山元克之)、お品書き: 赤い麺蔵スペシャル、牛と土ゴボウのおうどん、京カレーうどん、鶏ささみ天うどん、土ゴボウ天うどん、香味油のうどん、つけ麺、ざるうどん、杏仁豆腐など、「想い」: ばあちゃんがうどん屋を営んでいた土地、打ちたて茹でたてのうどん、鰹でしっかりとった天然だし。店のブログ (2026年10月8日): 10月9日から価格改定。食べログ: うどん 百名店 2017〜2019、うどん WEST 百名店 2020・2022・2024、子ども可、駐車場3台、2006年8月27日オープン。口コミ(2026年10月〜11月): ゴボウ天、鶏ささみ天、長い麺にハサミ、杏仁豆腐のサービス、温かい接客、海外の客も多い。

cultural_comfort.note: The official menu has English, Korean and Chinese versions; many overseas diners (October 2026); reservations by phone or TableCheck.

kyoto_sottaku_tsukamoto_gion.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion, one of Kyoto's hardest seats] Eight seats at an L-shaped counter on Nishi-hanamikoji, under a framed “Sottaku Dōji”. Chef Tsukamoto cooks quiet, exact Japanese food — figs with sesame, hamo grilled over charcoal, pressed mackerel sushi, a Matsutake and hamo soup — that diners praise for its sauces and dressings rather than show. No photos, no menu talk, cash only. The shop moved here from Pontocho in 2008; one 2025 reviewer lists two Michelin stars from 2011 to 2016. Tabelog Gold 2024–2026. It is not taking new reservations, so the only way in is with a regular.

kyoto_yamaguchi_gion.notes: [Italian · Gion, a referral-only Japanese-Italian counter] A Gion townhouse redone for its 15th year in April 2026 — grey walls, a curved copper ceiling, an L-shaped counter of ten — where chef Yamaguchi, a soba-kaiseki cook turned Italian chef, serves an omakase heavy with luxury: fig and foie gras brûlée, sea urchin, Ezo abalone on Matsutake risotto, beef fillet, and a signature chilled capellini with sweet shrimp under as much bottarga as you can face. Diners in 2026 describe a cheerful chef, jokes with regulars and a brisk pace (one course came in about 90 minutes). First visits need a referral. Tabelog Gold 2020 and Silver every other year since 2019. From ¥46,000 plus service; closed Sundays, Mondays and holidays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yamaguchi (Tabelog: "Tadashi Yamaguchi"; three October 2026 reviews: "Masashi Yamaguchi"; no kanji in a source)
roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog: opened Yamaguchi "in 2011 as the owner-chef")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1975 in Gifu; entered cooking at 18; trained at the soba restaurant "Kihōshi" in Tokyo (an October 2026 review calls it the soba-kaiseki restaurant "Yoshihoshi"), then turned to Italian at Canoviano in Daikanyama, was a founding member of Canoviano Kyoto, and worked at Ristorante t.v.b in Gion before opening Yamaguchi in 2011. The interior was renewed in April 2026 for the 15th anniversary (Tabelog). An October 2026 review adds a sister restaurant, "Kyoto Amanohashidate Hoshiumi", in Amanohashidate from 2024. Reviewers in 2026 describe the chef as cheerful and funny. Tabelog Award Gold 2020, Silver 2019 and 2021–2026; Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: A "complete referral" style to keep trust with guests; serve the ingredients guests want to eat at that moment (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Chilled capellini with sweet shrimp and bottarga; abalone with Matsutake risotto.

anecdotes.text: "One unique feature of this restaurant is that it starts with dessert-like items." — October 2026, a third visit.
"The pace of service is quite fast, with all dishes served within about 90 minutes." — October 2026, first visit with a regular.
"Chef Yamaguchi brings a lively spirit to the dining experience, often injecting humor into his service." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): やまぐち、イタリアン・イノベーティブ、東山区祇園町南側570-185、火〜土と祝前日・祝後日、カウンターは17:00〜19:00と19:30〜21:30の2部、日・月・祝休み、初めての客は紹介制、1人46,000円〜 (税込、サービス料10%別)、10席、2026年4月に15周年で改装 (個室をなくしてカウンターを10席に、入口はフラットで靴のまま)、子どもは相談、カード可、2011年開業、The Tabelog Award Gold 2020・Silver、イタリアン WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025。シェフは1975年 Gifu 生まれ、18歳で料理の道へ、東京のそば店で修業後イタリアンへ、Canoviano、Ristorante t.v.b を経て独立。口コミ (2026年9〜10月、英語): いちじくとフォアグラのブリュレ、甘海老の冷製カッペリーニとボッタルガ、Ezo の鮑のステーキと Matsutake のリゾット、乳製品を使わない蟹のカルボナーラ、栗のかき氷、明るく冗談の多いシェフ。

kyoto_guu_kiyamachi_nijo.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; the course is Chinese with dim sum (xiao long bao, shumai, a pastry swan), noodles and Shaoxing-wine and soy-based seasonings (2026 reviews).
kyoto_guu_kiyamachi_nijo.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a Chinese course of seafood, Peking duck, beef and pork (2026 reviews).
kyoto_guu_kiyamachi_nijo.hours_raw: Dinner starts at 18:00; lunch from 12:00 for private bookings only; closed Sunday, Monday and irregularly (Tabelog). Reservation only and booked years ahead — 2026 diners were told the next openings are in 2030; for new guests, leftover seats for the following month go first-come by Instagram DM from midnight on the 1st (Tabelog). Same course and price at lunch and dinner (Tabelog). 6 counter seats; whole-shop hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). About 5 min from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Stn; next to the Kiyamachi-Nijo police box (Tabelog; September 2026 review). Opened 17 September 2022 (Tabelog).
kyoto_guu_kiyamachi_nijo.notes: [Chinese · Kiyamachi-Nijo, six seats in front of the wok] A Kyoto townhouse beside the Kiyamachi-Nijo police box where six diners watch owner-chef Kaname Miyatani (宮谷要) cook at fierce flame and over clouds of steam, the energy of a Hong Kong kitchen that won the chef over as a teenager. The course changes monthly: a swan of potato pastry around daikon, apple and blue cheese, dim sum steamed to order, Peking duck in two courses, shark fin, and fried rice from the hottest burner in Japan, as one reviewer put it, if you add it. Diners find it light and never greasy. Seats are booked to about 2030; newcomers can try for leftover seats by Instagram DM on the 1st of each month. Tabelog Silver 2026.

chef_bio.chef_name: Kaname Miyatani (宮谷要)
roles: Owner-chef (official site: "Guuオーナーシェフ　宮谷　要")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1982 in Shiga; won over by authentic Chinese cooking on a training trip to Guangzhou at 21; returned to China at 26 for a year of training; worked in Shiga and Tokyo while preparing to go independent; founded the company Guu (catering and mail order) in 2020; in 2021 went to Russia as personal chef to Yusaku Maezawa's space-travel team, and still travels abroad as a personal chef. The official site's greeting says the chef first stepped into a Hong Kong kitchen as a teenager and was captivated by the cooks' energy, the dim sum, the steam and the roar of the flames. Tabelog Award Bronze 2025, Silver 2026; Chinese WEST "Tabelog 100" 2024, 2026.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Overwhelming dynamism": to cook in front of guests in a space like the Hong Kong kitchen that first captivated the chef, sharing the excitement (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: The swan pastry; dim sum steamed to order; Peking duck.

anecdotes.text: "I finally got to visit after making a reservation two years ago." — September 2026.
"I hear the next reservation is in 2030, but I definitely want to come back to this place!" — September 2026.
"The fierce flames and rising steam right in front of me felt like a form of entertainment." — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (guu-kyoto.main.jp): 中国菜 Guu、圧倒的な躍動感、香港の厨房に10代で初めて足を踏み入れたときに魅了された、料理人の熱量、点心の技術、噴き上がる蒸気、強烈な炎の音、店内はカウンター6席のみ、お客様の目の前で料理を創り上げる、Guu オーナーシェフ 宮谷要、店の情報は主に Instagram で、紹介制の通販 (dim sum Guu)。食べログ: 中国料理、中京区樋之口467-2、ディナー18:00スタート、ランチ12:00は貸切のみ、日・月と不定休、予約のみ、新規の客は毎月1日の0時から翌月の空席を Instagram の DM で先着順、カウンター6席、カード可、2022年9月17日オープン、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2025・Silver 2026、中国料理 WEST 百名店 2024・2026。口コミ (2026年6月、日本語): 木屋町二条近く、6席のカウンター、JAZZ が流れる、目の前で一皿ずつ仕上げるライヴ感、油っこさを感じさせない繊細な味付け、季節のお野菜と海鮮のオードブル (賀茂茄子、帆立、鮑のジュレ)、本鮪の中トロの紹興酒漬けと特級クラゲ、スペシャリティのパイ (大根、ブルーチーズ、リンゴ、ジャガイモのペースト)。

cultural_comfort.note: Booked years ahead; leftover seats go by Instagram DM on the 1st of each month; one set course at a six-seat counter.

kyoto_kiu_shijo_karasuma.gf_detail: Ask through whoever books (the shop works mainly by referral). No gluten information; nigiri and small dishes with soy and other seasonings, and a Matsutake tempura coated in crushed rice crackers in autumn (2026 reviews).
kyoto_kiu_shijo_karasuma.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a sushi omakase of fish and shellfish (2026 reviews).
kyoto_kiu_shijo_karasuma.hours_raw: Two sittings, from 17:00 and from 20:15, each booked as a private party of 5–6; Tabelog lists 17:00–22:30 every day with irregular closures; a November 2026 diner came for lunch (Tabelog; reviews). kyoto_kiu_shijo_karasuma.notes: [Sushi · Shijo-Karasuma, five seats of creative sushi] Up a flight of stairs near Shijo-Karasuma, five seats and two sittings a night, each booked whole by one party. The nigiri sits on soft rice seasoned with white balsamic vinegar, a light touch that diners say lets fish like Lake Biwa trout, sayori and nodoguro shine, after small dishes such as Matsutake fried in crushed rice crackers or hairy crab with sea urchin. The chef's big, warm personality keeps the room loud with laughter, and visiting chefs come to eat. Mostly by referral; Tabelog opens a few new slots a year. Tabelog Silver 2026. Expect ¥40,000–59,999.

kyoto_iida_anekoji.gf_detail: Ask through whoever books (seats go mainly to regulars and their guests). No gluten information; a kaiseki course seasoned with soy sauce and miso, with sushi and noodles in some months (2026 reviews).
kyoto_iida_anekoji.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a kaiseki course built on dashi, with eel, carp, bonito, sea bream, ayu and hamo (2026 reviews).
kyoto_iida_anekoji.hours_raw: Daily from 18:00 (Tabelog lists 18:00–20:00), reservation only, closing days irregular (Tabelog); a September 2026 dinner took about 2.5 hours. Seats go mostly to regulars and referrals; several 2026 diners came as guests of regulars, one booked a year ahead (2026 reviews). 10 seats: a counter of about 5–6 and a 4.5-mat tatami room for 4 (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Shoes off at the entrance (May, September 2026). No photos of the dishes; photos of the vessels allowed on one October 2026 visit; posting on social media not permitted (2026 reviews). Cash only (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). About 7 min from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Stn, 10 min from Karasuma Stn (Tabelog; reviews). Opened 2010 (May 2026 review).
kyoto_iida_anekoji.notes: [Kaiseki · Anekoji, tea-kaiseki cooking on Rosanjin ware] A Sukiya-style house from the early Showa era, once a tea-utensil shop, left almost as it was: a broad entrance, a small inner garden, a counter of five or six and a four-and-a-half-mat room down the corridor. Chef Shinichi Iida, who trained in Kanazawa and Kyoto, has haunted antique shops since apprentice days, and the course comes on pieces by Rosanjin and Eiraku alongside Taisho glass. The cooking keeps to the shape of tea kaiseki — eel Yawata-maki in May, a hamo and ume soup in June, Matsutake in autumn — and reviewers call the clear soups the measure of the place. No photos of the food, cash only, and nearly every seat goes to regulars and their guests. Tabelog Gold every year from 2019 to 2026.

chef_bio.chef_name: Shinichi Iida (Tabelog; a May 2026 review)
roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog: "The chef, Shinichi Iida"; 2026 reviews: "the owner")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: trained in Kanazawa and Kyoto; built the cooking on tea kaiseki; since training days has visited antique shops whenever possible, valuing the "harmony between food and tableware"; uses works by Rosanjin and Eiraku, Taisho-era glass and contemporary pieces; fell in love with an early-Showa Sukiya-style house that was a tea-utensil shop and left it nearly untouched apart from the counter and kitchen. A May 2026 reviewer gives 2010 as the opening year and says the chef opened it. Reviewers in 2026 describe the owner as warm and engaging, explaining dishes in the private room. Tabelog Award Gold 2019–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Harmony between food and vessel; a chance to touch the depth of Japanese culture through a meal (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Tea-kaiseki courses on Rosanjin and Eiraku ware; clear soups.

anecdotes.text: "This is the only month when I can enjoy the eel Yawata-maki from the May menu!" — May 2026, a ninth visit.
"On this day, the hamo (pike eel) and ume (plum) soup was exceptional. I feel that the quality of a Japanese restaurant can be best judged by its clear soup." — June 2026.
"While I couldn't take photos of the food, I was allowed to photograph the beautiful vessels, including a teacup made by Rosanjin." — October 2026.

kyoto_kiyama_gosho.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; a kaiseki course built on bonito dashi and seasoned with soy sauce and miso, with tempura, sushi and a clam-dashi ramen among the closing dishes in 2026.
kyoto_kiyama_gosho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the course centres on dashi from freshly shaved bonito, with fish, shellfish and beef (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_kiyama_gosho.hours_raw: Daily lunch 12:00–15:00 (last entry 13:00) and dinner 18:00–22:00 (last entry 19:30); closing days irregular (Tabelog). The head chef is away on some days, listed on Tabelog — in 2026: 26–28 September, 17, 18, 30, 31 October and 1 November. Reservation only; no bookings through third parties; no seat requests; stairs may be involved; no strong fragrances (Tabelog). 30 seats: a counter of 9 and private rooms, on two floors (Tabelog; October 2026 review). Smart casual, no T-shirts, shorts or sandals (Tabelog). Children and babies welcome; children eat at the counter only on the adult course, otherwise in a private room with à la carte dishes by arrangement (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). About 5 min from Marutamachi Stn (Tabelog). Opened 25 April 2017 (Tabelog).
kyoto_kiyama_gosho.notes: [Kaiseki · Gosho-nishi, a former Wakuden head chef's dashi theatre] Natural wood, a counter of nine and private rooms near the west side of the Imperial Palace, in the building where the chef struck good well water while opening in 2017. The course starts with a cup of that water, then the chef shaves bonito in front of you, lets you taste two kinds of flakes and pours the first dashi — a ritual 2026 diners call the heart of the meal, not a show. Yoshiro Kiyama, from Gifu, spent 15 years at Wakuden, ten as head chef of Kyoto Wakuden and Murasakino Wakuden; Kiyama won a Michelin star a year after opening. The finish is a spread of five rice and noodle dishes you can size and repeat. Tabelog Silver almost every year since 2019 (Gold 2021). Lunch from about ¥19,000; the chef is away on some listed days.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yoshiro Kiyama (Tabelog; 2026 reviews also give "Yoshio" and "Yoshihiro"; no kanji in a source)
roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog chef section; August 2026 review: "The owner, Yoshio Kiyama")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1981 in Gifu; after high school went into cooking; joined Wakuden at 19 and trained there 15 years, ten of them as head chef at Kyoto Wakuden and Murasakino Wakuden Hishitate; opened Kiyama in April 2017 and won a Michelin star in 2018. A September 2026 reviewer says a well-digger found a good water vein when the shop was being built. An August 2026 reviewer cites a star in the Michelin Guide Kyoto-Osaka 2026; an October 2026 reviewer mentions a ryotei the team has opened in Beppu. Tabelog Award Silver 2019–2020 and 2022–2026, Gold 2021; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Highlight the deliciousness of water from start to finish" (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Well-water kaiseki; bonito shaved at the counter; the first dashi; a choice of closing rice dishes.

anecdotes.text: "The chef shaves bonito flakes right in front of the customers, and tasting the freshly shaved flakes and the first dashi is not just a performance; it enhances the entire course." — October 2026, second visit.
"Every summer, I come to Kiyama for lunch, mainly for the watermelon." — August 2026; lunch ¥18,870.
"For the finale, there are five different dishes, and you can adjust the portion sizes in advance, with the option to order more." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 木山、日本料理、中京区絹屋町136 ヴェルドール御所 1F、丸太町駅から徒歩5分、昼12:00〜13:00 (最終入店)、夜18:00〜19:30 (最終入店)、不定休、大将不在の日あり、第三者による予約は不可、席の指定不可、香水は控えて、30席 (カウンター9と個室)、スマートカジュアル、子ども・赤ちゃん可でお子様メニューあり、カード可、サービス料10%、2017年4月25日オープン、The Tabelog Award Gold 2021・Silver、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025。シェフは1981年 Gifu 生まれ、19歳で Wakuden に入り15年、うち10年は料理長、2017年に独立、2018年にミシュランの星。口コミ (2026年8〜10月、英語): 井戸水を沸かした湯から始まる、目の前で削る katsuobushi と一番出汁、締めのご飯が5種類、Matsutake、夏の昼のスイカ、Beppu に料亭。

kyoto_gion_sasaki.gf_detail: Ask when booking by phone. No gluten information; the course includes sushi, somen noodles, sesame tofu and tempura (a corn tempura as dessert in July 2026), seasoned with soy sauce and dashi.
kyoto_gion_sasaki.vegan_detail: Not vegan: Tabelog states the shop cannot accommodate vegan menu requests; the course uses fish, shellfish and shark fin.
kyoto_gion_sasaki.hours_raw: Lunch Thu, Fri, Sat, one start at 12:00; dinner Tue–Sat, one start at 18:30; closed Sunday, Monday and irregularly (official site; Tabelog). More than 30 minutes late counts as a cancellation (Tabelog). Reservations by phone only, from the first business day of each month for dates up to the end of the month after next; the site gives call hours of 10:00–12:00 and 14:00 (or 16:30)–18:30 (official site). 20 seats: a main counter of 13 and a private counter of 7 (Tabelog). Shoes off at the entrance; smart casual, no sandals or shorts for men (Tabelog). No children under 10 (Tabelog). Non-smoking, with a smoking area outside (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR; service included at lunch, 10% at dinner (Tabelog). About 10–15 min from Gion-Shijo Stn, 3 min from the Kiyomizu-michi bus stop (Tabelog; official site).
kyoto_gion_sasaki.notes: [Kaiseki · Yasaka-dori, a showman's Kyoto kaiseki] Up steps on Yasaka-dori south of Kennin-ji, past guardian figures at the door, thirteen guests at a counter with a big charcoal grill in the middle watch a crew of apprentices and chef Hiroshi Sasaki work, and everyone starts together. The chef buys at markets and fishing ports and serves the day's best with wit and some theatre: abalone porridge, a cutlassfish so big it is called a dragon, sushi handed across the counter, a dessert of corn tempura. Born in Nara in 1961 into a family of cooks, the chef ran Fujita in Pontocho at 27 and opened Gion Sasaki in 1998, moving here in 2006; 2026 reviewers note seven straight years of three Michelin stars. One July 2026 diner found the apprentices did most of the cooking that day. Book by phone at the start of each month for two months ahead. Lunch ¥22,000, dinner ¥44,000 all in.

chef_bio.chef_name: Hiroshi Sasaki (佐々木浩; official site: "sasaki hiroshi")
roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog: "the owner, Mr. Sasaki"; official site)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1961 in Nara into a family of cooks — a grandfather in catering, a father with a kaiseki restaurant, relatives running inns and sushi shops; trained at places including the kaiseki inn Rinko-an in Shiga; head chef at Fujita in Pontocho at 27; opened Gion Sasaki in 1998 on the north side of Gion, moved to a larger room in 2002 and to the present house south of Kennin-ji in 2006. A May 2026 review adds training at Funaiwa (Shiga), Mikazukiro and Shin Gion. 2026 reviewers note three Michelin stars for seven consecutive years (May, September 2026). The group also runs Gion Rakumi, Sushi Rakumi and Shoku Bar Rakumi (official site). Tabelog Award Bronze 2019–2021, 2023, 2024, 2026, Silver 2022, 2025; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Delicious… no, fun!": for guests, the chef and the whole staff to enjoy the meal together as one (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: The day's best ingredients; counter theatre; charcoal grilling.

anecdotes.text: "For the second dessert, I was served corn tempura. Sweet corn. It was interesting to have this as a dessert." — July 2026, a seventh visit.
"The chef personally handed me sushi he prepared right at the counter, including freshly boiled natural sweet shrimp, which he peeled while still steaming." — September 2026, first visit.
"The dishes are primarily prepared by the apprentice. While Chef Sasaki greeted us at the beginning, he was not present during the meal." — July 2026, lunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (gionsasaki.com): 祇園さゝ木、佐々木浩、お客様の「おいしい・・・、いや楽しい。」の言葉が一番の望み、スタッフ全員が楽しみながら料理を出し店内が一体感のある時間を、昼は木・金・土のみ12:00一斉スタート、夜18:30一斉スタート、ランチ22,000円・ディナー44,000円 (税サ込み、仕入れで変動)、予約は毎月月初の営業日から2か月先の末日まで、電話のみ、日曜・月曜休みと不定休、東山区八坂通り小松町566-27、市バス清水道から徒歩3分、グループ店は祇園楽味、鮨楽味、食ばぁー楽味。食べログ (店舗会員): ヴィーガンメニューには対応できない、30分以上の遅刻はキャンセル扱い、20席 (カウンター13、個室カウンター7)、10歳未満不可、靴を脱ぐ、昼はサービス料込み・夜は10%、The Tabelog Award Bronze・Silver、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2025。口コミ (2026年5〜10月、英語): 一斉スタート、大勢の弟子、炭火の焼き場、大将が手渡す寿司、ミシュラン三つ星7年連続。

kyoto_oryori_hayashi.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information, and dishes are not explained at the table; a traditional Kyoto course seasoned with soy sauce and miso, with fried dishes and tempura (2026 reviews).
kyoto_oryori_hayashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a traditional kaiseki built on dashi, with sea bream, swordfish, hamo and ayu (2026 reviews).
kyoto_oryori_hayashi.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–15:00 (last entry 13:00) and dinner 17:30–21:30 (last entry 19:00); closed Wednesday, some Thursdays and about twice a month (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; changes after confirmation cannot be accommodated, so call (Tabelog). 23 seats: a counter of 7 on the ground floor and three tatami private rooms upstairs for 2–8; whole-shop hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). No photos at the counter; dishes are deliberately not explained (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Shoes off (September 2026). Children welcome; call first (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards: JCB and AMEX only; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). A 10% service charge, then 10% tax on the total (Tabelog). About 7 min from Demachiyanagi Stn, 2 min from the Kawaramachi-Imadegawa bus stop (Tabelog).
kyoto_oryori_hayashi.notes: [Kaiseki · Demachiyanagi, a quiet old-school Kyoto counter] A wooden townhouse in a lane across from the Kitamura Art Museum, with a seven-seat counter downstairs where a still, focused chef cooks in full view and three tatami rooms upstairs. Chef Wataru Hayashi, more than fifty years in the trade, has run the place for over thirty: plain, deeply seasoned Kyoto cooking without show, from a shrimp dumpling soup to a salt-grilled sea bream collar and a cold rice porridge. There is no menu and no explanation — the house style is to let you guess. The counter is hushed (one diner found it tense) and allows no photos; the upstairs rooms are more relaxed. Lunch from about ¥15,700 is the gentle way in. Tabelog Silver or Bronze every year since 2019. Closed Wednesdays; JCB and AMEX only.

chef_bio.chef_name: Wataru Hayashi (August 2026 review; no kanji in a source)

kyoto_nishibuchi_hanten.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; a Chinese course with sauces such as fermented black bean and liver sauce, fried rice and cold noodles (2026 reviews).
kyoto_nishibuchi_hanten.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a Chinese course of shark fin, abalone, chicken, pork and beef in superior broth (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_nishibuchi_hanten.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–21:00; closed Sunday and holidays (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, but hard to get; several 2026 diners came through a regular or a private booking, including private lunches (June, October 2026). 10 seats at the counter (Tabelog); an October 2026 diner used a private room. Cash only (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). About 586 m from Gion-Shijo Stn, at the end of a quiet lane near Yasaka Shrine (Tabelog). Opened 25 April 2013 (Tabelog).
kyoto_nishibuchi_hanten.notes: [Chinese · Higashiyama, Chinese cooking with a kappo soul] At the end of a quiet lane near Yasaka Shrine, a machiya with a white noren and a small garden looks like a kappo, and the ten-seat counter works like one. Chef Kentaro Nishibuchi, from Joyo in Kyoto Prefecture, learned Chinese cooking for six years at Kakan in the Kyoto Brighton Hotel, then five years of Japanese cooking at Gion Sasaki, and opened here in 2013. The result is gentle, layered Chinese food: shark fin braised and then grilled in superior broth, chicken wings stuffed with bird's nest, fried rice lightened with grated daikon. Diners in 2026 praise the chef's warm smile and call it very hard to book. Tabelog Silver every year since 2019. Cash only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Kentaro Nishibuchi (Tabelog; no kanji in a source)
roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog: "In 2013, he opened Nishibuchi Hanten")

Tabelog praises the chef's spirit of exploration and warm smile. In September 2026 the restaurant cooked a two-day special course in Tokyo, including an Amex cardholder event and a collaboration with Yoshidashioto (September 2026 reviews); one September 2026 diner heard an Italian restaurant would open nearby. Tabelog Award Silver 2019–2026; Chinese WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2024, 2026.
chef_bio.specialty: Shark fin in superior broth; bird's-nest-stuffed chicken wings; daikon fried rice.

kyoto_yassan_gion.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; beef sashimi comes with ponzu or ume paste, grilled cuts and the stew are seasoned with a long-kept sauce (miso-based, per an October 2026 diner) (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_yassan_gion.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a beef restaurant — beef sashimi, grilled beef and oxtail stew (Tabelog; official site).
kyoto_yassan_gion.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–22:30; closed Sunday and holidays (official site; Tabelog). The ground-floor counter takes no reservations — diners queue from before 18:00 or try around 20:00; the upstairs tatami rooms can be booked for groups of three or more (official site; 2026 reviews). Counter of about 22 on the ground floor, tatami rooms upstairs (Tabelog). Smoking allowed, per Tabelog. No photos of the raw meat (2026 reviews). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). The house was renovated for earthquake safety and reopened in March 2025 with the old interior kept (Tabelog). About 10 min from Gion-Shijo Stn; across the street from Gion Ichiriki-tei (official site). Mail order through OMAKASE and Ikyu (official site).
kyoto_yassan_gion.notes: [Beef · Gion, a family meat counter since 1948] Look for the red lanterns across from Ichiriki-tei: inside, a long, Showa-red counter under hanging gourds, packed and loud with Kyoto dialect. The founder, from 門前仲町 in Tokyo, opened in 1948 and created the oxtail stew that still simmers in a big pot behind the counter, its sauce topped up for over 77 years; the second generation turned it into meat kappo. There is no menu: the staff lead you from cold oxtail soup through beef-tongue, heart and tripe sashimi to grilled cuts and the stew, which you finish by picking up the bones. The counter cannot be booked, so queue before 18:00. Now run by fourth-generation Yoshifumi Sakakibara with family. Tabelog Bronze 2025–2026. Closed Sundays and holidays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yoshifumi Sakakibara (Tabelog; no kanji in a source)
roles: Fourth-generation chef (Tabelog: "took over as the fourth generation")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: born in Kyoto in 1994, the founder's first great-grandchild; drawn to cooking by watching the grandfather, the second generation, in the kitchen; trained from 19 at local Japanese restaurants and butchers, then apprenticed at Yassan under the senior cooks; took over at 26 as the fourth generation, running the restaurant with family: a sister, Tomoyo, a mother, Yuko, and a grandmother, Nobe, the head of the house. The official site says the first owner, from 門前仲町 in Tokyo, created the oxtail stew in Kyoto in 1948 and the second generation made it a meat kappo. Tabelog adds that it began in Teramachi-Rokkaku and moved to Gion around 1968. An October 2026 reviewer calls it a long-time favourite of actors. Tabelog Award Bronze 2025, 2026.
chef_bio.philosophy: Keep the order of dishes, light to rich, unchanged since the founding (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Oxtail stew; beef-tongue sashimi; blanched tripe with ume.

anecdotes.text: "The details of the sauce are a secret, but the stew becomes delicious by including various parts like tongue, heart, cheek meat, and sirloin." — the chef, on Tabelog.
"I arrived at 17:40 on a weekday and found five people waiting outside." — October 2026.
"I started with the beef tongue sashimi, followed by heart and lean cuts. No photos allowed." — September 2026, first visit after queuing.

kyoto_gion_nishi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a kaiseki course built on dashi, with sea urchin, hamo, beef and foie gras (2026 reviews).
kyoto_gion_nishi.hours_raw: Dinner from 18:00 Tue–Sun; lunch from 12:00 Thu–Sun; closed Monday and irregularly (Tabelog; official site); evening times can be discussed (Tabelog). Reservations by phone (August 2026). 20 seats: a counter of 6 and tables for up to 14 (Tabelog). Children who can eat the course are welcome (Tabelog). Non-smoking, with an ashtray at the entrance (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and QR payments (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay); service charge 10% (Tabelog). About 8 min from Gion-Shijo Stn: from the Higashiyama-Yasui crossing go about 50 m along Higashioji-dori, on the left (Tabelog). Opened 7 July 2016 (Tabelog). GION NISHI CAFE is on the floor above (official site).
kyoto_gion_nishi.notes: [Kaiseki · near Yasaka Shrine, kaiseki with an Italian twist and good wine] A calm room of a six-seat counter and tables a few minutes from Yasaka Shrine, run by owner-chef Jumpei Nishi (西隼平), born in Kyoto Prefecture in 1983, who trained at Tokuwo, spent time in an Italian kitchen and ran a Gion kitchen before opening in 2016. The cooking keeps kaiseki form but borrows Italian ideas, with a hassun that is the centrepiece and luxuries like a chawanmushi of sea urchin, abalone and caviar. The chef is a certified sommelier and sake expert and pours by the glass to your taste; you can even ask for curry at the end. A Japanese review praises the okami's care. Lunch ¥19,360 all in is good value for the area. Tabelog Bronze every year since 2019. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Jumpei Nishi (西隼平)
roles: Owner-chef (official site: "店主・西隼平")
Certified wine sommelier and sake expert (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog's chef section: born in 1983 in Kyoto Prefecture; trained at the Kyoto Japanese restaurant Tokuwo, then at an Italian restaurant to broaden the cooking; head chef at a Japanese restaurant in Gion before opening Gion Nishi in July 2016. The official site says the chef brings young sensibility and Italian essence to Japanese tradition and actively uses ingredients and techniques Japanese cooking does not; the shop also produces GION NISHI CAFE upstairs. A June 2026 Japanese review praises the 大将's delicate cooking and the 女将 and staff's care. Tabelog Award Bronze 2019–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: No compromise on ingredients, drink, tableware or space; original dishes made with playfulness (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: The hassun; kaiseki with Italian touches; wine pairings.

anecdotes.text: "Even when I requested curry, they served it with a smile, without any hint of displeasure." — July 2026.
"I opted for the Omakase course priced at JPY 19,360 (including tax and service charge)." — August 2026, lunch.
"When I shared my preferences, they served me a glass from a bottle they had." — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (gion-nishi.com): 祇園 にし、店主・西隼平は日本料理店とイタリアンで修行、日本料理の伝統に若い感性とイタリアンのエッセンス、食材・お酒・器・空間に妥協しない、日本料理では扱わない食材や技法も取り入れる、八坂神社の近く、二階に GION NISHI CAFE、東山区月見町21-2 1階、月曜全日と不定休。食べログ (店舗会員): 火・水は夜のみ、木〜日は昼と夜、20席 (カウンター6、テーブル14)、カードと QR 可、サービス料10%、2016年7月7日オープン、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2019〜2026、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025。口コミ (2026年6月、日本語): 大将の繊細で工夫に満ちた料理、女将さんやスタッフの細やかな気遣い、長芋素麺と蓴菜に大間の雲丹、牡丹鱧の白味噌仕立てのお椀、アオリイカ・マグロ・雲丹・ノドグロのお造り、オマール海老やとうもろこしのムースの八寸、鮎の海苔巻き寿司、牛ロースと賀茂茄子の海老の田楽。

kyoto_mashiro_rokkaku.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; French-based cooking that uses soy sauce and miso in its sauces (Tabelog), with a rice-cracker cup for the opening sea urchin and vegetable fritters in 2026.
kyoto_mashiro_rokkaku.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a seafood-led course with beef, lamb and chicken (2026 reviews).
kyoto_mashiro_rokkaku.hours_raw: Lunch from 12:00 and dinner from 18:00, each starting together; closed irregularly (official site; Tabelog). Reservation only, online (official site); a July 2026 diner booked 63 days ahead on TableCheck. 11 seats at a counter cut from a single slab over 10 m long (Tabelog). Children from 10, on the adult course (Tabelog). Smart casual (Tabelog). Non-smoking; wheelchair access (Tabelog). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR; service charge 10% (Tabelog). 4 min from Karasuma Oike Stn exit 5, 6 min from Karasuma Stn exit 21 (official site). Opened 20 August 2023 (Tabelog).
kyoto_mashiro_rokkaku.notes: [French · Karasuma-Rokkaku, a genre-free chef's counter] A second-floor room near Rokkakudo with a single-slab counter over ten metres long, hexagonal tiles that nod to the temple, and an open kitchen run like a show. The chef trained at the Rihga Royal Hotel in Osaka, became the youngest chef in its history at 33 at Restaurant Chambord in 小倉, went to the 2015 Bocuse d'Or Japan final, and won Michelin stars at Cosimo Plus in Ashiya and Gion Roshoku before opening MASHIRO in 2023. Every meal opens with "Uni", sea urchin and seawater jelly in a rice-cracker cup; after that the course follows the market, with French sauces sharpened by soy or miso. Pairings come from sommelier-manager Masahiro Kobayashi, a partner of over 20 years. Tabelog Bronze 2026. Book online well ahead.

chef_bio.chef_name: Hiroyuki Koshimo (Tabelog's chef heading; the same listing also writes "Kosimo", "Koshiro" and "Kosumo"; no kanji in a source read)
roles: Chef (official site; Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: trained at the Rihga Royal Hotel in Osaka and at 33 became the youngest chef in the hotel's history, at the 小倉 grand maison Restaurant Chambord; then chef at DOUZE GOUT 12+ in Kyoto; a Japan finalist for the Bocuse d'Or 2015; opened コシモ・プリュス in Ashiya in May 2012 (one Michelin star, Kyoto-Osaka 2014) and 祇園 呂色 in November 2017 (one star, 2018); opened MASHIRO in Karasuma-Rokkaku in August 2023. The name means "pure white": reset your mind and enjoy the food with all six senses. The sommelier and manager, Masahiro Kobayashi, has worked with the chef for over 20 years (Tabelog). The site lists tie-in plans with the 南座 theatre (2026). Tabelog Award Bronze 2026; Innovative/Creative "Tabelog 100" 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Tradition matters, but as Japanese French cuisine we must change something" (Tabelog); "Make your heart pure white" (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: The opening "Uni"; market-led courses; pairings.

anecdotes.text: "The chef kindly included a birthday message and a note related to my favorite artist on the final dessert plate." — July 2026, lunch.
"Every month, I look forward to dining at MASHIRO!" — September 2026, a fourteenth visit.
"The ribbonfish, which looks massive, is said to be nearly 2 meters long, and its fat is exquisite." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (mashiro-kyoto.com): 真白 MASHIRO ジャンルレス料理、真白な空気で深呼吸し1日が始まる、毎朝生産者から届く最高の食材、漬・焼・煮・蒸・揚・発酵・熟成、シェフは大阪「リーガロイヤルホテル」で修業、同ホテル史上最年少の33歳で小倉「レストラン シャンボール」のシェフ、京都「DOUZE GOUT 12＋」のシェフ、ボキューズ・ドール2015日本代表ファイナリスト、2012年5月 芦屋に「コシモ・プリュス」(ミシュラン京都・大阪2014で一つ星)、2017年11月「祇園 呂色」(2018で一つ星)、2023年8月 烏丸・六角に「真白」、「心を真っ白に」、堂之前町234 OHG京都六角ビル2階、ランチ12:00〜・ディナー18:00〜 一斉スタート、不定休、南座とのタイアッププラン。食べログ (店舗会員): カウンター11席、10歳以上、スマートカジュアル、サービス料10%、ペアリング 昼8,800円・夜11,000円、2023年8月20日オープン、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2026。口コミ (2026年7〜10月、英語): 名物の雲丹、メッセージプレート、季節の魚、ペアリング。

kyoto_muromachi_wakuden.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; a kaiseki course seasoned with soy sauce and miso, with fried dishes and sushi among the closing rices (2026 reviews).
kyoto_muromachi_wakuden.vegan_detail: Ask: the official site lists a shojin (Buddhist vegetarian) course at ¥25,000, bookable up to three days ahead, and Tabelog marks vegetarian options; whether it uses any animal-based dashi or egg is not stated. The regular courses use fish, eel, turtle and beef.
kyoto_muromachi_wakuden.hours_raw: Lunch Mon, Fri, Sat, Sun 12:00–15:00 (last seating 13:00); dinner 18:00–21:00 (Tabelog: last seating 19:00, to 22:00); closed Wednesday; also closed 5 November and 25–30 December 2026 (official site; Tabelog). Reservation requested, online or by phone (official site). Cancellation the day before or on the day: 80% (official site). 50 seats: a counter of 15 and four private rooms for 4–20 (Tabelog). Counter from junior-high age; children of any age in the private rooms, with a kids' menu and strollers welcome (Tabelog). English menu (Tabelog). Wheelchair accessible; non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards accepted; prices include tax and service (official site). 5 min east of Karasuma Oike Stn exit 3-1 (official site).
kyoto_muromachi_wakuden.notes: [Kaiseki · Sakaimachi-Oike, a ryotei house's counter] The town branch of Wakuden, a Kyoto ryotei family that began as an inn in Tango in 1870: a renovated machiya with a garden, a counter of fifteen around a crew of young cooks, and private rooms for families. Courses follow the season — in autumn a chrysanthemum dish for the Choyo festival, Matsutake in a teapot soup, and narai-yaki, eel wrapped around Matsutake, a house dish for half a century — and end with a choice of clay-pot rices, the rest wrapped as onigiri for later. A shojin course is available if you book three days ahead. About half the guests one September 2026 night were from overseas, with explanations in English. Some 2026 diners found it salty or routine. Lunch from ¥13,000 all in; closed Wednesdays.

roles: Run by Wakuden Inc. (official site's copyright: "wakuden Inc.")
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: the Wakuden house was established in 1870 as a ryokan in Tango; the Muromachi restaurant is a Kyoto townhouse built by Nakamura Sotoku Construction (as Tabelog's English gives it), with a counter designed so every seat watches the chefs. The official site lists the group's other ryotei (Kodaiji Wakuden, Kyoto Wakuden), soba and other restaurants, and gift shops in Kyoto, Tokyo and Nagoya. An October 2026 reviewer calls the house a training ground for chefs such as those of Tokuwo and Kiyama (kyoto_kiyama_gosho in this data). Tabelog Award Bronze 2017–2022, 2025, 2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Serve the true flavours of each season, nurtured by nature, with sincerity (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Narai-yaki of eel and Matsutake; clay-pot rice; seasonal kaiseki at the counter.

anecdotes.text: "Almost half of the guests were from overseas, and the staff provided explanations in English." — September 2026.
"Their signature rice was wonderfully sticky, and they even made the leftovers into onigiri for me to take home." — September 2026.
"There were many dishes that were overly salty." — October 2026.

kyoto_kyo_seika_okazaki.gf_detail: Ask when booking by phone. No gluten information; the course includes spring rolls, steamed buns, noodles and Sichuan-style sauces (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_kyo_seika_okazaki.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a Chinese course of shark fin, abalone, sea cucumber, crab, char siu and wagyu (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_kyo_seika_okazaki.hours_raw: Dinner only, everyone starting at 18:00; closed Monday and Tuesday and irregularly — check the calendar on the official site (official site; Tabelog). The restaurant closed from 1 May 2026 for maintenance and training and reopened in September 2026 (official site). Bookings by phone only, up to the end of the month two months ahead, 11:00–16:00 on business days; not by Instagram or Facebook messages (official site). Cancellation: 100% on the day, 50% the day before; no children below junior-high age except for whole-room bookings (official site). 16 seats: a round table for 10 and two tables for 3 (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards accepted; service charge 10% (Tabelog). The site warns of fake websites using its name. About 5 min from Higashiyama Stn (Tabelog). Opened 20 April 2008 (Tabelog).
kyoto_kyo_seika_okazaki.notes: [Chinese · Okazaki, a master's quiet Chinese table near Heian Shrine] A second-floor room by the Biwako Sosui canal, one round table and two small ones, everyone starting at 18:00. Owner-chef Shizuo Miyamoto ran Seika in Hamamatsu for 25 years from 1983, trained in Hong Kong, Taiwan and Beijing, studied again in Beijing in middle age, and opened here in 2008; dishes recreate techniques from classical Chinese texts with Kyoto vegetables. Every meal starts with a crisp spring roll and a spicy sorbet, and the course runs through shark fin and abalone soups, char siu and steamer baskets of crab rice and buns. After two apprentices left to open their own places, the restaurant closed from May 2026 and reopened in September with the chef cooking alone. ¥27,500 including tax, plus service; book by phone. Tabelog Bronze in most years since 2017.

chef_bio.chef_name: Shizuo Miyamoto (an October 2025 review; Tabelog: "The chef, Mr. Miyamoto"; no kanji in a source)

kyoto_kikunoi_honten.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; a kaiseki course seasoned with soy sauce and miso, with sushi and egg-yolk soy sauce among 2026 dishes.
kyoto_kikunoi_honten.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a kaiseki built on dashi, with hamo, ayu, tuna and beef (2026 reviews); no vegetarian course is listed.
kyoto_kikunoi_honten.hours_raw: Lunch entry 12:00–12:30, dinner entry 17:00–19:30; closed the first and third Tuesday (may change by month) and over the New Year (official site; Tabelog lists 12:00–14:00 and 17:00–20:00 daily). Bookings by phone 10:00–22:00 (official site); a 2026 diner booked two months ahead, another found it easy. 120 seats in 10 tatami rooms, for 4 to over 30 (Tabelog). Designated smoking area; parking available (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, JCB, AMEX); service charge 15% (official site; Tabelog).
kyoto_kikunoi_honten.notes: [Kaiseki · Higashiyama, a century-old ryotei by Kodai-ji] Up the slope past Maruyama Park, beside Kodai-ji, a ryotei founded in the first year of the Taisho era by a family that kept the spring "Kikusui no I" once used for Nene's tea. Third-generation owner Yoshihiro Murata, born in 1951, trained in France and Nagoya before taking up the family craft, and has led the push to have washoku listed by UNESCO. Meals are served in ten tatami rooms over the garden, some hung with works such as Ito Jakuchu screens, with a new seasonal menu every month: Matsutake and hamo in a teapot soup, ayu shown alive before grilling, tuna with egg-yolk soy sauce. The site reports three Michelin stars in 2024, 2025 and 2026. Lunch from ¥16,500 plus 15% service is the gentle way in.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yoshihiro Murata (Tabelog; no kanji in a source read)
roles: Third-generation owner (Tabelog)
chef_bio.origin: Kyoto, born 1951 (Tabelog: "born as the eldest son of … Kikunoi in Gion").
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: born in 1951 as the eldest son of Kikunoi; while at Ritsumeikan University went to France to learn French cooking but chose Japanese cuisine; trained at a Nagoya restaurant and opened Kikunoi Kiyamachi in 1976; vice-president of the Japan Food Culture National Council in the campaign for washoku's UNESCO listing and chairman of the Japanese Culinary Academy; awarded the Medal with Yellow Ribbon. The family were tea masters who kept the spring Kikusui no I, used by Nene (Kita no Mandokoro) for tea; the ryotei was founded in the first year of Taisho (Tabelog). The official site lists the house's other restaurants (露庵, 赤坂菊乃井, 無碍山房) and three Michelin stars in the Kyoto-Osaka guides 2024, 2025 and 2026. A September 2026 diner was greeted by the owner. Tabelog Award Bronze 2018, 2019, 2021–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Cooking with water: vegetables simmered in dashi to carry flavour, and the spirit of the tea ceremony (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal Kyoto kaiseki; dashi; the hassun.

anecdotes.text: "We were greeted by the stunning two-panel folding screen and hanging scroll by the genius Edo-period painter Ito Jakuchu." — September 2026, a family celebration.
"It's not difficult to make a reservation, making it a reliable choice for important business meals." — September 2026.
"They showed us the fish before grilling, and it was so fresh it almost jumped out of the basket!" — October 2026, a sixth visit.

kyoto_gion_sakagawa.gf_detail: Ask when booking by phone; à la carte ordering makes it easier to choose (2026 reviews). No gluten information; tempura, sushi and soy- and miso-seasoned dishes are on the menu.
kyoto_gion_sakagawa.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish-led kappo with turtle and beef, built on dashi (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_gion_sakagawa.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00, entry 17:00–20:30; closed Sunday (Tabelog); a September 2026 diner describes two seatings, at 17:00 and 20:00. Reservations accepted, by phone (2026 reviews); call ahead if you want a particular ingredient such as crab or abalone (Tabelog). More than 15 minutes late without word counts as a cancellation; no perfume or strong scents (Tabelog). 21 seats: a counter of 9 and private rooms for 3–4 on the ground floor and 5–8 upstairs, some with sunken seating (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 6 min from Gion-Shijo Stn exit 7 (Tabelog).
kyoto_gion_sakagawa.notes: [Kappo · Gion, a classic counter where you can order à la carte] An old-style house in a Gion lane: a wood counter of nine full of regulars and a lively voice behind it, sunken seats, and tatami rooms upstairs. Chef Hirokazu Sakagawa trained at Kappo Nakagawa in north Gion before opening here in the Heisei era. The draw is choice: take the course or order à la carte from the day's ingredients — bamboo shoots from Tsukahara in spring, hamo grilled on a shichirin in summer, Wakasa gurnard and turtle in autumn — and the kitchen cooks them as you like. Regulars order at their own pace; first-timers find the chef quietly welcoming. Market prices can climb (one September 2026 evening came to ¥39,000 with drinks). Tabelog Bronze every year since 2019. Closed Sundays.

kyoto_gion_nishikawa.notes: [Kaiseki · Higashiyama, a warm chef's sukiya house below Yasaka Shrine] Down a stone-paved lane between Yasaka Shrine and Kodaiji, a sukiya-style house of bamboo and hinoki with a single-slab counter 7.5 metres long and a small garden visible from every room. Owner-chef Masayoshi Nishikawa, born in Kyoto in 1975 to a family of Yuzen dyers, trained at Gion Sasaki, ran the kitchen at Warabi no Sato, and opened here in 2009; a Michelin listing followed within a year, and 2026 reviewers count two stars for fifteen years running. The menu changes daily: dashi from Yasaka Shrine's soft spring water, Ohara vegetables, a pressed mackerel sushi diners rave about, and touches like caviar on grilled eggplant. Reviewers love the chef's jokes and send-offs; in September 2026 the chef was running the kitchen almost alone, with an apprentice joining in October.

kyoto_sangencha_gion.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion, tea-ceremony cooking at a friendly counter] Through a noren and down a water-sprinkled stone alley off Hanamikoji, a hinoki counter of ten looks onto a small garden, with tatami rooms upstairs set with fine tableware. Chef Nobuhiko Masuda, born in Shiga in 1957, spent twenty years at the ryotei Shofukuro, opened Sangencha in Mizuguchi, Shiga, and moved to Gion; the cooking keeps the spirit of Zen cuisine and the tea meal while playing with ideas like mascarpone soy sauce for the sashimi. Courses end with rice from the chef's home town, as much as you like, and a melting mizu-yokan. Regulars come back for years for the chef's gentle humour; families are welcome, with a kids' menu. Lunch from about ¥10,000. Closed Tuesdays.

Children only if able to stay seated through the course; no shorts or sandals; photos of the food only, and post videos muted (official site). kyoto_takayama_kawaramachi.notes: [Italian · Kawaramachi-Shijo, a three-hour creative show of 25 small plates] A white room on the second floor of GOOD NATURE STATION with a curved counter of twelve around a stage-like open kitchen and no handle on the door. Owner-chef Tadashi Takayama went to Italy at 22, came home defeated by the language, went back at 27 to cook in Piedmont and Tuscany, and was sous-chef at Crescios in Campania before opening here in 2019. The course is about 25 bites built for fun as well as flavour: a juice wrapped in white chocolate with the menu as a printed QR code, Miyazaki caviar on squid-ink crisps, foie gras choux, a risotto of Seiko crab. Plan on three hours and come hungry. Many guests are from overseas, and staff are young and warm. ¥30,000 all in, plus ¥1,000 for water; closed Mondays.

kyoto_lurra_higashiyama.notes: [Innovative · Higashiyama, Nordic-Japanese cooking over open fire] A townhouse more than 250 years old, a minute from Higashiyama station, where ten guests at the counter watch the cooks work a wood fire and oven. Chef Jacob Kear, born in California and raised in Japan, cooked at Noma in Copenhagen and Noma Tokyo and was head chef of Clooney in New Zealand; drinks come from Yusuke Sakaibe, a cocktail champion the chef met in New Zealand. The name is Basque for earth, the ring a moon. Courses mix Nordic fermentation with Japanese seasons and Ohara vegetables — sea urchin manju, Biwa trout roasted in the fireplace with clam chowder sauce, fried ice-cream doughnuts to finish. A 2026 review reports a Michelin star in the Kyoto Osaka 2026 guide. In August a casual walk-in lunch runs for a few weeks. Book online; closed Sundays and Mondays.

kyoto_gion_matayoshi.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion, a tea-kaiseki counter with a big heart] Through a lattice door off Hanamikoji and along a stone path: a calm counter of eight and private rooms. The owner-chef, who ran the kitchen of a long-established inn before opening here in 2015, cooks about thirteen courses in the spirit of tea kaiseki on made-to-order pottery — a crab-only sushi roll, mackerel with its own liver sauce, Ishigaki beef in a hot pot, rice with Lake Biwa eel. Tabelog says it has held two Michelin stars since 2016. Diners find the chef imposing at first and warm once you settle; the staff chat and send you off with walking tips. Bookings are for two or more, and first-timers must book online. Lunch from ¥20,000. A casual sister, また吉, serves lunch, shaved ice and Italian nearby.

chef_bio.chef_name: Matayoshi (surname only, from the shop name and an August 2026 review: "Mr. Matayoshi"; Tabelog's English also writes "Matakichi"; no given name in a source)
roles: Owner-chef (official site: "老舗旅館で料理長を務めた店主")
chef_bio.origin: Not settled: Tabelog speaks of the chef's Okinawan roots, and a regular's October 2022 visit notes touches from the chef's hometown, Okinawa; an August 2026 reviewer says the chef hails from Kyushu.
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the owner was head chef of a long-established ryokan and cooks with the spirit of tea kaiseki; the room has a stone approach from the lattice door. Tabelog: two Michelin stars continuously since 2016; calligraphy of the shop name by 石川九楊 (as Tabelog's English gives it: Ishikawa Kyōyō); custom tableware from a pottery studio. The official site also announces a casual sister shop, また吉, opened 1 August 2021 at 祇園町南側570-120 (lunch, natural-ice kakigori, Italian at night), and New Year osechi. A February 2026 regular writes of being intimidated at first, then finding it the most relaxing place. Tabelog Award Bronze 2019–2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Ichigo ichie: dishes born from the day's conversation with guests, keeping the heart of tea kaiseki (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Tea-kaiseki courses; crab sushi roll; hot pot of Ishigaki beef.

anecdotes.text: "During my first visit, I was a bit intimidated by the atmosphere and the chef's presence, but once I got used to it, it became the ultimate relaxation spot." — February 2026, a fifth visit.
"On my way out, they recommended a charming street in Kyoto, so I took a leisurely walk back." — March 2026.
"The hot pot was simply prepared with Ishigaki beef briefly dipped in broth, yet it was exquisite." — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (gion-matayoshi.com): 祇園又吉、茶懐石のこころを大切に、季節の粋を集め、その日そのときお客様との会話から生まれる一期一会の味わい、祇園花見小路、格子戸を開けると石畳、老舗旅館で料理長を務めた店主、祇園町南側570-123、祇園四条駅から徒歩5分、初めての方は WEB 予約のみ、御節七寸三段86,400円、姉妹店「また吉」(2021年8月1日開店、祇園町南側570-120 万治ビル1階、昼ごはん、天然氷のかき氷、夜は和の器でイタリアン)。食べログ (店舗会員): 日本料理、2名から、カウンターは2〜3名、4名以上は個室、1ドリンク制、代理予約は断る場合あり、6月1日から昼20,000円 (カウンター)・22,000円 (座敷)、夜36,000円・38,000円、サービス料あり、小学6年生以上は個室で、24席、2015年2月10日オープン、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2019〜2026、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023・2025。口コミ (2025年1月〜2026年10月、英語): 蟹だけの巻き寿司、Ishigaki の牛の鍋、Aramasa を中心とした日本酒、気さくなスタッフ。

cultural_comfort.note: First visits book online (TableCheck, TABLEALL); parties of two or more; many overseas guests (February 2026).

existence.note: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing and official site; reviews dated through October 2026.

kyoto_kyo_kaiseki_kichisen.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; a tea-style kaiseki of about 13 dishes with soy and miso seasoning, sushi and a steamed sushi wrapped in egg (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_kyo_kaiseki_kichisen.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a kaiseki built on kombu-and-bonito dashi (official site), with fish, crab and eel.
kyoto_kyo_kaiseki_kichisen.hours_raw: Lunch with entry at 12:00 only (to 14:30) and dinner with entry at 18:00 only (to 21:00); closed irregularly (Tabelog). Reservation only; more than 15 minutes late without word counts as a cancellation (Tabelog). 17 seats: a counter of 6 (March 2025 review) and private rooms for 2–8 (Tabelog). Children: call to book; a kids' menu is available (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); service charge 10% (Tabelog). About 10 min on foot from Demachiyanagi Stn, or a short taxi from Imadegawa Stn (Tabelog). Opened 1983 in a hotel; on this site two years later (official site).
kyoto_kyo_kaiseki_kichisen.notes: [Kaiseki · Shimogamo, a master's tea-style kaiseki by the Tadasu no Mori] Beside the ancient woods of Shimogamo Shrine, a 455 m² compound with counter seats, three private rooms and a tea room, "Suishoan", moved here from a 1935 building, all hung with scrolls and flowers chosen by the owner. Owner-chef Yoshimi Tanigawa (谷河吉巳), born in Hyogo in 1951, started cooking at 15, learned from some fifty teachers in tea, flowers, incense and poetry as well as food, was head chef at an Arashiyama ryotei at 26, and opened Kichisen in 1983; the site lists two Michelin stars in 2010–2013 and three in 2014–2019, and a win on Iron Chef in 1999. Meals are tea-style kaiseki of about thirteen dishes, still cooked by the owner, who goes to market at 4 a.m. Dinner around ¥44,000 plus service; book ahead.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yoshimi Tanigawa (谷河吉巳; romaji from Tabelog, which also writes the shop as "Yoshizumi")
roles: Owner-chef (official site: "亭主 谷河吉巳")
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: found the joy of cooking at 9 and came to Kyoto at 15; did not train at a famous ryotei but met some 50 teachers, learning tea, flower arrangement, incense, calligraphy and poetry, with influences including 福富雪底 of Daitokuji, 寛海 of Jukoin, the chef 竹端寅一 and 菅田宗匠 of Omotesenke; head chef of an Arashiyama ryotei at 26; opened Kichisen in a hotel in 1983 at 31 and built the present Shimogamo house two years later; featured in The New York Times in 1986; won a hamo battle against 森本正治 on Iron Chef in 1999; two Michelin stars 2010–2013 and three 2014–2019; has worked on ceremonial knife cooking, kaiseki for diabetics, and promoting Kyoto cuisine abroad; appeared on television about strict but warm training. Tabelog adds the chef still cooks, goes to market at 4 a.m. with an apprentice, and has trained over 60 apprentices; the tea room "Suishoan" was moved from a 1935 site. Tabelog Award Bronze 2017, 2019–2022, 2026, Silver 2018; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023.
chef_bio.philosophy: Gochisō — gathering the season's best from across Japan as hospitality; dashi of kombu and bonito as the life of Kyoto cooking (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Tea-style kaiseki; dew-sprinkled soups; tuna sushi.

anecdotes.text: "I have been coming to this restaurant for nearly 40 years." — March 2025.
"The hanging scroll by Jakuchu is also authentic, which is quite rare to find." — August 2026, a tenth visit.
"The head chef had a powerful presence yet was very kind." — November 2025, Matsutake.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (kichisen-kyoto.com): 京懐石 吉泉、茶懐石の流れを汲んだ伝統的なもてなし料理、日本中から旬の食材、糺の森、亭主 谷河吉巳: 9歳で調理する歓びを知り15歳で京へ、50人の師との出会い (茶道、華道、香道、書、詩歌)、26歳で嵯峨嵐山の料亭の料理長、1983年31歳でホテルの一角に「吉泉」、2年後に下鴨に「京懐石 吉泉」、1986年 NewYorkTimes、1999年「料理の鉄人」の鱧対決で森本正治氏に勝利、2010〜2013年ミシュラン二ツ星、2014〜2019年三ツ星、献立は酒一献から、お椀の蓋に茶筅で露を打つ、昆布と鰹の出汁。食べログ (店舗会員): 日本料理、下鴨森本町5、昼12:00入店のみ、夜18:00入店のみ、不定休、17席、個室あり、お子様メニューあり、サービス料10%、The Tabelog Award Bronze・Silver 2018、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023。口コミ (2025年3月〜2026年8月、英語): Sakura-yu、マグロの寿司、Matsutake、Jakuchu の掛け軸。

cultural_comfort.note: Set kaiseki with fixed entry times; the official site has English, Chinese and Korean pages; book ahead.

kyoto_calvador_bar.gf_detail: Ask. A Calvados bar: apple and pear brandies and cocktails are the mainstay; the only food the 2026 reviewers mention is Calvados chocolate.
kyoto_calvador_bar.vegan_detail: Ask. Spirits and cocktails may suit; the chocolates are not described.
kyoto_calvador_bar.hours_raw: 19:00–23:00; closed Wednesday and Thursday (Tabelog); a May 2026 regular was told of a special Thursday opening. Reservations accepted (Tabelog); an April 2026 diner says it has been very hard to get in for about ten years, and diners phone ahead (2026 reviews). 8 seats at the counter (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog). Table charge ¥1,000 (Tabelog). Cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners) and Rakuten Pay (Tabelog). Second floor, with no sign outside (2026 reviews). About 313 m from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Stn (Tabelog). Opened 28 April 2004 (Tabelog).
kyoto_calvador_bar.notes: [Bar · Kyoto City Hall, the Calvados specialist] Up to the second floor of an unmarked building near Kyoto City Hall, eight counter seats and a list of over 500 apple brandies. Master Takayama, said by 2026 regulars to know more about Calvados than anyone in Japan, travels to France to source it; there are single casks bottled for the bar and vintages such as a Lauriston 1963. Start with a Jack Rose, then let the master pour a 34-year single cask or a pear-heavy rarity, perhaps with Calvados chocolates from Assemblage Kakimoto. Regulars say it has been hard to get into for a decade, so phone first. Smoking allowed; ¥1,000 charge. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Takayama (surname only; 2026 reviews: "Master Takayama", "Mr. Takayama")
roles: Owner-bartender (2026 reviews: "The owner, Mr. Takayama")
chef_bio.background: Opened 28 April 2004 (Tabelog). Per 2026 reviews: the master is said to be the most knowledgeable person about Calvados in Japan and goes to France to source it (February); has single casks bottled for the bar, such as a 34-year Toutain (2026 reviews); greets returning guests by name (February); the bar holds over 500 kinds of Calvados (May). Selected for Tabelog Bar "Tabelog 100" 2022. The official website address returned a hosting placeholder page in November 2026.
chef_bio.specialty: Calvados, including old vintages and the bar's own single casks; Jack Rose.

anecdotes.text: "The moment I made eye contact with Master Takayama, he smiled and said, 'Ah, it's you, Mr. XX,' which instantly eased my tension." — February 2026.
"In the past, I could walk in without a reservation, but for about the last 10 years, it has become extremely difficult to get a table at this bar." — April 2026.
"When paired with Calvados chocolate, it felt like I was drowning in a giant baked apple pie." — May 2026.

kyoto_bar_rocking_chair.gf_detail: Ask. A cocktail bar: spirits and fresh-fruit cocktails are the likelier choices; the food includes fresh pasta (June 2026), and the table charge includes a small snack.
kyoto_bar_rocking_chair.vegan_detail: Ask. Fruit cocktails and spirits may suit; the pasta seen in 2026 came with oil sardines.
kyoto_bar_rocking_chair.hours_raw: Daily except Tuesday 17:00–1:00 (last order 24:00); also closed on 9 and 16 November 2026 (official site). Bookings only for arrivals between 17:00 and 18:00, from the start of each month; after that, phone 30 minutes ahead and a free seat is held for 30 minutes (official site); groups of up to 4 (official site). 24 seats: 9 at the counter and 5 tables, plus two rocking chairs by the fireplace (Tabelog; June 2026). Smoking allowed, cigars available; no minors (Tabelog). Table charge ¥880 including a snack (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) (Tabelog). The fireplace is lit for the season on 19 November 2026, with inoko-mochi for guests (official site). Opened 2 February 2009 (Tabelog).
kyoto_bar_rocking_chair.notes: [Bar · Shijo-Kawaramachi, cocktails by the fire in a Kyoto townhouse] Through a small garden off Miyukimachi-dori, a warm wood-lined machiya bar with a long counter, tables, and two rocking chairs in front of a fireplace that is lit each November with the season's first inoko-mochi. Owner-bartender Kenji Tsubokura runs a team whose bartender Kato won a national competition with the cocktail "The Best Scene"; seasonal fruit drinks such as a watermelon salty dog sit beside sharp classics. It is popular: you can book only for 17:00–18:00, otherwise phone half an hour ahead and a seat is held for you. Smoking and cigars allowed, so no minors; ¥880 charge with a snack. Open to 1:00, closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Kenji Tsubokura (坪倉健児; official site: "Kenji Tsubokura, Owner Bartender")
roles: Owner-bartender (official site)
Bartender Kato, winner of a national bartender competition (August 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Opened 2 February 2009 (Tabelog). The official site, signed by the owner, posts monthly hours and holidays, explains the booking rules (bookings only for 17:00–18:00; later a 30-minute seat hold by phone), and announces the yearly lighting of the fireplace with inoko-mochi, a sweet said to ward off fire. A June 2026 diner found it through a book by Kazuhiko Ota. Selected for Tabelog Bar "Tabelog 100" 2022.
chef_bio.philosophy: A glass to enjoy slowly as the seasons change (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Seasonal fruit cocktails; the fireplace and rocking chairs.

anecdotes.text: "True to its name, there are two rocking chairs placed in front of the fireplace." — June 2026.
"I ordered the championship-winning cocktail, 'The Best Scene.' I was warned that it was on the stronger side." — August 2026.

kyoto_kyoshumi_hishiiwa.gf_detail: Ask when ordering. No gluten information; set boxes of about 20 Kyoto dishes, simmered and grilled, with sushi and a fried item (official site; 2025 reviews).
kyoto_kyoshumi_hishiiwa.vegan_detail: Not vegan: Kyoto cooking on dashi, with duck breast, eel, fish and shrimp (2025 reviews).
kyoto_kyoshumi_hishiiwa.hours_raw: Orders and pickup 11:30–18:00; closed Sunday and the second and last Monday, and irregularly (official site; Tabelog lists 11:30–20:30). Bento by advance order only, by phone (075-561-0413) up to the day before; two days ahead is safer (April 2026 review); a day's numbers are limited (official site). Collect on the day and eat the same day (official site); delivery to nearby wards such as Higashiyama and Nakagyo (official site). June–September: sales generally stop for hygiene, except for bento eaten within about an hour of pickup (official site). No eating in (Tabelog), but in August–September 2026 the shop served a limited lunch, a hamo mabushi set, in a private room, booked by phone after an Instagram notice (2026 reviews). Cash only (Tabelog; November 2025 review). On Shinmonzen-dori, 7 min from Sanjo Stn (Tabelog; April 2026 review).
kyoto_kyoshumi_hishiiwa.notes: [Bento · Shinmonzen, Kyoto's benchmark bento since 1829] A caterer of nearly two hundred years, whose boxed bento are, to many reviewers, the best in Japan: some twenty small dishes — duck breast, a perfect dashi omelette, sushi in bamboo leaf, eel, simmered vegetables each seasoned on its own — that still taste right cold. There is no dining room: order by phone by the day before, collect on Shinmonzen-dori (or have it delivered nearby), and eat it the same day, at Minami-za, on the Shinkansen or in your hotel. From ¥3,780; the two-tier boxes feed two or more. Cash only, closed Sundays, and bento mostly pause June–September. In late summer 2026 it also served a limited sit-down lunch of hamo on rice.

roles: Catering house, run by the current head of the family (official site: "現当主", no name given)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: founded in the first year of Tenpō (1829) as a neighbourhood caterer, carrying fish bought at market to nearby homes on a shoulder pole; the third-generation master, 松之助, created the half-moon 半月弁当; the house sees itself as "the customer's kitchen". The Tabelog Award 2020 Bronze (Tabelog). Reviewers note deliveries to the Minami-za theatre (December 2025) and sales through Takashimaya and Isetan by reservation (October 2025).
chef_bio.philosophy: Traditional Kyoto cooking made for the customer's pleasure, with the spirit of "the customer's kitchen" (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Boxed bento (折詰弁当); half-moon bento.

anecdotes.text: "Even after some time and carrying it around, I was surprised that everything inside was perfectly intact!" — October 2025.
"They even deliver to Minami-za Theatre." — December 2025, eaten on the Shinkansen.
"Since I was in a private room, I could enjoy my meal in peace and quiet." — August 2026, the limited lunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (hishiiwa.com): 天保初年 (1829年) 創業の仕出し料理専門店、「お客様の台所」の心構え、3代目主人松之助が半月弁当を考案、折詰弁当は梅3,780円・月4,860円・花6,480円・松8,100円・白川11,880円・八坂14,040円・東山21,600円 (税込、白川・八坂・東山は数量限定)、半月弁当4,320〜5,940円、松花堂弁当7,020円・8,640円、注文は全て電話で前日までの完全予約制、販売・予約受付11:30〜18:00、当日中に食べる、東山区・中京区などへ配達、6〜9月は衛生を考え基本的に販売中止、日曜と第2・最終月曜定休。食べログ: 弁当、東山区西之町213、店内飲食不可、カード不可、The Tabelog Award 2020 Bronze。口コミ (2025年10月〜2026年9月、英語): 日本一の仕出し弁当、Minami-za への配達、期間限定の昼の hamo mabushi。

cultural_comfort.note: Orders by phone only, by the day before; the official English page says there are no English-speaking staff and suggests booking through your hotel concierge.

kyoto_gion_endo.gf_detail: Ask. An à la carte menu of some 70 dishes, so sashimi, grilled fish and salt-grilled dishes can be chosen; the famous horse mackerel fry, fried oysters and tempura are breaded or battered (Waraku 2024; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_gion_endo.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish-centred kappo; vegetable dishes such as dashi-soaked eggplant rely on dashi (2026 reviews).
kyoto_gion_endo.hours_raw: 18:00–24:00 Mon–Sat; closed Sunday (Tabelog); Waraku (2024) also gives public holidays as closed. Booking needed (Waraku 2024), by phone 075-551-7271 (Tabelog). 16 seats: 8 at the counter, 8 at tables (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners) (Tabelog). Inside the 楽宴小路 alley off Hanamikoji, 381 m from Gion-Shijo Stn (Tabelog). Opened 25 November 2011 (Tabelog).
kyoto_gion_endo.notes: [Kappo · Gion, the à la carte fish counter] Down a narrow alley off Hanamikoji, a calm counter where you order what your appetite wants from a handwritten board of about seventy dishes. Owner-chef Kouta Endo comes from a family of fishmongers who supply Kyoto's famous restaurants, so the fish is outstanding: Akashi sea bream and striped jack as sashimi, a thick horse mackerel fry still rare in the middle that diners call the best anywhere, drunken Matsuba crab in winter, and a grilled rice ball to finish. Regulars come as a first stop or a late second one; it is open to midnight. Book by phone; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.chef_name: Kouta Endo (遠藤功太; reading こうた per Waraku; romaji from a June 2026 review)
roles: Owner-chef
chef_bio.background: Per Waraku (April–May 2024 issue, web reprint November 2024): opened in Gion in 2011 as a counter kappo of fish dishes where you eat what you like, as much as you like; the family business is a fish shop that supplies famous restaurants; the motto is to make the most of the finest ingredients quickly and deliciously. A June 2026 review adds that the family fish shop is now run by a brother and that simmered dishes are cooked first and seasoned after. Tabelog Award Bronze 2017–2020, 2025, 2026; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: To make the most of the finest ingredients, quickly and deliciously (Waraku 2024).
chef_bio.specialty: Horse mackerel fry; sashimi; drunken crab in season.

anecdotes.text: "The friendly owner creates a warm and inviting atmosphere." — January 2026.
"Here, the dilemma isn’t about “what to choose” but rather “what to give up.”" — October 2025.
"It’s fantastic that we can enjoy such high-quality fish a la carte until late at night." — March 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 和樂 (2024年4・5月号、web 2024年11月): ぎをん 遠藤、2011年に祇園にオープン、魚料理を中心に好きなものを好きなだけ楽しめるカウンター割烹、店主の遠藤功太 (こうた) さん、実家は有名店御用達の魚店、「最強の食材を活かすべく、手早くおいしく」がモットー、旬の魚のお造りや焼き物、煮物、サラダにオムレツ、丼からチャーハンまで70種ほど、「最強のアジフライ」はウスターソースとマヨネーズで、穴子の白焼き、明石の鯛のお造り、鯛のあら炊き、ひとり10,000〜15,000円が目安、18時〜、要予約、日曜・祝日休み。食べログ: 日本料理、祇園町北側347-118 楽宴小路内、月〜土18:00〜24:00、日曜休み、16席 (カウンター8、テーブル8)、カード可、2011年11月25日オープン、The Tabelog Award Bronze 2017〜2020・2025・2026、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2025。口コミ (2025年10月〜2026年8月、英語): アジフライ、Matsuba crab の酔っ払い蟹、気さくな大将。

cultural_comfort.note: A handwritten Japanese menu ordered dish by dish; book by phone.

existence.note: Tabelog listing with the 2026 Bronze award; reviews dated through August 2026; Waraku feature 2024.

kyoto_gion_kida.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; a long omakase with soy-seasoned sushi, fried dishes and, at times, ramen or crab noodles (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_gion_kida.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a dashi-based kaiseki of crab, fugu, tuna, eel and beef (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_gion_kida.hours_raw: Dinner from 18:00; closed irregularly (Tabelog); the Michelin Guide page gives 18:00–22:00. Reservation only, by phone 075-551-3923 (Tabelog); hard to book (October 2026 review). Omakase course ¥35,000 before tax and service (Tabelog); diners report ¥40,000–79,999 with drinks. Courses run over three hours (June 2025 review). Each December the shop turns into "Izakaya Kida", an à la carte month of about 84 dishes (December 2025 reviews). 14 seats: a counter of 8 and a private counter of 6 (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners) (Tabelog). Photos allowed, but posting them online is not encouraged (Tabelog, May 2025). About 6 min from Gion-Shijo Stn (Tabelog). Opened 17 June 2016 (Tabelog).
kyoto_gion_kida.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion, a Sasaki alumnus's generous counter] Yasuo Kida spent 27 years beside Hiroshi Sasaki at Gion Sasaki and was first head chef of its offshoot 楽味 before opening Gion Kida in 2016. Dinner is a long, lavish omakase — crab, fugu, Matsutake, marinated tuna sushi, Kagoshima beef — with portions diners call generous and a pace of three hours or more; each December the room turns into "Izakaya Kida", an à la carte feast of oden and sushi. Regulars praise the chef's warmth. Reservation only and hard to book; around ¥35,000 plus tax and service, more with drink.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yasuo Kida (木田; romaji from a June 2025 review, surname in kanji from Retty reviews)
roles: Owner-chef
chef_bio.background: Per a June 2025 review: trained for 27 years under Hiroshi Sasaki of 祇園 さゝ木 and was the first head chef at 楽味, a restaurant Sasaki founded; opened Gion Kida in 2016; the review says it won a Michelin star in the Kyoto-Osaka guide. Retty reviews (2018–2019) call the chef the long-time right hand and first apprentice of Gion Sasaki who went independent after 楽味. Tabelog: opened 17 June 2016; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023. The Michelin Guide page describes the 因縁果 approach of cooking each day's ingredients.
chef_bio.philosophy: 因縁果: the producer's land and care (cause), the season, technique and meeting with guests (condition), and the flavour that results (June 2025 review; Michelin Guide).
chef_bio.specialty: Crab dishes in season; marinated tuna sushi; December "Izakaya Kida".

anecdotes.text: "Mr. Kida's warm personality makes every meal enjoyable." — June 2025, an eighth visit.
"Gion Kida opens its limited-time Izakaya Kida every December!!" — December 2025.
"An incredibly popular restaurant that's hard to book" — October 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Retty (祇園 きだ): 東山区祇園町南側570-192、2018年の口コミ「祇園さゝ木で長年右腕として働いていた木田さんが、楽味を経て一昨年独立して出されたお店」、2019年の口コミ「祇園ささきの一番弟子の木田さん」。ミシュランガイド (日本語ページ): 日本料理、一年の旬を七十二候に分ける、因縁果、18:00〜22:00。食べログ: 日本料理、予約のみ、18時から、不定休、おまかせコース35,000円 (税・サービス料別)、14席 (カウンター8、個室カウンター6)、カード可、写真は可だがネット掲載は好まれない (2025年5月時点)、2016年6月17日オープン、日本料理 WEST 百名店 2021・2023。口コミ (2025年6月〜2026年10月、英語): 佐々木浩さんのもとで27年、楽味の初代料理長、量の多いおまかせ、12月の「Izakaya Kida」、予約が取りにくい。

cultural_comfort.note: Set omakase at the counter; booking by phone only, so a hotel concierge may help.
